metadata.title: Discretization, Uniform-in-Time Estimations and Approximation of Invariant Measures for Nonlinear Stochastic Differential Equations with Non-Uniform Dissipativity

extraction_notes.note: The roadmap paragraph before Theorem 4.8 is a proof sketch; the sketch rule asks for rigor semi_formal while the rigor rule excludes proofs. Followed the rigor rule (no rigor field on the proof) since the finishing step flags rigor on proofs.
Condition (3) in the introduction restates Assumption 2's inequality (8) in different notation; both are numbered displays, so both were kept as equation nodes rather than merged.
Propositions 2 and 5 are argued partly in running text (case overview, subcase (III), Case 3 reduction); these were emitted as separate proof parts linked to the propositions.
The TEM scheme is given as a cases display inside a definition sentence; its three algorithm steps are lines of that display.
Prose explanations of the coupling, the scalar-noise values of alpha_1, alpha_3, alpha_4, the Zwanzig interpretation and figure-only content were not extracted as nodes.

nodes.name: Overdamped Langevin diffusion
nodes.statement: \mathrm d x_t=-\nabla U(x_t)\,\mathrm dt+\sqrt{2}\,\mathrm d B_t ,
nodes.label: E1

nodes.name: Additive-noise SDE with superlinear drift
nodes.statement: In this paper we study this problem for the more general additive-noise SDE \begin{equation} \mathrm d x_t=b(x_t)\,\mathrm dt+\Sigma\,\mathrm d B_t,\qquad x_0\in\mathbb R^d, \end{equation} where $B$ is a $q$-dimensional Brownian motion, $b:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ is locally Lipschitz and has superlinear growth, and $\Sigma\in\mathbb R^{d\times q}$ is non-degenerate in the sense that \(\Gamma:=\Sigma\Sigma^{\mathrm T}>0\).
nodes.statement_short: The SDE $dx_t=b(x_t)dt+\Sigma dB_t$ with locally Lipschitz superlinear drift and non-degenerate constant noise, $\Gamma=\Sigma\Sigma^T>0$.

nodes.name: Additive-noise SDE
nodes.statement: \mathrm d x_t=b(x_t)\,\mathrm dt+\Sigma\,\mathrm d B_t,\qquad x_0\in\mathbb R^d,
nodes.label: E

nodes.name: Dissipativity-at-infinity condition (intro form)
nodes.statement: \langle x-y,b(x)-b(y)\rangle \leqslant L|x-y|^2\mathbf 1_{\{|x-y|\leqslant R\}} -K|x-y|^2\mathbf 1_{\{|x-y|>R\}}, \qquad x,y\in\mathbb R^d .
nodes.label: NGC

nodes.name: Uniform dissipativity condition
nodes.statement: A large body of work has studied approximation of invariant measures under the uniform dissipativity condition \begin{equation} \langle x-y,b(x)-b(y)\rangle\leqslant -K|x-y|^2,\qquad x,y\in\mathbb R^d , \end{equation} which corresponds to strong convexity in the Langevin case.

nodes.name: Uniform dissipativity condition
nodes.statement: \langle x-y,b(x)-b(y)\rangle\leqslant -K|x-y|^2,\qquad x,y\in\mathbb R^d ,
nodes.label: E2

nodes.name: Explicit scheme with uniform-in-time strong error and invariant-measure error under dissipativity at infinity
nodes.statement: For SDEs with superlinearly growing drift under the dissipativity-at-infinity condition \eqref{NGC}, can one design an explicit and implementable numerical scheme which simultaneously provides a uniform-in-time strong error estimate with a quantitative convergence rate and an error estimate for invariant measures?
nodes.statement_short: Can an explicit scheme for superlinear SDEs dissipative only at infinity give both a uniform-in-time strong rate and an invariant-measure error bound?

nodes.name: Positive integers
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{N}$ denote the set of all positive integers.

nodes.name: Non-negative reals
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{R}_+$ denote the set of all non-negative real numbers.

nodes.name: Generic constants C and C_l
nodes.statement: Let $C$ denote a generic positive constant whose value may change from line to line while $C_l$ is a positive constant depending on the parameter $l$.

nodes.name: Minimum, maximum and positive part
nodes.statement: For any $a, b\in \mathbb{R}$, let $a\wedge b = \min\{a, b\}$, $a\vee b = \max\{a, b\}$ and \((a-b)^+ = a-a\wedge b\).

nodes.name: Euclidean and Frobenius norm
nodes.statement: Let $|\cdot|$ denote both the Euclidean norm in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and the Frobenius norm in $\mathbb{R}^{d \times m}$.

nodes.name: Transpose
nodes.statement: For a vector $A\in\mathbb{R}^d$, denote its transpose by $A^\mathrm{T}$.

nodes.name: Inner product
nodes.statement: For $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$, let $\langle x, y \rangle$ denote the inner product of $x$ and $y$.

nodes.name: Identity matrix
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{I}$ be the $d\times d$ identity matrix.

nodes.name: Complete filtered probability space
nodes.statement: Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\geqslant 0}, \mathbb{P})$ be a complete filtered probability space with $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\geqslant0}$ satisfying the usual conditions (that is, it is right-continuous and increasing while $\mathcal{F}_0$ contains all $\mathbb{P}$-null sets).

nodes.name: Expectation
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{E}$ denote the expectation corresponding to $\mathbb{P}$.

nodes.name: Brownian motion B
nodes.statement: Let $\{B_t\}_{t\geqslant 0}$ be a $q$-dimensional Brownian motion defined on the probability space.

nodes.name: Borel sets
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{B}(E)$ denote the family of all Borel sets on $E$.

nodes.name: Complement and indicator function
nodes.statement: For a set $\mathbb{D}$, let $\mathbb{D}^c$ be the complement of $\mathbb{D}$ and $\1_\mathbb{D}(x) = 1$ if $x\in\mathbb{D}$ and $0$ otherwise.

nodes.name: L^p spaces of random variables
nodes.statement: For $p\geqslant1$, let $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d)$ be the family of \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-valued random variables $\xi$ satisfying $\|\xi\|_p:=(\mathbb{E}|\xi |^p)^{1/p}<\infty$.

nodes.name: Law of a random variable
nodes.statement: For a random variable $\xi\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d)$, let $\mathcal{L}(\xi)$ denote its distribution.

nodes.name: Normal distribution
nodes.statement: Let $N(a, \Gamma)$ denote the normal distribution with mean $a\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and positive definite covariance matrix $\Gamma\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$.

nodes.name: Gaussian density
nodes.statement: Let $p_{a,\Gamma}(\cdot)$ be the density function of $N(a,\Gamma)$ described by \begin{equation*} p_{a,\Gamma}(x) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{(2\pi)^d\mathrm{det}(\Gamma)}}\mathrm{exp}\left(-\frac{1}{2}(x-a)^\mathrm{T}\Gamma^{-1}(x-a)\right). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Probability measures on R^d
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ denote the set of all probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$.

nodes.name: Integral of a function against a measure
nodes.statement: For $\mu\in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and a measurable function $g$, define $\mu(g):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}g(x)\mu(\mathrm{d} x)$ whenever the integral exists.

nodes.name: Strictly increasing cost function f
nodes.statement: Let $f:[0, +\infty)\rightarrow [0, +\infty)$ be a strictly increasing function satisfying $f(0) = 0$.

nodes.name: Wasserstein-type distance W_f
nodes.statement:
Given two probability measures $\mu, 
u\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ satisfying \(\mu(f(|\cdot|))<\infty\) and \(
u(f(|\cdot|))<\infty\), define $$\mathcal{W}_f(\mu, 
u):= \inf_{\mathbf{\pi}\in \mathscr{C}(\mu, 
u)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d	imes \mathbb{R}^d} f(|x-y|)\mathbf{\pi}(\mathrm{d} x, \mathrm{d} y),$$ where $\mathscr{C}(\mu, 
u)$ is the collection of probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d	imes \mathbb{R}^d$ with marginals $\mu$ and $

nodes.statement_short: Optimal-transport cost $\mathcal W_f$ with cost $f(|x-y|)$ over couplings $\mathscr C(\mu,\nu)$.

nodes.name: L^p-Wasserstein distance
nodes.statement:
For any $p\geqslant 1$, define $$\mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d):=\left\{\mu \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^{d}) : \mu(|\cdot|^p)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}|x|^p\mu(\mathrm{d}x)<\inftyight\} $$ and the $L^p$-Wasserstein distance $\mathcal{W}_p$ for $\mu, 
u\in\mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ $$\mathcal{W}_p(\mu, 
u):= \inf_{\mathbf{\pi}\in \mathscr{C}(\mu, 
u)}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^d	imes \mathbb{R}^d} |x-y|^p\mathbf{\pi}(\mathrm{d} x, \mathrm{d} y)ight)^{ rac{1}{p}}.$$

nodes.name: Completeness of the Wasserstein space
nodes.statement: Then, $(\mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d),\mathcal{W}_p)$ is a complete metric space for any $p\geqslant 1$, see \cite{Chen}.
conclusions: $(\mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d),\mathcal{W}_p)$ is a complete metric space for any $p\geqslant 1$

nodes.name: Local Lipschitz condition (Assumption 1)
nodes.statement: For any $n>0$, there is a constant $L_n>0$ such that \begin{equation} |b(x)-b(y)|\leqslant L_n|x-y| \end{equation} for any $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$ with $|x|\vee|y|\leqslant n$.
nodes.label: A

nodes.name: Local Lipschitz bound
nodes.statement: |b(x)-b(y)|\leqslant L_n|x-y|
nodes.label: LL

nodes.name: Dissipativity at infinity (Assumption 2)
nodes.statement: There exist constants $L, K>0$ and $R\geqslant 0$ such that \begin{equation} \langle x-y, b(x)-b(y)\rangle \leqslant L|x-y|^2 {\bf{1}}_{[0, R]}(|x-y|)-K|x-y|^2\1_{(R, +\infty)}(|x-y|) \end{equation} for any $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$.
nodes.label: A1

nodes.name: Dissipativity at infinity inequality
nodes.statement: \langle x-y, b(x)-b(y)\rangle \leqslant L|x-y|^2 {\bf{1}}_{[0, R]}(|x-y|)-K|x-y|^2\1_{(R, +\infty)}(|x-y|)
nodes.label: CaI

nodes.name: One-sided growth bound from dissipativity at infinity
nodes.statement: It follows from \eqref{CaI} that for any $\epsilon\in(0, K)$, \begin{equation*} \langle x, b(x)\rangle \leqslant(L+K)R^2-(K-\epsilon)|x|^2+\frac{|b(\mathbf{0})|^2}{4\epsilon}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Dissipativity at infinity gives an upper bound on $\langle x,b(x)\rangle$ of the form $C-(K-\epsilon)|x|^2$.
nodes.label: Re0

nodes.name: Outside-of-sphere contractivity versus dissipativity at infinity
nodes.statement: Some previous references \cite{Bao, Bao1, Bao2, 2025SPA, A.D. N} impose the outside-of-sphere contractivity condition. That is, there exist constants $L',K',R' > 0$ such that \begin{equation} \langle x-y, b(x)-b(y)\rangle\leqslant L'|x-y|^2 {\bf{1}}_{[0, R']}(|x|\vee|y|)-K'|x-y|^2\1_{(R', +\infty)}(|x|\vee|y|) \end{equation} for any $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$. In the one-dimensional case, there are several functions $b$ satisfying (\ref{DOS}), such as the functions $-x, x-x^3$ and $b_1(x) := -x|x|+6x$. We observe that $(\ref{CaI})$ follows from $(\ref{DOS})$ with $L = L', K = K'$ and $R = 2R'$. However, $(\ref{DOS})$ is only sufficient but not necessary for $(\ref{CaI})$. In fact, there exist several functions $b$ satisfying $(\ref{CaI})$ but not $(\ref{DOS})$. For example, the functions $-x+\sin(2x), -3x/2+\ln(1+|x|)-2\sin (x), -x+(2-\cos(\pi x/4))\sin(2\pi x)$ and $b_2(x) := -x|x|+6x-2x \cos(x)$. Figure \ref{Fre} geometrically visualizes the difference between the two dissipative properties described by (\ref{CaI}) and (\ref{DOS}). The functions $-x$ and $b_1(x)$ exhibit uniform dissipation outside a certain sphere. However, the class of functions satisfying dissipativity at infinity is broader: it includes not only such functions, but also functions with frequent local oscillations, such as \(-x+\sin(2x)\) and \(b_2(x)\). \begin{figure}[!htb] \centering \includegraphics[width=12cm]{RE.png} \caption{Functions satisfying outside-of-sphere dissipativity or dissipativity at infinity.} \end{figure}
nodes.statement_short: The outside-of-sphere condition implies dissipativity at infinity but not conversely; examples of drifts in each class.
nodes.label: ree1

nodes.name: Outside-of-sphere contractivity condition
nodes.statement: \langle x-y, b(x)-b(y)\rangle\leqslant L'|x-y|^2 {\bf{1}}_{[0, R']}(|x|\vee|y|)-K'|x-y|^2\1_{(R', +\infty)}(|x|\vee|y|)
nodes.label: DOS

nodes.name: Well-posedness, Markov property and uniform moment bounds of the SDE
nodes.statement: Under Assumption \ref{A}, the SDE \eqref{E} admits a unique global solution \((x_t)_{t\geqslant 0}\) for every initial value \(x_0\in\mathbb R^d\). Moreover, \((x_t)_{t\geqslant 0}\) is a time-homogeneous Markov process with transition probability \(P_t(x,A):=\mathbb P(x_t\in A\mid x_0=x)\) for any \(t\geqslant0, A\in\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d)\). If, in addition, Assumption \ref{A1} holds, then for every \(q>0\), \[\sup_{0\leqslant t<\infty}\mathbb E|x_t|^q \leqslant C_q(1+|x_0|^q),\] where \(C_q\) is independent of \(t\).
nodes.origin_citation: Li, Mao & Yin 2019 (IMA J. Numer. Anal.), Theorems 2.3 and 5.2
nodes.statement_short: Under local Lipschitz drift the SDE has a unique global Markov solution; with dissipativity at infinity its moments are bounded uniformly in time.
conclusions: the SDE \eqref{E} admits a unique global solution \((x_t)_{t\geqslant 0}\) for every initial value \(x_0\in\mathbb R^d\)

nodes.name: m-step transition probability of a Markov chain
nodes.statement: Let \(\Phi=\{\Phi_n\}_{n\geqslant0}\) be a discrete-time homogeneous Markov chain on \((E,\mathcal{B}(E))\). For any \(m\geqslant0\), \(x\in E\), and \(A\in\mathcal{B}(E)\), define \[ P^m_{\Phi}(x,A):=\mathbb{P}_x(\Phi_m\in A), \] which is called the \(m\)-step transition probability of the chain \(\Phi\). For notational simplicity, we denote the one-step transition probability \(P^1_{\Phi}(x,A)\) by \(P_{\Phi}(x,A)\).

nodes.name: Geometric ergodicity criterion for Markov chains
nodes.statement: Assume that the following conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] The \(E\)-valued time-homogeneous Markov chain \(\Phi=\{\Phi_n\}_{n\geqslant0}\) is \(\psi\)-irreducible and aperiodic, where \(\psi\) is a measure on \((E,\mathcal{B}(E))\). \item[(ii)] There exist a petite set \(A_*\in\mathcal{B}(E)\), constants \(\gamma<\infty\), \(\beta<1\), and a measurable function \(V:E\to[1,+\infty)\) such that \[ \int_E V(y)P_{\Phi}(x,\mathrm{d} y) \leqslant \beta V(x)+\gamma \mathbf{1}_{A_*}(x), \qquad x\in E. \] \end{enumerate} Then the chain \(\Phi\) admits a unique invariant probability measure \(\pi\), and there exist constants \(\bar{c}>1\) and \(\tilde{c}>0\) such that, for any \(x\in E\), \begin{equation} \sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\bar{c}^m \sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_V} \left| \int_E g(y)P^m_{\Phi}(x,\mathrm{d} y) - \int_E g(y)\pi(\mathrm{d} y) \right| \leqslant \tilde{c}V(x), \end{equation} where \[ \mathbb{G}_V := \{g:E\to\mathbb{R} \text{ measurable}: |g(x)|\leqslant V(x),\ \forall x\in E\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: A psi-irreducible aperiodic chain with a Lyapunov drift condition towards a petite set is V-geometrically ergodic.
assumptions: The \(E\)-valued time-homogeneous Markov chain \(\Phi=\{\Phi_n\}_{n\geqslant0}\) is \(\psi\)-irreducible and aperiodic, where \(\psi\) is a measure on \((E,\mathcal{B}(E))\).

There exist a petite set \(A_*\in\mathcal{B}(E)\), constants \(\gamma<\infty\), \(\beta<1\), and a measurable function \(V:E\to[1,+\infty)\) such that \[ \int_E V(y)P_{\Phi}(x,\mathrm{d} y) \leqslant \beta V(x)+\gamma \mathbf{1}_{A_*}(x), \qquad x\in E. \]
conclusions: the chain \(\Phi\) admits a unique invariant probability measure \(\pi\)

there exist constants \(\bar{c}>1\) and \(\tilde{c}>0\) such that, for any \(x\in E\), \begin{equation} \sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\bar{c}^m \sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_V} \left| \int_E g(y)P^m_{\Phi}(x,\mathrm{d} y) - \int_E g(y)\pi(\mathrm{d} y) \right| \leqslant \tilde{c}V(x),
nodes.label: GET

nodes.name: Geometric ergodicity series bound
nodes.statement: \sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\bar{c}^m \sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_V} \left| \int_E g(y)P^m_{\Phi}(x,\mathrm{d} y) - \int_E g(y)\pi(\mathrm{d} y) \right| \leqslant \tilde{c}V(x),

nodes.name: Exponential decay of V-weighted distance to equilibrium
nodes.statement: It follows from \eqref{2.7} that, for any \(x\in E\) and \(m\geqslant1\), \[ \sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_V} \left| \int_E g(y)P^m_{\Phi}(x,\mathrm{d} y) - \int_E g(y)\pi(\mathrm{d} y) \right| \leqslant \tilde{c}\mathrm{e}^{-m\ln\bar{c}}V(x). \]
nodes.label: RE1

nodes.name: Modulus function phi
nodes.statement: Under the local Lipschitz condition \eqref{LL}, we choose a strictly increasing continuous function \(\phi:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+\) such that \(\phi(u)\to\infty\) as \(u\to\infty\) and \begin{equation} \sup_{\substack{|x|\vee |y|\leqslant u\\ x\neq y}} \frac{|b(x)-b(y)|}{|x-y|} \leqslant \phi(u), \qquad u>0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A strictly increasing continuous $\phi$ diverging at infinity that dominates the local Lipschitz constant of $b$ on balls of radius $u$.

nodes.name: Local Lipschitz modulus bound by phi
nodes.statement: \sup_{\substack{|x|\vee |y|\leqslant u\\ x\neq y}} \frac{|b(x)-b(y)|}{|x-y|} \leqslant \phi(u), \qquad u>0.
nodes.label: Tr

nodes.name: Non-uniqueness of the modulus function phi
nodes.statement: The function \(\phi\) satisfying \eqref{Tr} is not unique. For example, if \eqref{Tr} holds for some function \(\phi\), then it also holds for any function in the family \(\{k\phi+l:\ k\geqslant1,\ l>0\}\). Here we only need to choose one that works.

nodes.name: Unit direction e_x
nodes.statement: For any $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, define $\boldsymbol{e}_{x} = x/|x|$ if $x\neq \boldsymbol{0}$ and \(\boldsymbol{e}_{x} = \boldsymbol{0}\) otherwise.

nodes.name: Truncation parameters M and bar theta
nodes.statement: Fix a parameter $M> \phi(0)\vee|b(\mathbf{0})|$ and a constant $\bar{\theta}\in(0, 1/2)$.

nodes.name: Truncation mapping pi_h
nodes.statement: For any step size $h\in(0,1]$ and $\theta\in(0, \bar{\theta}]$, define the truncation mapping $\pi_h:\mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow\mathbb{R}^d$ by \begin{equation} \pi_h(x) = \Big(|x| \wedge \phi^{-1}(Mh^{-\theta})\Big) \boldsymbol{e}_{x} , \end{equation} where $\phi^{-1}$ denotes the inverse function of $\phi$.
nodes.statement_short: $\pi_h$ projects $x$ onto the ball of radius $\phi^{-1}(Mh^{-\theta})$.

nodes.name: Truncation mapping pi_h
nodes.statement: \pi_h(x) = \Big(|x| \wedge \phi^{-1}(Mh^{-\theta})\Big) \boldsymbol{e}_{x} ,
nodes.label: TF

nodes.name: Global Lipschitz bound of truncated drift
nodes.statement: |b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y))|\leqslant Mh^{-\theta}|\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y)|,~~\forall~ x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d.
nodes.label: GL

nodes.name: Linear growth bound of the truncated drift
nodes.statement: This, together with \(M\geqslant |b(\mathbf{0})|\) and \(h\in(0,1]\), yields \[ |b(\pi_h(x))| \leqslant Mh^{-\theta}(1+|\pi_h(x)|), \qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^d. \]

nodes.name: Truncated Euler-Maruyama (TEM) scheme
nodes.statement: Next, we propose an explicit scheme for (\ref{E}), called the truncated Euler-Maruyama (TEM) scheme. For any integer $k\geqslant 0$, define \begin{equation} \left\{ \begin{aligned} X_0 &= \pi_h(x_0),\\ \hat{X}_{k+1} &= X_k + b(X_k)h + \Sigma Z_{k+1}, \\ X_{k+1} &= \pi_h(\hat{X}_{k+1}), \end{aligned}\right. \end{equation} where $t_k=kh$ and $Z_{k+1} := B_{t_{k+1}}-B_{t_{k}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Explicit Euler-Maruyama step from the projected state, followed by projection onto a ball of radius growing as $h\to0$.

nodes.name: TEM scheme recursion
nodes.statement: \left\{ \begin{aligned} X_0 &= \pi_h(x_0),\\ \hat{X}_{k+1} &= X_k + b(X_k)h + \Sigma Z_{k+1}, \\ X_{k+1} &= \pi_h(\hat{X}_{k+1}), \end{aligned}\right.
nodes.label: TEM

nodes.name: Project the initial value
nodes.statement_short: Start from the projected initial value.

nodes.name: Explicit Euler-Maruyama step
nodes.statement: \hat{X}_{k+1} &= X_k + b(X_k)h + \Sigma Z_{k+1},
nodes.statement_short: One explicit Euler-Maruyama step from the current state.

nodes.name: Truncate the new state
nodes.statement_short: Project the Euler-Maruyama output back onto the ball.

nodes.name: TEM scheme reduces to Euler-Maruyama for globally Lipschitz drift
nodes.statement: Assume that the drift coefficient \(b\) is globally Lipschitz continuous; that is, there exists a constant \(\tilde{L}>0\) such that $|b(x)-b(y)|\leqslant \tilde{L} |x-y|$ for all $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$. In this case, no truncation is needed. Equivalently, one may formally take \(\pi_h(x)=x\) for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Then the TEM scheme \eqref{TEM} reduces to the classical Euler--Maruyama scheme. Therefore, the TEM scheme can be regarded as a generalization of the EM scheme to SDEs with nonlinear drift coefficients.

nodes.name: Markov property and uniform moment bounds of the TEM scheme
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{A} and \ref{A1} hold. $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ is a time-homogeneous Markov chain with the $m$-step transition probability $P^m_X(x, A) = \mathbb{P}(X_m\in A \mid X_0 = x)$ and has the property \begin{equation*} \sup_{h\in(0, \bar{h}]}\sup_{k\geqslant 0}\mathbb{E} |X_k|^q\leqslant \sup_{h\in(0, \bar{h}]}\sup_{k\geqslant 1}\mathbb{E} |\hat{X}_k|^q\leqslant C_q(1+|x_0|^q), \end{equation*} for any $q>0$, where $\bar{h}:= (KM^{-2})^{1/(1-2\bar{\theta})}\wedge\left(2K^{-1}\right)$ provided that $M\geqslant \sqrt{K}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Li, Mao & Yin 2019 (IMA J. Numer. Anal.), Lemma 7.8 and Theorem 5.5
nodes.statement_short: The TEM chain is a time-homogeneous Markov chain with moments bounded uniformly in time and step size.
conclusions: $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ is a time-homogeneous Markov chain with the $m$-step transition probability $P^m_X(x, A) = \mathbb{P}(X_m\in A \mid X_0 = x)$
nodes.label: Le2

nodes.name: Feller property of the TEM chain
nodes.statement: Let Assumption \ref{A} hold. \((X_k)_{k\geqslant0}\) is a Feller Markov chain.
nodes.label: Le3

nodes.name: Proof of Feller property of the TEM chain
nodes.statement: Let \((X_k^{x_0})_{k\geqslant0}\) and \((X_k^{x'_0})_{k\geqslant0}\) be two numerical solutions of \eqref{TEM} with initial values \(x_0,x'_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\), respectively, driven by the same Brownian increments. By the argument in \cite[p.142, Lemma 8.1.4]{Ok}, it is sufficient to prove that, for any fixed \(k\geqslant1\), \[ \lim_{x_0\to x'_0}\mathbb{E}|X_k^{x_0}-X_k^{x'_0}|^2=0. \] Since \(\pi_h\) is the projection onto the closed ball centered at the origin with radius \(\phi^{-1}(Mh^{-\theta})\), it is non-expansive, that is, for any \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d\), \(|\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y)|\leqslant |x-y|\). Hence, using \eqref{GL} and \eqref{TEM}, for any fixed integer \(k\geqslant1\), \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}|X_k^{x_0}-X_k^{x'_0}|^2 &\leqslant \mathbb{E}\left| X_{k-1}^{x_0}-X_{k-1}^{x'_0} +h\left(b(X_{k-1}^{x_0})-b(X_{k-1}^{x'_0})\right) \right|^2\\ &\leqslant 2(1+M^2h^{2-2\theta}) \mathbb{E}|X_{k-1}^{x_0}-X_{k-1}^{x'_0}|^2. \end{align*} Iterating this inequality gives \[ \mathbb{E}|X_k^{x_0}-X_k^{x'_0}|^2 \leqslant 2^k(1+M^2h^{2-2\theta})^k |\pi_h(x_0)-\pi_h(x'_0)|^2. \] Since \(\pi_h\) is non-expansive, we further obtain \[ \mathbb{E}|X_k^{x_0}-X_k^{x'_0}|^2 \leqslant 2^k(1+M^2h^{2-2\theta})^k |x_0-x'_0|^2. \] Letting $x_0\rightarrow x'_0$, the desired inequality follows. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Couple two chains with common noise and iterate a one-step mean-square Lipschitz bound using non-expansiveness of $\pi_h$.

nodes.name: Reduce Feller property to mean-square continuity
nodes.statement: Let \((X_k^{x_0})_{k\geqslant0}\) and \((X_k^{x'_0})_{k\geqslant0}\) be two numerical solutions of \eqref{TEM} with initial values \(x_0,x'_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\), respectively, driven by the same Brownian increments. By the argument in \cite[p.142, Lemma 8.1.4]{Ok}, it is sufficient to prove that, for any fixed \(k\geqslant1\), \[ \lim_{x_0\to x'_0}\mathbb{E}|X_k^{x_0}-X_k^{x'_0}|^2=0. \]
nodes.statement_short: Couple two TEM chains with the same noise and reduce to continuity of $\mathbb E|X_k^{x_0}-X_k^{x_0'}|^2$.

nodes.name: One-step mean-square Lipschitz bound
nodes.statement: Since \(\pi_h\) is the projection onto the closed ball centered at the origin with radius \(\phi^{-1}(Mh^{-\theta})\), it is non-expansive, that is, for any \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d\), \(|\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y)|\leqslant |x-y|\). Hence, using \eqref{GL} and \eqref{TEM}, for any fixed integer \(k\geqslant1\), \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}|X_k^{x_0}-X_k^{x'_0}|^2 &\leqslant \mathbb{E}\left| X_{k-1}^{x_0}-X_{k-1}^{x'_0} +h\left(b(X_{k-1}^{x_0})-b(X_{k-1}^{x'_0})\right) \right|^2\\ &\leqslant 2(1+M^2h^{2-2\theta}) \mathbb{E}|X_{k-1}^{x_0}-X_{k-1}^{x'_0}|^2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Non-expansiveness of $\pi_h$ and the truncated Lipschitz bound give a one-step growth factor.

nodes.name: Iterate the one-step bound
nodes.statement: Iterating this inequality gives \[ \mathbb{E}|X_k^{x_0}-X_k^{x'_0}|^2 \leqslant 2^k(1+M^2h^{2-2\theta})^k |\pi_h(x_0)-\pi_h(x'_0)|^2. \] Since \(\pi_h\) is non-expansive, we further obtain \[ \mathbb{E}|X_k^{x_0}-X_k^{x'_0}|^2 \leqslant 2^k(1+M^2h^{2-2\theta})^k |x_0-x'_0|^2. \]
nodes.statement_short: Iterate to bound the $k$-step difference by $|x_0-x_0'|^2$.

nodes.name: Pass to the limit
nodes.statement: Letting $x_0\rightarrow x'_0$, the desired inequality follows. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Let $x_0\to x_0'$.

nodes.name: Numerical ergodicity of the TEM scheme
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{A} and \ref{A1} hold. For any integer $p\geqslant 1$, $\theta\in(0, \bar{\theta}]$ and $h\in(0, \bar{h}]$, the TEM chain $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ admits a unique invariant measure $\mu_h$ on \(\mathbb{B}^h:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d: |x|\leqslant \phi^{-1}(Mh^{-\theta})\}\). Moreover, there exist constants $\bar{c}>1$, $\tilde{c}>0$, possibly depending on \(p,h,\theta\), such that \begin{equation*} \sum_{k = 1}^{\infty}\bar{c}^k\sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_{V_p}}|\mathbb{E} g(X_k)-\mu_h(g)|\leqslant \tilde{c}(1+|x_0|^{2p}), \end{equation*} where $\bar{h}$ is defined in Lemma \ref{Le2}, $V_p(x) = 1+|x|^{2p}$ and \[\mathbb{G}_{V_p}: = \{g:\mathbb{R}^d\rightarrow\mathbb{R}:~|g(x)|\leqslant V_p(x), ~\forall x\in \mathbb{R}^d\}.\]
nodes.statement_short: For small step sizes the TEM chain has a unique invariant measure $\mu_h$ and converges to it geometrically in $V_p$-weighted norm.
conclusions: the TEM chain $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ admits a unique invariant measure $\mu_h$ on \(\mathbb{B}^h:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d: |x|\leqslant \phi^{-1}(Mh^{-\theta})\}\).

there exist constants $\bar{c}>1$, $\tilde{c}>0$, possibly depending on \(p,h,\theta\), such that \begin{equation*} \sum_{k = 1}^{\infty}\bar{c}^k\sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_{V_p}}|\mathbb{E} g(X_k)-\mu_h(g)|\leqslant \tilde{c}(1+|x_0|^{2p}), \end{equation*}
nodes.label: Pro1

nodes.name: Proof of Numerical ergodicity of the TEM scheme
nodes.statement: Fix $p\geqslant 1$, $\theta\in(0, \bar{\theta}]$ and $h\in(0, \bar{h}]$. Let \(\mathcal{E}_h:=\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap \mathbb{B}^h\), which is a $\Sigma$-algebra by \cite[p. 145, Lemma 3]{Pro}. For the numerical ergodicity, we only verify that conditions $(\mathrm{i})$ and $(\mathrm{ii})$ hold in Lemma \ref{GET} with $E = \mathbb{B}^h$. Since the proof is rather technical, we divide it into two steps. {\bf Step 1: Irreducibility and aperiodicity.} Let \(\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}\) denote the Lebesgue measure restricted to \(\mathbb{B}^h\). For \(x\in \mathbb B^h\), the random variable \(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1\) has a strictly positive Gaussian density on \(\mathbb{R}^d\). Hence, for any \(x\in\mathbb{B}^h\) and nonempty set \(A\in\mathcal{E}_h\) with \(\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}(A)>0\), \[ \begin{aligned} P_X(x,A) = \mathbb{P}\big(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)\in A\big) &\geqslant \mathbb{P}\big(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1\in A\big) \\ &= \int_A p_{x+b(x)h,h\Sigma \Sigma^{\mathrm T}}(y)\,\mathrm{d} y >0. \end{aligned} \] Therefore, according to \cite[Proposition 4.2.1]{Meyn}, \((X_k)_{k\geqslant0}\) is $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}$-irreducible. We next show that it is aperiodic. Suppose, to the contrary, that the chain has period \(d_0\geqslant2\). Then, according to the definition of a periodic Markov chain \cite[p.122-123]{Meyn}, there exist disjoint nonempty sets \(D_1,\ldots,D_{d_0}\in\mathcal{E}_h\) such that \[ \mathbb{B}^h=\bigcup_{i=1}^{d_0}D_i, \qquad P_X(x,D_{i+1})=1,\quad x\in D_i, \] with the convention \(D_{d_0+1}=D_1\). Since $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}(\mathbb{B}^h)>0$, there exists an $i_0\in \{1, 2, \cdots, d_0\}$ such that $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}(D_{i_0} )>0$. By the irreducibility argument above, \[ P_X(x,D_{i_0})>0, \qquad x\in E_h. \] In particular, this holds for \(x\in D_{i_0}\). However, the cyclic decomposition implies \[ P_X(x,D_{i_0})=0, \qquad x\in D_{i_0}, \] because the chain must move from \(D_{i_0}\) to \(D_{i_0+1}\) in one step. This is a contradiction. Hence the chain is aperiodic. {\bf Step 2: Lyapunov drift condition.} For any $x\in \mathbb{B}^h$, by \(|\pi_h(z)|\leqslant |z|\), we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) &= 1+\mathbb{E}|\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)|^{2p}\leqslant 1+\mathbb{E}|x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1|^{2p}, \end{align*} which yields \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \\ \leqslant &1+\mathbb{E}\left(|x|^2+2h\langle x, b(x) \rangle+h^2|b(x)|^2+|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\langle x+b(x)h,\Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right)^p. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Using Remark \ref{Re0} with $\epsilon = K/4$ implies that for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{equation} \langle x, b(x)\rangle \leqslant -\frac{3K}{4}|x|^2+R^2(L+K)+\frac{1}{K}|b(\mathbf{0})|^2. \end{equation} By (\ref{GL}), (\ref{Reeq}) and $M^2h^{2-2\theta}\leqslant Kh$, we further have for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{align*} 2h\langle x, b(x) \rangle+h^2|b(x)|^2 &\leqslant-\frac{3Kh}{2}|x|^2+2hR^2(L+K)+\frac{2h}{K}|b(\mathbf{0})|^2+M^2h^{2-2\theta} \left|x\right|^2\\ &\leqslant -\frac{Kh}{2}|x|^2+q_1h, \end{align*} where $q_1 := 2R^2(L+K)+2|b(\mathbf{0})|^2/K$. Substituting this into (\ref{Proeq1}), we obtain that \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1))\!\leqslant\! 1\!+\!\mathbb{E}\!\left(\!\left(1\!-\!Kh/2\right)|x|^2+q_1h\!+\!|\Sigma Z_1|^2\!+\!2\langle x\!+\!b(x)h, \!\Sigma Z_1 \rangle\!\right)^p\!. \end{equation} For $p =1$, since $\mathbb{E}\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle = 0$ and $\mathbb{E}|\Sigma Z_1|^{2p} \leqslant C_dh^p$ (see \cite{BMSC}), we have \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}V_1(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1))\leqslant 1+\left(1-\frac{Kh}{4}\right)|x|^2+\gamma_1 h, \end{aligned} \end{equation} where $\gamma_1:= q_1+C_d$. Next, we consider the case $p\geqslant 2$. For any $h\in(0, 2/K]$, we have \(1-Kh/2\in[0,1)\). Together with (\ref{EV}) and the binomial theorem, this gives that for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant 1+\left(1-\frac{Kh}{2}\right)|x|^{2p}+\mathrm{I}_1+\mathrm{I}_2, \end{align*} where $$\mathrm{I}_1 := p|x|^{2p-2}\left(q_1h+\mathbb{E}|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\mathbb{E}\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right),$$ $$\mathrm{I}_2:=\sum_{k =0}^{p-2}C_p^k|x|^{2k}\mathbb{E}\left(q_1h+|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right)^{p-k},$$ and $C_p^k := p!/(k!(p-k)!)$. Next, we estimate $\mathrm{I}_1$ and $\mathrm{I}_2$. Similar to the argument for \eqref{EV1}, we have \begin{equation} \mathrm{I}_1\leqslant p|x|^{2p-2}\left(q_1h+C_d\Sigma^2 h^p\right)\leqslant C_d|x|^{2p-2}h\leqslant Kh|x|^{2p}/8+C_dh. \end{equation} Since $C_p^k\leqslant C_p^{\lfloor p/2 \rfloor}$ for any $k\in[0, p]\cap \mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{E}|Z_1|^{p-k} \leqslant C_dh^{(p-k)/2}\leqslant C_dh$ for any $k\in[0,p-2]\cap\mathbb{N}$, and $|b(x)|h\leqslant Mh^{1-\theta}(1+|x|)\leqslant M\sqrt{h}(1+|x|)$ for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$, we have \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_2\leqslant C_p^{\lfloor p/2 \rfloor}\sum_{k =0}^{p-2}|x|^{2k}\mathbb{E}\left(q_1h+|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right)^{p-k}\!\leqslant\! C_d\sum_{k =0}^{p-2}\left(|x|^{2k}h^2+|x|^{p+k}h\right). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Noticing that $p/(p-k)\in[1, p/2]$ and $k/(p-k)\in[0, p/2-1]$ for any $k\in [0, p-2]$, by Young's inequality and \eqref{I2}, we have \begin{equation} \mathrm{I}_2\leqslant \frac{Kh}{8}|x|^{2p} + C_dh. \end{equation} This, together with (\ref{I1}) and (\ref{I2-}), implies that for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant \left(1-\frac{Kh}{4}\right)|x|^{2p}+\gamma_p, \end{equation} where $\gamma_p = 1+C_dh$. Therefore, combining (\ref{EV1}) with (\ref{Proeq5}), we obtain that for any $p\in[1, +\infty)\cap\mathbb{N}$ and $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$, $$\mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant \left(1-\frac{Kh}{4}\right)|x|^{2p}+\gamma_p = \left(1-\frac{Kh}{8}\right)|x|^{2p}+\left(\gamma_p -\frac{Kh}{8}|x|^{2p}\right).$$ Hence, for any $p\in\mathbb{N}$ and $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$, \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant \gamma_p\1_{A_p}(x)+\left(1-\frac{Kh}{8}\right) V_p(x), \end{equation} where the compact set $A_p := \left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d: |x|^{2p}\leqslant 8\gamma_p/(Kh)\right\}\cap\mathbb{B}^h.$ Since $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ is a Feller process and $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ is $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}$-irreducible, $A_p$ is a petite set for $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ by using \cite[Proposition 6.2.8]{Meyn}. This, together with (\ref{Ev}), implies that condition $(\mathrm{ii})$ in Lemma \ref{GET} holds with $V_p(x) = 1+|x|^{2p}$, $\beta = 1-Kh/8$, $\gamma = \gamma_p$ and petite set $A_p$. According to Lemma \ref{GET} and Remark \ref{RE1}, there exists a unique invariant probability $\mu_h$ such that for any $k\geqslant 1$, $$ \sup_{g\in \mathbb{G}_{V_p}}|\mathbb{E} g(X_k)-\mu_h(g)|\leqslant \tilde{c} \mathrm{e}^{-k\ln \bar{c}}V_p(X_0)$$ for suitable constants $\tilde{c},\bar{c}>0$. This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Verify the Meyn-Tweedie criterion: Gaussian positivity gives irreducibility and aperiodicity, and a Lyapunov drift bound for $V_p=1+|x|^{2p}$ holds towards a petite set. The key step is the moment expansion controlling cross terms by dissipativity.

nodes.name: Reduce to the ergodicity criterion
nodes.statement: Fix $p\geqslant 1$, $\theta\in(0, \bar{\theta}]$ and $h\in(0, \bar{h}]$. Let \(\mathcal{E}_h:=\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap \mathbb{B}^h\), which is a $\Sigma$-algebra by \cite[p. 145, Lemma 3]{Pro}. For the numerical ergodicity, we only verify that conditions $(\mathrm{i})$ and $(\mathrm{ii})$ hold in Lemma \ref{GET} with $E = \mathbb{B}^h$. Since the proof is rather technical, we divide it into two steps.
nodes.statement_short: Fix parameters and reduce to verifying conditions (i) and (ii) of the Markov-chain ergodicity criterion on $\mathbb B^h$.

nodes.name: Step 1: irreducibility and aperiodicity
nodes.statement: {\bf Step 1: Irreducibility and aperiodicity.} Let \(\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}\) denote the Lebesgue measure restricted to \(\mathbb{B}^h\). For \(x\in \mathbb B^h\), the random variable \(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1\) has a strictly positive Gaussian density on \(\mathbb{R}^d\). Hence, for any \(x\in\mathbb{B}^h\) and nonempty set \(A\in\mathcal{E}_h\) with \(\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}(A)>0\), \[ \begin{aligned} P_X(x,A) = \mathbb{P}\big(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)\in A\big) &\geqslant \mathbb{P}\big(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1\in A\big) \\ &= \int_A p_{x+b(x)h,h\Sigma \Sigma^{\mathrm T}}(y)\,\mathrm{d} y >0. \end{aligned} \] Therefore, according to \cite[Proposition 4.2.1]{Meyn}, \((X_k)_{k\geqslant0}\) is $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}$-irreducible. We next show that it is aperiodic. Suppose, to the contrary, that the chain has period \(d_0\geqslant2\). Then, according to the definition of a periodic Markov chain \cite[p.122-123]{Meyn}, there exist disjoint nonempty sets \(D_1,\ldots,D_{d_0}\in\mathcal{E}_h\) such that \[ \mathbb{B}^h=\bigcup_{i=1}^{d_0}D_i, \qquad P_X(x,D_{i+1})=1,\quad x\in D_i, \] with the convention \(D_{d_0+1}=D_1\). Since $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}(\mathbb{B}^h)>0$, there exists an $i_0\in \{1, 2, \cdots, d_0\}$ such that $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}(D_{i_0} )>0$. By the irreducibility argument above, \[ P_X(x,D_{i_0})>0, \qquad x\in E_h. \] In particular, this holds for \(x\in D_{i_0}\). However, the cyclic decomposition implies \[ P_X(x,D_{i_0})=0, \qquad x\in D_{i_0}, \] because the chain must move from \(D_{i_0}\) to \(D_{i_0+1}\) in one step. This is a contradiction. Hence the chain is aperiodic.
nodes.statement_short: Positivity of the Gaussian transition density gives irreducibility; a cyclic decomposition leads to a contradiction, giving aperiodicity.

nodes.name: Lebesgue irreducibility
nodes.statement: {\bf Step 1: Irreducibility and aperiodicity.} Let \(\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}\) denote the Lebesgue measure restricted to \(\mathbb{B}^h\). For \(x\in \mathbb B^h\), the random variable \(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1\) has a strictly positive Gaussian density on \(\mathbb{R}^d\). Hence, for any \(x\in\mathbb{B}^h\) and nonempty set \(A\in\mathcal{E}_h\) with \(\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}(A)>0\), \[ \begin{aligned} P_X(x,A) = \mathbb{P}\big(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)\in A\big) &\geqslant \mathbb{P}\big(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1\in A\big) \\ &= \int_A p_{x+b(x)h,h\Sigma \Sigma^{\mathrm T}}(y)\,\mathrm{d} y >0. \end{aligned} \] Therefore, according to \cite[Proposition 4.2.1]{Meyn}, \((X_k)_{k\geqslant0}\) is $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}$-irreducible.
nodes.statement_short: The one-step law has positive Gaussian density, so the chain is Lebesgue-irreducible.

nodes.name: Aperiodicity by contradiction
nodes.statement: We next show that it is aperiodic. Suppose, to the contrary, that the chain has period \(d_0\geqslant2\). Then, according to the definition of a periodic Markov chain \cite[p.122-123]{Meyn}, there exist disjoint nonempty sets \(D_1,\ldots,D_{d_0}\in\mathcal{E}_h\) such that \[ \mathbb{B}^h=\bigcup_{i=1}^{d_0}D_i, \qquad P_X(x,D_{i+1})=1,\quad x\in D_i, \] with the convention \(D_{d_0+1}=D_1\). Since $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}(\mathbb{B}^h)>0$, there exists an $i_0\in \{1, 2, \cdots, d_0\}$ such that $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}(D_{i_0} )>0$. By the irreducibility argument above, \[ P_X(x,D_{i_0})>0, \qquad x\in E_h. \] In particular, this holds for \(x\in D_{i_0}\). However, the cyclic decomposition implies \[ P_X(x,D_{i_0})=0, \qquad x\in D_{i_0}, \] because the chain must move from \(D_{i_0}\) to \(D_{i_0+1}\) in one step. This is a contradiction. Hence the chain is aperiodic.
nodes.statement_short: Assume a period $d_0\ge2$; irreducibility contradicts the cyclic decomposition.

nodes.name: Step 2: Lyapunov drift condition
nodes.statement: {\bf Step 2: Lyapunov drift condition.} For any $x\in \mathbb{B}^h$, by \(|\pi_h(z)|\leqslant |z|\), we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) &= 1+\mathbb{E}|\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)|^{2p}\leqslant 1+\mathbb{E}|x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1|^{2p}, \end{align*} which yields \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \\ \leqslant &1+\mathbb{E}\left(|x|^2+2h\langle x, b(x) \rangle+h^2|b(x)|^2+|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\langle x+b(x)h,\Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right)^p. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Using Remark \ref{Re0} with $\epsilon = K/4$ implies that for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{equation} \langle x, b(x)\rangle \leqslant -\frac{3K}{4}|x|^2+R^2(L+K)+\frac{1}{K}|b(\mathbf{0})|^2. \end{equation} By (\ref{GL}), (\ref{Reeq}) and $M^2h^{2-2\theta}\leqslant Kh$, we further have for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{align*} 2h\langle x, b(x) \rangle+h^2|b(x)|^2 &\leqslant-\frac{3Kh}{2}|x|^2+2hR^2(L+K)+\frac{2h}{K}|b(\mathbf{0})|^2+M^2h^{2-2\theta} \left|x\right|^2\\ &\leqslant -\frac{Kh}{2}|x|^2+q_1h, \end{align*} where $q_1 := 2R^2(L+K)+2|b(\mathbf{0})|^2/K$. Substituting this into (\ref{Proeq1}), we obtain that \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1))\!\leqslant\! 1\!+\!\mathbb{E}\!\left(\!\left(1\!-\!Kh/2\right)|x|^2+q_1h\!+\!|\Sigma Z_1|^2\!+\!2\langle x\!+\!b(x)h, \!\Sigma Z_1 \rangle\!\right)^p\!. \end{equation} For $p =1$, since $\mathbb{E}\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle = 0$ and $\mathbb{E}|\Sigma Z_1|^{2p} \leqslant C_dh^p$ (see \cite{BMSC}), we have \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}V_1(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1))\leqslant 1+\left(1-\frac{Kh}{4}\right)|x|^2+\gamma_1 h, \end{aligned} \end{equation} where $\gamma_1:= q_1+C_d$. Next, we consider the case $p\geqslant 2$. For any $h\in(0, 2/K]$, we have \(1-Kh/2\in[0,1)\). Together with (\ref{EV}) and the binomial theorem, this gives that for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant 1+\left(1-\frac{Kh}{2}\right)|x|^{2p}+\mathrm{I}_1+\mathrm{I}_2, \end{align*} where $$\mathrm{I}_1 := p|x|^{2p-2}\left(q_1h+\mathbb{E}|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\mathbb{E}\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right),$$ $$\mathrm{I}_2:=\sum_{k =0}^{p-2}C_p^k|x|^{2k}\mathbb{E}\left(q_1h+|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right)^{p-k},$$ and $C_p^k := p!/(k!(p-k)!)$. Next, we estimate $\mathrm{I}_1$ and $\mathrm{I}_2$. Similar to the argument for \eqref{EV1}, we have \begin{equation} \mathrm{I}_1\leqslant p|x|^{2p-2}\left(q_1h+C_d\Sigma^2 h^p\right)\leqslant C_d|x|^{2p-2}h\leqslant Kh|x|^{2p}/8+C_dh. \end{equation} Since $C_p^k\leqslant C_p^{\lfloor p/2 \rfloor}$ for any $k\in[0, p]\cap \mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{E}|Z_1|^{p-k} \leqslant C_dh^{(p-k)/2}\leqslant C_dh$ for any $k\in[0,p-2]\cap\mathbb{N}$, and $|b(x)|h\leqslant Mh^{1-\theta}(1+|x|)\leqslant M\sqrt{h}(1+|x|)$ for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$, we have \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_2\leqslant C_p^{\lfloor p/2 \rfloor}\sum_{k =0}^{p-2}|x|^{2k}\mathbb{E}\left(q_1h+|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right)^{p-k}\!\leqslant\! C_d\sum_{k =0}^{p-2}\left(|x|^{2k}h^2+|x|^{p+k}h\right). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Noticing that $p/(p-k)\in[1, p/2]$ and $k/(p-k)\in[0, p/2-1]$ for any $k\in [0, p-2]$, by Young's inequality and \eqref{I2}, we have \begin{equation} \mathrm{I}_2\leqslant \frac{Kh}{8}|x|^{2p} + C_dh. \end{equation} This, together with (\ref{I1}) and (\ref{I2-}), implies that for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant \left(1-\frac{Kh}{4}\right)|x|^{2p}+\gamma_p, \end{equation} where $\gamma_p = 1+C_dh$. Therefore, combining (\ref{EV1}) with (\ref{Proeq5}), we obtain that for any $p\in[1, +\infty)\cap\mathbb{N}$ and $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$, $$\mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant \left(1-\frac{Kh}{4}\right)|x|^{2p}+\gamma_p = \left(1-\frac{Kh}{8}\right)|x|^{2p}+\left(\gamma_p -\frac{Kh}{8}|x|^{2p}\right).$$ Hence, for any $p\in\mathbb{N}$ and $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$, \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant \gamma_p\1_{A_p}(x)+\left(1-\frac{Kh}{8}\right) V_p(x), \end{equation} where the compact set $A_p := \left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d: |x|^{2p}\leqslant 8\gamma_p/(Kh)\right\}\cap\mathbb{B}^h.$ Since $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ is a Feller process and $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ is $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}$-irreducible, $A_p$ is a petite set for $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ by using \cite[Proposition 6.2.8]{Meyn}. This, together with (\ref{Ev}), implies that condition $(\mathrm{ii})$ in Lemma \ref{GET} holds with $V_p(x) = 1+|x|^{2p}$, $\beta = 1-Kh/8$, $\gamma = \gamma_p$ and petite set $A_p$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\mathbb E V_p$ after one step using dissipativity and Gaussian moments, giving a drift condition towards a petite set.

nodes.name: Expand the one-step Lyapunov function
nodes.statement: {\bf Step 2: Lyapunov drift condition.} For any $x\in \mathbb{B}^h$, by \(|\pi_h(z)|\leqslant |z|\), we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) &= 1+\mathbb{E}|\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)|^{2p}\leqslant 1+\mathbb{E}|x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1|^{2p}, \end{align*} which yields \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \\ \leqslant &1+\mathbb{E}\left(|x|^2+2h\langle x, b(x) \rangle+h^2|b(x)|^2+|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\langle x+b(x)h,\Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right)^p. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Using Remark \ref{Re0} with $\epsilon = K/4$ implies that for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{equation} \langle x, b(x)\rangle \leqslant -\frac{3K}{4}|x|^2+R^2(L+K)+\frac{1}{K}|b(\mathbf{0})|^2. \end{equation} By (\ref{GL}), (\ref{Reeq}) and $M^2h^{2-2\theta}\leqslant Kh$, we further have for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{align*} 2h\langle x, b(x) \rangle+h^2|b(x)|^2 &\leqslant-\frac{3Kh}{2}|x|^2+2hR^2(L+K)+\frac{2h}{K}|b(\mathbf{0})|^2+M^2h^{2-2\theta} \left|x\right|^2\\ &\leqslant -\frac{Kh}{2}|x|^2+q_1h, \end{align*} where $q_1 := 2R^2(L+K)+2|b(\mathbf{0})|^2/K$. Substituting this into (\ref{Proeq1}), we obtain that \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1))\!\leqslant\! 1\!+\!\mathbb{E}\!\left(\!\left(1\!-\!Kh/2\right)|x|^2+q_1h\!+\!|\Sigma Z_1|^2\!+\!2\langle x\!+\!b(x)h, \!\Sigma Z_1 \rangle\!\right)^p\!. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Use $|\pi_h(z)|\le|z|$, Remark 1 and the truncated drift bound to control the one-step second moment.

nodes.name: Equation (15)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \\ \leqslant &1+\mathbb{E}\left(|x|^2+2h\langle x, b(x) \rangle+h^2|b(x)|^2+|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\langle x+b(x)h,\Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right)^p. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: Proeq1

nodes.name: Equation (16)
nodes.statement: \langle x, b(x)\rangle \leqslant -\frac{3K}{4}|x|^2+R^2(L+K)+\frac{1}{K}|b(\mathbf{0})|^2.
nodes.label: Reeq

nodes.name: Equation (17)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1))\!\leqslant\! 1\!+\!\mathbb{E}\!\left(\!\left(1\!-\!Kh/2\right)|x|^2+q_1h\!+\!|\Sigma Z_1|^2\!+\!2\langle x\!+\!b(x)h, \!\Sigma Z_1 \rangle\!\right)^p\!.
nodes.label: EV

nodes.name: Case p = 1
nodes.statement: For $p =1$, since $\mathbb{E}\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle = 0$ and $\mathbb{E}|\Sigma Z_1|^{2p} \leqslant C_dh^p$ (see \cite{BMSC}), we have \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}V_1(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1))\leqslant 1+\left(1-\frac{Kh}{4}\right)|x|^2+\gamma_1 h, \end{aligned} \end{equation} where $\gamma_1:= q_1+C_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian moments give the drift inequality for $p=1$.

nodes.name: Equation (18)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}V_1(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1))\leqslant 1+\left(1-\frac{Kh}{4}\right)|x|^2+\gamma_1 h, \end{aligned}
nodes.label: EV1

nodes.name: Case p >= 2
nodes.statement: Next, we consider the case $p\geqslant 2$. For any $h\in(0, 2/K]$, we have \(1-Kh/2\in[0,1)\). Together with (\ref{EV}) and the binomial theorem, this gives that for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant 1+\left(1-\frac{Kh}{2}\right)|x|^{2p}+\mathrm{I}_1+\mathrm{I}_2, \end{align*} where $$\mathrm{I}_1 := p|x|^{2p-2}\left(q_1h+\mathbb{E}|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\mathbb{E}\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right),$$ $$\mathrm{I}_2:=\sum_{k =0}^{p-2}C_p^k|x|^{2k}\mathbb{E}\left(q_1h+|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right)^{p-k},$$ and $C_p^k := p!/(k!(p-k)!)$. Next, we estimate $\mathrm{I}_1$ and $\mathrm{I}_2$. Similar to the argument for \eqref{EV1}, we have \begin{equation} \mathrm{I}_1\leqslant p|x|^{2p-2}\left(q_1h+C_d\Sigma^2 h^p\right)\leqslant C_d|x|^{2p-2}h\leqslant Kh|x|^{2p}/8+C_dh. \end{equation} Since $C_p^k\leqslant C_p^{\lfloor p/2 \rfloor}$ for any $k\in[0, p]\cap \mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{E}|Z_1|^{p-k} \leqslant C_dh^{(p-k)/2}\leqslant C_dh$ for any $k\in[0,p-2]\cap\mathbb{N}$, and $|b(x)|h\leqslant Mh^{1-\theta}(1+|x|)\leqslant M\sqrt{h}(1+|x|)$ for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$, we have \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_2\leqslant C_p^{\lfloor p/2 \rfloor}\sum_{k =0}^{p-2}|x|^{2k}\mathbb{E}\left(q_1h+|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right)^{p-k}\!\leqslant\! C_d\sum_{k =0}^{p-2}\left(|x|^{2k}h^2+|x|^{p+k}h\right). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Noticing that $p/(p-k)\in[1, p/2]$ and $k/(p-k)\in[0, p/2-1]$ for any $k\in [0, p-2]$, by Young's inequality and \eqref{I2}, we have \begin{equation} \mathrm{I}_2\leqslant \frac{Kh}{8}|x|^{2p} + C_dh. \end{equation} This, together with (\ref{I1}) and (\ref{I2-}), implies that for any $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$ \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant \left(1-\frac{Kh}{4}\right)|x|^{2p}+\gamma_p, \end{equation} where $\gamma_p = 1+C_dh$. Therefore, combining (\ref{EV1}) with (\ref{Proeq5}), we obtain that for any $p\in[1, +\infty)\cap\mathbb{N}$ and $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$, $$\mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant \left(1-\frac{Kh}{4}\right)|x|^{2p}+\gamma_p = \left(1-\frac{Kh}{8}\right)|x|^{2p}+\left(\gamma_p -\frac{Kh}{8}|x|^{2p}\right).$$
nodes.statement_short: Binomial expansion and Young's inequality bound the cross terms $\mathrm I_1,\mathrm I_2$.

nodes.name: Equation (19)
nodes.statement: \mathrm{I}_1\leqslant p|x|^{2p-2}\left(q_1h+C_d\Sigma^2 h^p\right)\leqslant C_d|x|^{2p-2}h\leqslant Kh|x|^{2p}/8+C_dh.
nodes.label: I1

nodes.name: Equation (20)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_2\leqslant C_p^{\lfloor p/2 \rfloor}\sum_{k =0}^{p-2}|x|^{2k}\mathbb{E}\left(q_1h+|\Sigma Z_1|^2+2\langle x+b(x)h, \Sigma Z_1 \rangle\right)^{p-k}\!\leqslant\! C_d\sum_{k =0}^{p-2}\left(|x|^{2k}h^2+|x|^{p+k}h\right). \end{aligned}
nodes.label: I2

nodes.name: Equation (21)
nodes.statement: \mathrm{I}_2\leqslant \frac{Kh}{8}|x|^{2p} + C_dh.
nodes.label: I2-

nodes.name: Equation (22)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant \left(1-\frac{Kh}{4}\right)|x|^{2p}+\gamma_p,
nodes.label: Proeq5

nodes.name: Drift condition with a petite set
nodes.statement: Hence, for any $p\in\mathbb{N}$ and $x\in\mathbb{B}^h$, \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant \gamma_p\1_{A_p}(x)+\left(1-\frac{Kh}{8}\right) V_p(x), \end{equation} where the compact set $A_p := \left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d: |x|^{2p}\leqslant 8\gamma_p/(Kh)\right\}\cap\mathbb{B}^h.$ Since $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ is a Feller process and $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ is $\mu^{\mathrm{Leb}}$-irreducible, $A_p$ is a petite set for $(X_k)_{k\geqslant 0}$ by using \cite[Proposition 6.2.8]{Meyn}. This, together with (\ref{Ev}), implies that condition $(\mathrm{ii})$ in Lemma \ref{GET} holds with $V_p(x) = 1+|x|^{2p}$, $\beta = 1-Kh/8$, $\gamma = \gamma_p$ and petite set $A_p$.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain the drift inequality with the compact set $A_p$, which is petite by the Feller property and irreducibility.

nodes.name: Equation (23)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}V_p(\pi_h(x+b(x)h+\Sigma Z_1)) \leqslant \gamma_p\1_{A_p}(x)+\left(1-\frac{Kh}{8}\right) V_p(x),
nodes.label: Ev

nodes.name: Apply the ergodicity criterion
nodes.statement: According to Lemma \ref{GET} and Remark \ref{RE1}, there exists a unique invariant probability $\mu_h$ such that for any $k\geqslant 1$, $$ \sup_{g\in \mathbb{G}_{V_p}}|\mathbb{E} g(X_k)-\mu_h(g)|\leqslant \tilde{c} \mathrm{e}^{-k\ln \bar{c}}V_p(X_0)$$ for suitable constants $\tilde{c},\bar{c}>0$. This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: The criterion yields a unique invariant measure with geometric convergence.

nodes.name: Extension of TEM ergodicity beyond uniform dissipativity
nodes.statement: In \cite{IMA}, the existence and uniqueness of the numerical invariant measure for the TEM scheme were obtained under the uniformly dissipative condition. Since Assumption \ref{A1} reduces to the uniformly dissipative case when \(R=0\) in \eqref{CaI}, the present result extends the corresponding result in \cite{IMA} to the weaker long-distance dissipativity setting.

nodes.name: Exponential ergodicity of the TEM scheme in Wasserstein distance
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{A} and \ref{A1} hold. For any \(h\in(0,\bar h]\), where \(\bar h\) is given in Lemma \ref{Le2}, for any \(q\geqslant1\) and \(k\geqslant1\), the numerical solution \((X_k)_{k\geqslant0}\) satisfies \begin{equation*} \mathcal{W}_q(\mathcal{L}(X_k), \mu_h)\leqslant C_q (1+|x_0|)\mathrm{e}^{-\bar{c}'k}, \end{equation*} where $\bar{c}' = \ln \bar{c}/(q+2)$ and $\bar{c}>1$ are given in Theorem \ref{Pro1}. Here \(C_q>0\) is a constant independent of \(k\).
nodes.statement_short: The law of the TEM chain converges exponentially fast to $\mu_h$ in every $\mathcal W_q$, $q\geq1$.
nodes.label: Co

nodes.name: Proof of Exponential ergodicity of the TEM scheme in Wasserstein distance
nodes.statement:
We first recall the following standard estimate connecting the Wasserstein distance with a weighted total variation norm \cite[Theorem 6.15]{CV}. For any \(\mu,
u\in\mathcal{P}_{2p}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) with $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|x|^{2p}\mathrm{d} |\mu-
u|(x)<\infty$, \[\mathcal{W}_{2p}^{2p}(\mu,
u) \leqslant 2^{2p}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}(1+|x|^{2p})|\mu-
u|(\mathrm{d} x).\] By the dual representation of the weighted total variation norm \cite[p.110-111]{Hairer}, \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}(1+|x|^{2p})|\mu-
u|(\mathrm{d} x) = \sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_{V_p}} |\mu(g)-
u(g)|, \] where \(V_p(x)=1+|x|^{2p}\). Taking \(\mu=\mathcal{L}(X_k)\) and \(
u=\mu_h\), and using Theorem ef{Pro1}, we get \[ \sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_{V_p}} |\mathbb{E} g(X_k)-\mu_h(g)| \leqslant 	ilde c  ar c^{-k}(1+|x_0|^{2p}). \] Therefore, \[\mathcal{W}_{2p}(\mathcal{L}(X_k),\mu_h) \leqslant 2\left( \sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_{V_p}} |\mathbb{E} g(X_k)-\mu_h(g)| ight)^{1/(2p)} \leqslant 2	ilde c^{1/(2p)} \exp\left(- rac{k\ln ar c}{2p}ight) (1+|x_0|).\] Now let \(q\geqslant1\). Choose \(p\in\mathbb{N}\) such that \(q\in[2(p-1),2p)\). Then, by the monotonicity of Wasserstein distances, \[ \mathcal{W}_q(\mathcal{L}(X_k),\mu_h) \leqslant \mathcal{W}_{2p}(\mathcal{L}(X_k),\mu_h). \] Therefore, \[ \mathcal{W}_q(\mathcal{L}(X_k),\mu_h) \leqslant C_q(1+|x_0|) \exp\left(- rac{k\ln ar c}{q+2}ight). \] This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\mathcal W_{2p}$ by a weighted total-variation norm and apply the geometric ergodicity of Theorem 3.3; monotonicity in $q$ finishes.

u|(\mathrm{d} x).\] By the dual representation of the weighted total variation norm \cite[p.110-111]{Hairer}, \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}(1+|x|^{2p})|\mu-
u|(\mathrm{d} x) = \sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_{V_p}} |\mu(g)-
u(g)|, \] where \(V_p(x)=1+|x|^{2p}\).
nodes.statement_short: Recall the bound of $\mathcal W_{2p}^{2p}$ by a weighted total variation norm and its dual representation.

nodes.name: Apply numerical ergodicity
nodes.statement: Taking \(\mu=\mathcal{L}(X_k)\) and \(\nu=\mu_h\), and using Theorem \ref{Pro1}, we get \[ \sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_{V_p}} |\mathbb{E} g(X_k)-\mu_h(g)| \leqslant \tilde c \bar c^{-k}(1+|x_0|^{2p}). \] Therefore, \[\mathcal{W}_{2p}(\mathcal{L}(X_k),\mu_h) \leqslant 2\left( \sup_{g\in\mathbb{G}_{V_p}} |\mathbb{E} g(X_k)-\mu_h(g)| \right)^{1/(2p)} \leqslant 2\tilde c^{1/(2p)} \exp\left(-\frac{k\ln\bar c}{2p}\right) (1+|x_0|).\]
nodes.statement_short: Insert the geometric ergodicity bound of Theorem 3.3 to bound $\mathcal W_{2p}$.

nodes.name: Pass to general q
nodes.statement: Now let \(q\geqslant1\). Choose \(p\in\mathbb{N}\) such that \(q\in[2(p-1),2p)\). Then, by the monotonicity of Wasserstein distances, \[ \mathcal{W}_q(\mathcal{L}(X_k),\mu_h) \leqslant \mathcal{W}_{2p}(\mathcal{L}(X_k),\mu_h). \] Therefore, \[ \mathcal{W}_q(\mathcal{L}(X_k),\mu_h) \leqslant C_q(1+|x_0|) \exp\left(-\frac{k\ln\bar c}{q+2}\right). \] This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Use monotonicity of Wasserstein distances in $q$.

nodes.name: Polynomial Lipschitz condition (Assumption 3)
nodes.statement: There exist constants $L^*>0$ and $\ell>0$ such that for any $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$, \begin{equation*} |b(x)-b(y)|\leqslant L^*(1+|x|^\ell+|y|^\ell)|x-y|. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: A2

nodes.name: Polynomial growth of the drift
nodes.statement: Under Assumption \ref{A2}, by Young's inequality, one notes that for any $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ \[|b(x)|\leq \frac{L^*(\ell+2)}{\ell+1}|x|^{\ell+1}+\frac{L^*\ell}{\ell+1}+|b(\mathbf{0})|.\]
nodes.label: PG

nodes.name: Choice of the modulus function phi under polynomial Lipschitz condition
nodes.statement: Under Assumption \ref{A2}, we observe that any function $\phi$ with $\phi(u)\geqslant L^*(1+2u^\ell)$ for any $u>0$ satisfies \eqref{Tr}. In particular, we choose $\phi(u) = L^*(1+2u^\ell),~\forall~u\geqslant0$. Then, $\phi^{-1}(u) = ((u-L^*)/(2L^*))^{1/\ell}$ for all $u\geqslant L^*$.
nodes.label: mapping form

nodes.name: Auxiliary one-step process hat S_k
nodes.statement: For convenience, we introduce the auxiliary one-step process $(\hat{S}_{k})_{k=1}^\infty$ by \begin{equation} \hat{S}_{k}:= \pi_h(x_{t_{k-1}}) + hb(\pi_h(x_{t_{k-1}})) + \Sigma Z_{k},\quad k\geqslant 1. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\hat S_k$ is one TEM step started from the projected exact solution $\pi_h(x_{t_{k-1}})$.

nodes.name: Auxiliary one-step process
nodes.statement: \hat{S}_{k}:= \pi_h(x_{t_{k-1}}) + hb(\pi_h(x_{t_{k-1}})) + \Sigma Z_{k},\quad k\geqslant 1.
nodes.label: S

nodes.name: Three-term error decomposition
nodes.statement: By the triangle inequality, we obtain the following error decomposition: \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\left|X_{k}-x_{t_{k}}\right|\leqslant\mathbb{E}|X_{k}-\hat{X}_{k}|+\mathbb{E} |\hat{X}_{k}-\hat{S}_{k}|+ \mathbb{E} |\hat{S}_{k}-x_{t_{k}}|. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Truncation error of the projection pi_h
nodes.statement: For any \(M\geqslant 3L^*\), \(p,q>1\) with \(1/p+1/q=1\), and \(s,n\geqslant1\), if \[ \zeta\in L^{np}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L^{sq}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d), \] then \[ \mathbb{E} \left|\pi_h(\zeta)-\zeta\right|^n \leqslant 2^n\|\zeta\|^n_{np}\|\zeta\|^s_{sq} \left(3L^*M^{-1}\right)^{s/\ell}h^{s\theta/\ell}. \]
nodes.statement_short: The $n$-th moment of $\pi_h(\zeta)-\zeta$ decays like $h^{s\theta/\ell}$ for random vectors with finite moments.
nodes.label: Le4

nodes.name: Proof of Truncation error of the projection pi_h
nodes.statement: Define $$\mathbb{A}_h := \left\{\omega\in\Omega: |\zeta(\omega)|\leqslant \left(\frac{Mh^{-\theta}-L^*}{2L^*}\right)^{1/\ell}\right\}.$$ On \(\mathbb A_h\), we have \(\pi_h(\zeta)=\zeta\). Hence, by H{\"o}lder's inequality \cite[p.5]{Mao} and the fact $|\pi_h(\zeta)|\leqslant |\zeta|$, we obtain that for any $n\geqslant 1$, \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}|\zeta\!-\!\pi_h(\zeta)|^n \!=\! \mathbb{E}\!\left(|\zeta\!-\!\pi_h(\zeta)|^n\1_{\mathbb{A}_h^c}\!\right) \leqslant \left(\mathbb{E} |\zeta-\!\pi_h(\zeta)|^{np}\right)^\frac{1}{p}\!\left(\mathbb{P}(\mathbb{A}_h^c)\right)^{\frac{1}{q}}\leqslant 2^n \|\zeta\|^n_{np}\left(\mathbb{P}(\mathbb{A}_h^c)\right)^{\frac{1}{q}}\!. \end{equation} By Chebyshev's inequality \cite[p.5]{Mao}, $$\left(\mathbb{P}(\mathbb{A}_h^c)\right)^{\frac{1}{q}}\leqslant \|\zeta\|_{sq}^s\left(\frac{Mh^{-\theta}-L^*}{2L^*}\right)^{-s/\ell}.$$ Since \(M\geqslant3L^*\) and \(h\in(0,1]\), we have $(Mh^{-\theta}-L^*)/(2L^*)\geqslant Mh^{-\theta}/(3L^*).$ Consequently, for any $s\geqslant 1$, $\left((Mh^{-\theta}-L^*)/(2L^*)\right)^{-s/\ell}\leqslant \left(3L^*M^{-1}\right)^{s/\ell}h^{s\theta/\ell}$. Substituting this estimate into \eqref{Leeq1} gives the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Hoelder and Chebyshev on the event where the projection is active.

nodes.name: Event where the projection is inactive
nodes.statement: Define $$\mathbb{A}_h := \left\{\omega\in\Omega: |\zeta(\omega)|\leqslant \left(\frac{Mh^{-\theta}-L^*}{2L^*}\right)^{1/\ell}\right\}.$$ On \(\mathbb A_h\), we have \(\pi_h(\zeta)=\zeta\).
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the event $\mathbb A_h$ on which $\pi_h(\zeta)=\zeta$.

nodes.name: Hoelder's inequality
nodes.statement: Hence, by H{\"o}lder's inequality \cite[p.5]{Mao} and the fact $|\pi_h(\zeta)|\leqslant |\zeta|$, we obtain that for any $n\geqslant 1$, \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}|\zeta\!-\!\pi_h(\zeta)|^n \!=\! \mathbb{E}\!\left(|\zeta\!-\!\pi_h(\zeta)|^n\1_{\mathbb{A}_h^c}\!\right) \leqslant \left(\mathbb{E} |\zeta-\!\pi_h(\zeta)|^{np}\right)^\frac{1}{p}\!\left(\mathbb{P}(\mathbb{A}_h^c)\right)^{\frac{1}{q}}\leqslant 2^n \|\zeta\|^n_{np}\left(\mathbb{P}(\mathbb{A}_h^c)\right)^{\frac{1}{q}}\!. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Hoelder's inequality reduces the error to $\mathbb P(\mathbb A_h^c)^{1/q}$.

nodes.name: Equation (25)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}|\zeta\!-\!\pi_h(\zeta)|^n \!=\! \mathbb{E}\!\left(|\zeta\!-\!\pi_h(\zeta)|^n\1_{\mathbb{A}_h^c}\!\right) \leqslant \left(\mathbb{E} |\zeta-\!\pi_h(\zeta)|^{np}\right)^\frac{1}{p}\!\left(\mathbb{P}(\mathbb{A}_h^c)\right)^{\frac{1}{q}}\leqslant 2^n \|\zeta\|^n_{np}\left(\mathbb{P}(\mathbb{A}_h^c)\right)^{\frac{1}{q}}\!.
nodes.label: Leeq1

nodes.name: Chebyshev bound on the bad event
nodes.statement: By Chebyshev's inequality \cite[p.5]{Mao}, $$\left(\mathbb{P}(\mathbb{A}_h^c)\right)^{\frac{1}{q}}\leqslant \|\zeta\|_{sq}^s\left(\frac{Mh^{-\theta}-L^*}{2L^*}\right)^{-s/\ell}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\mathbb P(\mathbb A_h^c)$ by Chebyshev.

nodes.name: Simplify and conclude
nodes.statement: Since \(M\geqslant3L^*\) and \(h\in(0,1]\), we have $(Mh^{-\theta}-L^*)/(2L^*)\geqslant Mh^{-\theta}/(3L^*).$ Consequently, for any $s\geqslant 1$, $\left((Mh^{-\theta}-L^*)/(2L^*)\right)^{-s/\ell}\leqslant \left(3L^*M^{-1}\right)^{s/\ell}h^{s\theta/\ell}$. Substituting this estimate into \eqref{Leeq1} gives the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Simplify the radius bound using $M\ge3L^*$ and substitute.

nodes.name: Proof of Uniform truncation estimates
nodes.statement: Applying Lemma \ref{Le4} together with the uniform moment bounds of the exact and numerical solutions, we obtain the following uniform truncation estimates.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the truncation-error lemma with the uniform moment bounds of the exact and numerical solutions.

nodes.name: Uniform truncation estimates
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{A1} and \ref{A2} hold. For any \(M\geqslant |b(\mathbf{0})|\vee 3L^*\), \(\theta\in(0,\bar{\theta}]\), and \(h\in(0,\bar h]\), the exact solution \((x_t)_{t\geqslant0}\) and the numerical solution \((X_k)_{k\geqslant0}\) defined by \eqref{TEM} satisfy that, for any \(s,n\geqslant1\), \[ \sup_{t\geqslant0}\mathbb{E}|\pi_h(x_t)-x_t|^n \leqslant Ch^{s\theta/\ell}, \qquad \sup_{k\geqslant0}\mathbb{E}|X_k-\hat X_k|^n \leqslant Ch^{s\theta/\ell}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Truncation errors of the exact and numerical solutions are $O(h^{s\theta/\ell})$ uniformly in time.
nodes.label: co2

nodes.name: Local consistency error of the auxiliary one-step process
nodes.statement: Let Assumption \ref{A2} hold. Then \(\sup_{k\geqslant1}\mathbb{E}|\hat S_k-x_{t_k}| \leqslant Ch^{3/2}\).
nodes.statement_short: The one-step process $\hat S_k$ is within $O(h^{3/2})$ of the exact solution uniformly in $k$.
nodes.label: Le5

nodes.name: Proof of Local consistency error of the auxiliary one-step process
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{E} with \eqref{S}, we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{E} |\hat S_{k+1}-x_{t_{k+1}}| = \mathbb{E}\left| \pi_h(x_{t_k}) +h b(\pi_h(x_{t_k})) -x_{t_k} -\int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} b(x_t)\mathrm{d} t \right| \leqslant J_1+J_2+J_3, \end{equation} where \[ J_1:=\mathbb{E}|\pi_h(x_{t_k})-x_{t_k}|, \qquad J_2:=h\mathbb{E}|b(\pi_h(x_{t_k}))-b(x_{t_k})|, \] and \[ J_3:= \mathbb{E}\left| \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \bigl[b(x_{t_k})-b(x_t)\bigr]\mathrm{d} t \right|. \] By Corollary \ref{co2}, choosing \(s\geqslant 1\vee 3\ell/(2\theta)\), we get \begin{equation} J_1 \leqslant Ch^{s\theta/\ell} \leqslant Ch^{3/2}. \end{equation} Using Assumption \ref{A2}, Hölder's inequality, Lemma \ref{Ju}, and Corollary \ref{co2}, for \(s\geqslant 1\vee \ell/(2\theta)\), we obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} J_2 &\leqslant hL^* \mathbb{E}\left[ (1+|\pi_h(x_{t_k})|^\ell+|x_{t_k}|^\ell) |\pi_h(x_{t_k})-x_{t_k}| \right] \\ &\leqslant hL^* \left( \mathbb{E}(1+|\pi_h(x_{t_k})|^\ell+|x_{t_k}|^\ell)^2 \right)^{1/2} \left( \mathbb{E}|\pi_h(x_{t_k})-x_{t_k}|^2 \right)^{1/2} \\ &\leqslant Ch^{1+s\theta/\ell} \leqslant Ch^{3/2}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} For \(J_3\), by Assumption \ref{A2}, Hölder's inequality, and Lemma \ref{Ju}, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} J_3 &\leqslant L^* \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}\left[ (1+|x_{t_k}|^\ell+|x_t|^\ell) |x_{t_k}-x_t| \right]\mathrm{d} t \\ &\leqslant L^* \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}(1+|x_{t_k}|^\ell+|x_t|^\ell)^2\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2} \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}|x_{t_k}-x_t|^2\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2} \\ &\leqslant C\sqrt h \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}|x_t-x_{t_k}|^2\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Moreover, by Hölder's inequality, Itô's isometry, Remark \ref{PG}, and Lemma \ref{Ju}, for any \(t\in(t_k,t_{k+1}]\), \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}|x_t-x_{t_k}|^2 &= \mathbb{E}\left| \int_{t_k}^t b(x_u)\mathrm{d} u + \Sigma(B_t-B_{t_k}) \right|^2 \\ &\leqslant 2(t-t_k)\int_{t_k}^t \mathbb{E}|b(x_u)|^2\mathrm{d} u + 2|\Sigma|^2(t-t_k) \\ &\leqslant C\bigl[(t-t_k)^2+(t-t_k)\bigr]. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Substituting \eqref{Lqq4} into \eqref{LEeq3} yields \begin{equation} J_3 \leqslant C\sqrt h \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \bigl[(t-t_k)^2+(t-t_k)\bigr]\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2} \leqslant C\sqrt h\,(h^3+h^2)^{1/2} \leqslant Ch^{3/2}. \end{equation} Combining \eqref{LEeq}, \eqref{LEeq1}, \eqref{LEeq2}, and \eqref{LEeq4}, we obtain \(\mathbb{E}|\hat S_{k+1}-x_{t_{k+1}}| \leqslant Ch^{3/2}\). Taking the supremum over \(k\geqslant0\) completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Split the local error into three terms and bound each by $Ch^{3/2}$ via truncation estimates, polynomial Lipschitz bounds and Ito isometry.

nodes.name: Split the local error into three terms
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{E} with \eqref{S}, we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{E} |\hat S_{k+1}-x_{t_{k+1}}| = \mathbb{E}\left| \pi_h(x_{t_k}) +h b(\pi_h(x_{t_k})) -x_{t_k} -\int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} b(x_t)\mathrm{d} t \right| \leqslant J_1+J_2+J_3, \end{equation} where \[ J_1:=\mathbb{E}|\pi_h(x_{t_k})-x_{t_k}|, \qquad J_2:=h\mathbb{E}|b(\pi_h(x_{t_k}))-b(x_{t_k})|, \] and \[ J_3:= \mathbb{E}\left| \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \bigl[b(x_{t_k})-b(x_t)\bigr]\mathrm{d} t \right|. \]
nodes.statement_short: Write the local error as truncation, drift-truncation and drift-variation terms $J_1,J_2,J_3$.

nodes.name: Equation (26)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E} |\hat S_{k+1}-x_{t_{k+1}}| = \mathbb{E}\left| \pi_h(x_{t_k}) +h b(\pi_h(x_{t_k})) -x_{t_k} -\int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} b(x_t)\mathrm{d} t \right| \leqslant J_1+J_2+J_3,
nodes.label: LEeq

nodes.name: Bound J_1
nodes.statement: By Corollary \ref{co2}, choosing \(s\geqslant 1\vee 3\ell/(2\theta)\), we get \begin{equation} J_1 \leqslant Ch^{s\theta/\ell} \leqslant Ch^{3/2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 4.2 gives $J_1\le Ch^{3/2}$.

nodes.name: Equation (27)
nodes.statement: J_1 \leqslant Ch^{s\theta/\ell} \leqslant Ch^{3/2}.
nodes.label: LEeq1

nodes.name: Bound J_2
nodes.statement: Using Assumption \ref{A2}, Hölder's inequality, Lemma \ref{Ju}, and Corollary \ref{co2}, for \(s\geqslant 1\vee \ell/(2\theta)\), we obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} J_2 &\leqslant hL^* \mathbb{E}\left[ (1+|\pi_h(x_{t_k})|^\ell+|x_{t_k}|^\ell) |\pi_h(x_{t_k})-x_{t_k}| \right] \\ &\leqslant hL^* \left( \mathbb{E}(1+|\pi_h(x_{t_k})|^\ell+|x_{t_k}|^\ell)^2 \right)^{1/2} \left( \mathbb{E}|\pi_h(x_{t_k})-x_{t_k}|^2 \right)^{1/2} \\ &\leqslant Ch^{1+s\theta/\ell} \leqslant Ch^{3/2}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Polynomial Lipschitz bound, Hoelder and moment bounds give $J_2\le Ch^{3/2}$.

nodes.name: Equation (28)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} J_2 &\leqslant hL^* \mathbb{E}\left[ (1+|\pi_h(x_{t_k})|^\ell+|x_{t_k}|^\ell) |\pi_h(x_{t_k})-x_{t_k}| \right] \\ &\leqslant hL^* \left( \mathbb{E}(1+|\pi_h(x_{t_k})|^\ell+|x_{t_k}|^\ell)^2 \right)^{1/2} \left( \mathbb{E}|\pi_h(x_{t_k})-x_{t_k}|^2 \right)^{1/2} \\ &\leqslant Ch^{1+s\theta/\ell} \leqslant Ch^{3/2}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: LEeq2

nodes.name: Reduce J_3 to increments
nodes.statement: For \(J_3\), by Assumption \ref{A2}, Hölder's inequality, and Lemma \ref{Ju}, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} J_3 &\leqslant L^* \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}\left[ (1+|x_{t_k}|^\ell+|x_t|^\ell) |x_{t_k}-x_t| \right]\mathrm{d} t \\ &\leqslant L^* \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}(1+|x_{t_k}|^\ell+|x_t|^\ell)^2\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2} \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}|x_{t_k}-x_t|^2\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2} \\ &\leqslant C\sqrt h \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}|x_t-x_{t_k}|^2\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $J_3$ by the mean-square increment of $x_t$.

nodes.name: Equation (29)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} J_3 &\leqslant L^* \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}\left[ (1+|x_{t_k}|^\ell+|x_t|^\ell) |x_{t_k}-x_t| \right]\mathrm{d} t \\ &\leqslant L^* \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}(1+|x_{t_k}|^\ell+|x_t|^\ell)^2\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2} \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}|x_{t_k}-x_t|^2\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2} \\ &\leqslant C\sqrt h \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \mathbb{E}|x_t-x_{t_k}|^2\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: LEeq3

nodes.name: Mean-square increment bound
nodes.statement: Moreover, by Hölder's inequality, Itô's isometry, Remark \ref{PG}, and Lemma \ref{Ju}, for any \(t\in(t_k,t_{k+1}]\), \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}|x_t-x_{t_k}|^2 &= \mathbb{E}\left| \int_{t_k}^t b(x_u)\mathrm{d} u + \Sigma(B_t-B_{t_k}) \right|^2 \\ &\leqslant 2(t-t_k)\int_{t_k}^t \mathbb{E}|b(x_u)|^2\mathrm{d} u + 2|\Sigma|^2(t-t_k) \\ &\leqslant C\bigl[(t-t_k)^2+(t-t_k)\bigr]. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Ito isometry and moment bounds give $\mathbb E|x_t-x_{t_k}|^2\le C(t-t_k)$.

nodes.name: Equation (30)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}|x_t-x_{t_k}|^2 &= \mathbb{E}\left| \int_{t_k}^t b(x_u)\mathrm{d} u + \Sigma(B_t-B_{t_k}) \right|^2 \\ &\leqslant 2(t-t_k)\int_{t_k}^t \mathbb{E}|b(x_u)|^2\mathrm{d} u + 2|\Sigma|^2(t-t_k) \\ &\leqslant C\bigl[(t-t_k)^2+(t-t_k)\bigr]. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: Lqq4

nodes.name: Bound J_3
nodes.statement: Substituting \eqref{Lqq4} into \eqref{LEeq3} yields \begin{equation} J_3 \leqslant C\sqrt h \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \bigl[(t-t_k)^2+(t-t_k)\bigr]\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2} \leqslant C\sqrt h\,(h^3+h^2)^{1/2} \leqslant Ch^{3/2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute to get $J_3\le Ch^{3/2}$.

nodes.name: Equation (31)
nodes.statement: J_3 \leqslant C\sqrt h \left( \int_{t_k}^{t_{k+1}} \bigl[(t-t_k)^2+(t-t_k)\bigr]\mathrm{d} t \right)^{1/2} \leqslant C\sqrt h\,(h^3+h^2)^{1/2} \leqslant Ch^{3/2}.
nodes.label: LEeq4

nodes.name: Combine the three bounds
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{LEeq}, \eqref{LEeq1}, \eqref{LEeq2}, and \eqref{LEeq4}, we obtain \(\mathbb{E}|\hat S_{k+1}-x_{t_{k+1}}| \leqslant Ch^{3/2}\). Taking the supremum over \(k\geqslant0\) completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the bounds and take the supremum over $k$.

nodes.name: One-step TEM map hat X_h and u_h
nodes.statement: For any \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\), let \(Z\sim N(\mathbf{0},h\mathbf{I}_q)\) and define \[ \hat X_h(x,Z):=u_h(x)+\Sigma Z, \] where \(u_h(x):=\pi_h(x)+h b(\pi_h(x))\) and \(\pi_h\) is defined by \eqref{TF}.

nodes.name: One-step separation hat r_h
nodes.statement: For \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d\), set \[ \hat r_h(x,y):=u_h(x)-u_h(y). \]

nodes.name: Gamma^{-1}-inner product and reflection operator
nodes.statement: For \(\mathbf{0}\neq r\in \mathbb{R}^d\) and \(a, b\in \mathbb{R}^d\), define \[ \langle a,b\rangle_\Gamma:=a^{\mathrm T}\Gamma^{-1}b, \qquad |a|_\Gamma:=\langle a,a\rangle_\Gamma^{1/2}, \] and define the \(\Gamma^{-1}\)-reflection operator \(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma\) by \[ \mathcal R_r^\Gamma w := w-2\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2}r, \qquad w\in\mathbb R^d. \]
nodes.statement_short: Inner product weighted by $\Gamma^{-1}$ and the reflection $w\mapsto w-2\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma r/|r|_\Gamma^2$.

nodes.name: One-dimensional projection and truncation set
nodes.statement: Furthermore, define the one-dimensional projection \[ \lambda_r(w) := \frac{|r|}{|r|_\Gamma^2}\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma, \qquad w\in\mathbb R^d, \] and, for \(m>0\), \[ A_r^m := \{w\in\mathbb R^d:|\lambda_r(w)|\leqslant m\}. \]

nodes.name: Gaussian density and maximal-coupling weight
nodes.statement: Finally, let \[ \varphi_\Gamma(w) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{(2\pi h)^d\det\Gamma}} \exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2h}|w|_\Gamma^2\right\} \] be the density of \(N(0,h\Gamma)\), and set \[ v_r^m(w) := \left[ \frac{\varphi_\Gamma(r+w)}{\varphi_\Gamma(w)} \mathbf 1_{A_r^m}(w)\mathbf 1_{A_r^m}(r+w) \right] \wedge \mathbf 1_{A_r^m}(w). \] When \(r=\mathbf{0}\), we set \(v_{\mathbf{0}}^m\equiv1\).
nodes.statement_short: $\varphi_\Gamma$ is the $N(0,h\Gamma)$ density and $v_r^m$ the truncated density-ratio weight used to decide coalescence.

nodes.name: Uniform randomisation variable zeta
nodes.statement: Let \(\zeta\) be uniformly distributed on \([0,1]\), independently of \(Z\).

nodes.name: One-step reflection-synchronous coupling for the TEM scheme
nodes.statement: For \(\hat r_h(x,y)=\mathbf{0}\), set \(\hat Y_h(x,y, Z):=u_h(y)+\Sigma Z\). For \(\hat r_h(x,y)\neq\mathbf{0}\), define \begin{equation} \hat Y_h(x,y, Z) := \begin{cases} u_h(x)+\Sigma Z, & \zeta\leqslant v_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m(\Sigma Z),\ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m,\ |\hat r_h(x,y)|\leqslant 2R,\\[1mm] u_h(y)+\mathcal R_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^\Gamma\Sigma Z, & \zeta> v_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m(\Sigma Z),\ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m,\ |\hat r_h(x,y)|\leqslant 2R,\\[1mm] u_h(y)+\Sigma Z, & \Sigma Z\notin A_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m\ \text{or}\ |\hat r_h(x,y)|>2R . \end{cases} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Coalesce or reflect the noise (in $\Gamma^{-1}$-geometry) when the updated separation is at most $2R$ and the projected noise is small; otherwise use synchronous coupling.

nodes.name: One-step coupling Y_h
nodes.statement: \hat Y_h(x,y, Z) := \begin{cases} u_h(x)+\Sigma Z, & \zeta\leqslant v_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m(\Sigma Z),\ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m,\ |\hat r_h(x,y)|\leqslant 2R,\\[1mm] u_h(y)+\mathcal R_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^\Gamma\Sigma Z, & \zeta> v_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m(\Sigma Z),\ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m,\ |\hat r_h(x,y)|\leqslant 2R,\\[1mm] u_h(y)+\Sigma Z, & \Sigma Z\notin A_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m\ \text{or}\ |\hat r_h(x,y)|>2R . \end{cases}
nodes.label: hY

nodes.name: Discrete-time nature and directional truncation of the coupling
nodes.statement: The coupling constructed above is formulated entirely in a discrete-time framework. Our construction is tailored to the one-step transition of the TEM scheme. In particular, the coupling is applied directly to the nonlinear numerical map \[x\mapsto u_h(x)=\pi_h(x)+h b(\pi_h(x)),\] rather than to the exact continuous-time flow. This is essential for the analysis of the numerical scheme, since the projection operator \(\pi_h\) and the nonlinear drift both enter the transition mechanism. Moreover, the present construction uses a directional control of the noise. Instead of restricting the full noise magnitude \(|\Sigma Z|\) as in \cite{Majka}, we control only its projection along the direction of the one-step separation, \(|\lambda_{\hat r_h(x,y)}(\Sigma Z)|\). This directional truncation is more refined, since only the component of the noise that directly affects the coupling distance is restricted. It also reduces the relevant estimates to one-dimensional Gaussian integrals along the coupling direction, which is useful for treating high-dimensional problems in the subsequent analysis.
nodes.statement_short: The coupling acts on the nonlinear numerical one-step map and truncates only the noise component along the separation direction.

nodes.name: Properties of the Gamma^{-1}-reflection
nodes.statement: For \(\mathbf 0 \neq r\in\mathbb R^d\), the following properties hold. \begin{equation} \mathcal R_r^\Gamma r=-r, \qquad \bigl(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma\bigr)^2=\mathbf I . \end{equation} For every \(w\in\mathbb R^d\), \begin{equation} \langle r,\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\rangle_\Gamma = -\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma,\qquad |\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w|_\Gamma=|w|_\Gamma. \end{equation} Moreover, \begin{equation} \det(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma)=-1, \qquad |\det(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma)|=1. \end{equation} Consequently, for the Gaussian density \(\varphi_\Gamma\), \begin{equation} \varphi_\Gamma(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w)=\varphi_\Gamma(w), \qquad w\in\mathbb R^d . \end{equation} Furthermore, \begin{equation} \lambda_r(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w) = -\lambda_r(w), \qquad w\in\mathbb R^d, \end{equation} and hence, for every \(m>0\) and \(w\in A_r^m\) \begin{equation} w\in A_r^m\Longleftrightarrow \mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\in A_r^m. \end{equation} Finally, for every \(u\in\mathbb R^d\), \begin{equation} r+\mathcal R_r^\Gamma u = \mathcal R_r^\Gamma(u-r). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The $\Gamma^{-1}$-reflection is an involution with determinant $-1$ that preserves the Gaussian density and flips the projection $\lambda_r$.
conclusions: \begin{equation} \mathcal R_r^\Gamma r=-r, \qquad \bigl(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma\bigr)^2=\mathbf I . \end{equation} For every \(w\in\mathbb R^d\), \begin{equation} \langle r,\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\rangle_\Gamma = -\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma,\qquad |\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w|_\Gamma=|w|_\Gamma. \end{equation} Moreover, \begin{equation} \det(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma)=-1, \qquad |\det(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma)|=1. \end{equation} Consequently, for the Gaussian density \(\varphi_\Gamma\), \begin{equation} \varphi_\Gamma(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w)=\varphi_\Gamma(w), \qquad w\in\mathbb R^d . \end{equation} Furthermore, \begin{equation} \lambda_r(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w) = -\lambda_r(w), \qquad w\in\mathbb R^d, \end{equation} and hence, for every \(m>0\) and \(w\in A_r^m\) \begin{equation} w\in A_r^m\Longleftrightarrow \mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\in A_r^m. \end{equation} Finally, for every \(u\in\mathbb R^d\), \begin{equation} r+\mathcal R_r^\Gamma u = \mathcal R_r^\Gamma(u-r). \end{equation}
nodes.label: reflprop

nodes.name: Reflection involution
nodes.statement: \mathcal R_r^\Gamma r=-r, \qquad \bigl(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma\bigr)^2=\mathbf I .
nodes.label: R1

nodes.name: Reflection preserves Gamma-norm
nodes.statement: \langle r,\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\rangle_\Gamma = -\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma,\qquad |\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w|_\Gamma=|w|_\Gamma.
nodes.label: R2

nodes.name: Determinant of reflection
nodes.statement: \det(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma)=-1, \qquad |\det(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma)|=1.
nodes.label: R3

nodes.name: Gaussian density reflection invariance
nodes.statement: \varphi_\Gamma(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w)=\varphi_\Gamma(w), \qquad w\in\mathbb R^d .
nodes.label: R4

nodes.name: Projection sign flip
nodes.statement: \lambda_r(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w) = -\lambda_r(w), \qquad w\in\mathbb R^d,
nodes.label: R5

nodes.name: Truncation set invariance
nodes.statement: w\in A_r^m\Longleftrightarrow \mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\in A_r^m.
nodes.label: R6

nodes.name: Reflection shift identity
nodes.statement: r+\mathcal R_r^\Gamma u = \mathcal R_r^\Gamma(u-r).
nodes.label: R7

nodes.name: Proof of Properties of the Gamma^{-1}-reflection
nodes.statement: By the definition of \(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma\), \(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma r = -r\). Also, \[ \begin{aligned} \langle r,\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\rangle_\Gamma = \left\langle r, w-2\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2}r \right\rangle_\Gamma = \langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma - 2\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2} \langle r,r\rangle_\Gamma = -\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma . \end{aligned} \] Applying this identity once more gives \[\bigl(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma\bigr)^2w= \mathcal R_r^\Gamma w-2\frac{\langle r,\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2}r =w-2\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2}r+ 2\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2}r=w.\] Hence \eqref{R1} follows. Next, \[|\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w|_\Gamma^2 =\left|w-2\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2}r\right|_\Gamma^2 =|w|_\Gamma^2-4\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma^2}{|r|_\Gamma^2} +4\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma^2}{|r|_\Gamma^2}=|w|_\Gamma^2 .\] This proves \eqref{R2}. Since \[\det(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma) =1-2\frac{r^{\mathrm T}\Gamma^{-1}r}{|r|_\Gamma^2}=-1,\] \eqref{R3} holds. By the definition of \(\varphi_\Gamma(w)\), \eqref{R3} immediately implies \eqref{R4}. By the definition of \(\lambda_r\) and \eqref{R2}, \[\lambda_r(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w) =\frac{|r|}{|r|_\Gamma^2}\langle r,\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\rangle_\Gamma =-\frac{|r|}{|r|_\Gamma^2}\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma =-\lambda_r(w).\] This proves \eqref{R5}, which implies \eqref{R6}. Finally, \eqref{R1} immediately implies \eqref{R7}. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Direct algebraic verification from the definition of the $\Gamma^{-1}$-reflection.

nodes.name: Involution property
nodes.statement: By the definition of \(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma\), \(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma r = -r\).
