Also, \[ \begin{aligned} \langle r,\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\rangle_\Gamma = \left\langle r, w-2\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2}r \right\rangle_\Gamma = \langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma - 2\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2} \langle r,r\rangle_\Gamma = -\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma . \end{aligned} \] Applying this identity once more gives \[\bigl(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma\bigr)^2w= \mathcal R_r^\Gamma w-2\frac{\langle r,\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2}r =w-2\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2}r+ 2\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2}r=w.\] Hence \eqref{R1} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\langle r,\mathcal R w\rangle_\Gamma=-\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma$ and deduce $\mathcal R^2=I$.

nodes.name: Norm preservation
nodes.statement: Next, \[|\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w|_\Gamma^2 =\left|w-2\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma}{|r|_\Gamma^2}r\right|_\Gamma^2 =|w|_\Gamma^2-4\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma^2}{|r|_\Gamma^2} +4\frac{\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma^2}{|r|_\Gamma^2}=|w|_\Gamma^2 .\] This proves \eqref{R2}.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $|\mathcal R w|_\Gamma^2$ to get norm preservation.

nodes.name: Determinant and density invariance
nodes.statement: Since \[\det(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma) =1-2\frac{r^{\mathrm T}\Gamma^{-1}r}{|r|_\Gamma^2}=-1,\] \eqref{R3} holds. By the definition of \(\varphi_\Gamma(w)\), \eqref{R3} immediately implies \eqref{R4}.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the determinant and deduce invariance of the Gaussian density.

nodes.name: Projection sign flip
nodes.statement: By the definition of \(\lambda_r\) and \eqref{R2}, \[\lambda_r(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w) =\frac{|r|}{|r|_\Gamma^2}\langle r,\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\rangle_\Gamma =-\frac{|r|}{|r|_\Gamma^2}\langle r,w\rangle_\Gamma =-\lambda_r(w).\] This proves \eqref{R5}, which implies \eqref{R6}.
nodes.statement_short: Use (R2) to show $\lambda_r$ changes sign, hence the truncation set is invariant.

nodes.name: Shift identity
nodes.statement: Finally, \eqref{R1} immediately implies \eqref{R7}. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Deduce (R7) from (R1).

nodes.name: Geometric interpretation of the Gamma^{-1}-reflection
nodes.statement: For a fixed nonzero vector \(r\), the \(\Gamma^{-1}\)-reflection \(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w\) is the reflection with respect to the hyperplane \(H_\Gamma = \{x\in \mathbb{R}^d:\langle r,x\rangle_\Gamma=0\}\). In other words, the reflecting hyperplane is determined by the notion of orthogonality induced by the \(\Gamma^{-1}\)-inner product. In the example shown in Figure~\ref{sigma-ref}, we take \( r=(1,1)^{\mathrm T}, w=(2,1)^{\mathrm T}\). When \(\Gamma=I\), the \(\Gamma^{-1}\)-inner product \(\langle \cdot, \cdot\rangle_\Gamma\) is the usual Euclidean inner product. Hence the reflecting hyperplane is \(H_{\mathbf I}=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1+x_2=0\}\). Thus \(\mathcal R_r^{\mathbf I}\) maps the point \(w\) to \(\mathcal R_r^{\mathbf I} w=(-1,-2)^{\mathrm T}\). The corresponding unit ball is \(\{x = (x_1, x_2):|x|_{\mathbf I}\leqslant 1\} = \{(x_1,x_2):x_1^2+x_2^2\leqslant 1\}\), whose boundary is the usual unit circle. By contrast, when \(\Gamma=\operatorname{diag}(4,1)\), distances, angles, and orthogonality are changed by \(\Gamma^{-1}\), rather than the standard dot product. The reflecting hyperplane becomes \(H_\Gamma = \{(x_1,x_2): x_1/4+x_2=0\}\). Therefore the same point \(w\) is reflected to a different point, \(\mathcal R_r^\Gamma w =(-2/5,-7/5)\). In this geometry, the unit ball is \(\{x=(x_1, x_2):|x|_\Gamma\leqslant 1\} = \{(x_1, x_2):x_1^2/4+x_2^2\leqslant 1\}\). So its boundary is an ellipse rather than a circle. Thus, as illustrated in Figure~\ref{sigma-ref}, the difference between the two cases is that when \(\Gamma=I\), reflection is the usual Euclidean mirror reflection, whereas when \(\Gamma\neq I\), the mirror hyperplane, the unit ball, and the reflected point are all determined by the weighted geometry induced by \(\Gamma^{-1}\).
nodes.statement_short: The $\Gamma^{-1}$-reflection mirrors across the $\Gamma^{-1}$-orthogonal hyperplane, illustrated for $\Gamma=I$ and $\Gamma=\operatorname{diag}(4,1)$.

nodes.name: Coupling property of the one-step reflection coupling
nodes.statement: For every \(h, m>0\) and \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d\), the joint distribution of the random vector \((\hat X_h(x,Z),\hat Y_h(x,y,Z))\) defined by \eqref{hY} is a coupling of the laws of \(\hat X_h(x,Z)\) and \(\hat X_h(y,Z)\).
conclusions: the joint distribution of the random vector \((\hat X_h(x,Z),\hat Y_h(x,y,Z))\) defined by \eqref{hY} is a coupling of the laws of \(\hat X_h(x,Z)\) and \(\hat X_h(y,Z)\).
nodes.label: coup

nodes.name: Proof of Coupling property of the one-step reflection coupling
nodes.statement: We need to show that \[\mathcal L(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z))=\mathcal L(u_h(y)+\Sigma Z).\] We write $\hat{r}_h = \hat{r}_h(x, y)$ and $|\hat{r}_h| = |\hat{r}_h(x, y)|$ for short. If \(\hat r_h=\mathbf 0\) or \(|\hat r_h|>2R\), then by construction of \(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z)\), the conclusion is immediate. Assume therefore that \(\hat r_h\neq\mathbf 0\) and \(|\hat r_h|\leqslant 2R\).Let \(g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be bounded and measurable. We write $\hat{r}_h = \hat{r}_h(x, y)$ and $|\hat{r}_h| = |\hat{r}_h(x, y)|$ for short. According to the definition of $\hat{Y}_h(x, y, Z)$ given in (\ref{hY}) and using the independence of \(\zeta\), we immediately get \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb E g(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z)) &= \int_{(A_{\hat r_h}^m)^c} g(u_h(y)+w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw + \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} g(u_h(x)+w) v_{\hat r_h}^m(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw \\ &\quad+ \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} g\bigl( u_h(y)+\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma w \bigr) \bigl(1-v_{\hat r_h}^m(w)\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw . \end{aligned} \] By the definitions of \(u_h(x)\) and \(v_{\hat r_h}^m\), \[v_{\hat r_h}^m(w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)= \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr] \wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr],\] we obtain \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E g(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z)) \\ =&\int_{(A_{\hat r_h}^m)^c} g(u_h(y)+w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw \\ &+\int_{\mathbb R^d} g\bigl(u_h(y)+\hat r_h+w\bigr) \Bigl(\bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr] \wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr)\,\mathrm dw \\ &+ \int_{\mathbb R^d} g\bigl(u_h(y)+\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma w\bigr) \Bigl(\mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w)-\Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr]\wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr) \Bigr)\,\mathrm dw . \end{aligned} \] In the second integral, use \(s=\hat r_h+w\), which gives \[\begin{aligned} &\int_{\mathbb R^d} g\bigl(u_h(y)+\hat r_h+w\bigr)\Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr]\wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr)\,\mathrm dw \\ =& \int_{\mathbb R^d} g(u_h(y)+s)\Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(s-\hat r_h\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(s-\hat r_h\bigr) \bigr]\wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(s) \varphi_\Gamma(s) \bigr] \Bigr)\,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned}\] In the third integral, use \(v=\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma w\). By \eqref{R3}, the Jacobian is one. By \eqref{R4} and \eqref{R6}, \[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v\bigr) = \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(v)\varphi_\Gamma(v). \] Moreover, by \eqref{R7}, \eqref{R4}, and \eqref{R6}, \[\mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl( \hat r_h+ \mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v \bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl( \hat r_h+ \mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v \bigr) = \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr).\] Therefore the third integral becomes \[\int_{\mathbb R^d} g(u_h(y)+v) \Bigl( \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(v)\varphi_\Gamma(v) - \Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(v) \varphi_\Gamma(v) \bigr] \wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr) \Bigr) \,\mathrm dv.\] Hence we obtain \[\mathbb E g(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z))= \int_{(A_{\hat r_h}^m)^c} g(u_h(y)+w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw + \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} g(u_h(y)+v)\varphi_\Gamma(v)\,\mathrm dv = \mathbb E g(u_h(y)+\Sigma Z).\] Since this holds for every bounded measurable \(g\), \[\mathcal L(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z))=\mathcal L(u_h(y)+\Sigma Z)=\mathcal L(\hat X_h(y,Z)).\] The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Test against bounded functions and change variables in the coalescing and reflected parts using the reflection properties.

nodes.name: Reduce to the second marginal; trivial cases
nodes.statement: We need to show that \[\mathcal L(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z))=\mathcal L(u_h(y)+\Sigma Z).\] We write $\hat{r}_h = \hat{r}_h(x, y)$ and $|\hat{r}_h| = |\hat{r}_h(x, y)|$ for short. If \(\hat r_h=\mathbf 0\) or \(|\hat r_h|>2R\), then by construction of \(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z)\), the conclusion is immediate.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to identify the law of $\hat Y_h$; the synchronous cases are immediate.

nodes.name: Reflection case
nodes.statement: Assume therefore that \(\hat r_h\neq\mathbf 0\) and \(|\hat r_h|\leqslant 2R\).Let \(g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be bounded and measurable. We write $\hat{r}_h = \hat{r}_h(x, y)$ and $|\hat{r}_h| = |\hat{r}_h(x, y)|$ for short. According to the definition of $\hat{Y}_h(x, y, Z)$ given in (\ref{hY}) and using the independence of \(\zeta\), we immediately get \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb E g(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z)) &= \int_{(A_{\hat r_h}^m)^c} g(u_h(y)+w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw + \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} g(u_h(x)+w) v_{\hat r_h}^m(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw \\ &\quad+ \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} g\bigl( u_h(y)+\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma w \bigr) \bigl(1-v_{\hat r_h}^m(w)\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw . \end{aligned} \] By the definitions of \(u_h(x)\) and \(v_{\hat r_h}^m\), \[v_{\hat r_h}^m(w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)= \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr] \wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr],\] we obtain \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E g(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z)) \\ =&\int_{(A_{\hat r_h}^m)^c} g(u_h(y)+w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw \\ &+\int_{\mathbb R^d} g\bigl(u_h(y)+\hat r_h+w\bigr) \Bigl(\bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr] \wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr)\,\mathrm dw \\ &+ \int_{\mathbb R^d} g\bigl(u_h(y)+\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma w\bigr) \Bigl(\mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w)-\Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr]\wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr) \Bigr)\,\mathrm dw . \end{aligned} \] In the second integral, use \(s=\hat r_h+w\), which gives \[\begin{aligned} &\int_{\mathbb R^d} g\bigl(u_h(y)+\hat r_h+w\bigr)\Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr]\wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr)\,\mathrm dw \\ =& \int_{\mathbb R^d} g(u_h(y)+s)\Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(s-\hat r_h\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(s-\hat r_h\bigr) \bigr]\wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(s) \varphi_\Gamma(s) \bigr] \Bigr)\,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned}\] In the third integral, use \(v=\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma w\). By \eqref{R3}, the Jacobian is one. By \eqref{R4} and \eqref{R6}, \[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v\bigr) = \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(v)\varphi_\Gamma(v). \] Moreover, by \eqref{R7}, \eqref{R4}, and \eqref{R6}, \[\mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl( \hat r_h+ \mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v \bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl( \hat r_h+ \mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v \bigr) = \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr).\] Therefore the third integral becomes \[\int_{\mathbb R^d} g(u_h(y)+v) \Bigl( \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(v)\varphi_\Gamma(v) - \Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(v) \varphi_\Gamma(v) \bigr] \wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr) \Bigr) \,\mathrm dv.\] Hence we obtain \[\mathbb E g(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z))= \int_{(A_{\hat r_h}^m)^c} g(u_h(y)+w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw + \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} g(u_h(y)+v)\varphi_\Gamma(v)\,\mathrm dv = \mathbb E g(u_h(y)+\Sigma Z).\] Since this holds for every bounded measurable \(g\), \[\mathcal L(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z))=\mathcal L(u_h(y)+\Sigma Z)=\mathcal L(\hat X_h(y,Z)).\] The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Split $\mathbb E g(\hat Y_h)$ into synchronous, coalescing and reflected parts and change variables in each.

nodes.name: Write the expectation as three integrals
nodes.statement: Assume therefore that \(\hat r_h\neq\mathbf 0\) and \(|\hat r_h|\leqslant 2R\).Let \(g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be bounded and measurable. We write $\hat{r}_h = \hat{r}_h(x, y)$ and $|\hat{r}_h| = |\hat{r}_h(x, y)|$ for short. According to the definition of $\hat{Y}_h(x, y, Z)$ given in (\ref{hY}) and using the independence of \(\zeta\), we immediately get \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb E g(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z)) &= \int_{(A_{\hat r_h}^m)^c} g(u_h(y)+w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw + \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} g(u_h(x)+w) v_{\hat r_h}^m(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw \\ &\quad+ \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} g\bigl( u_h(y)+\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma w \bigr) \bigl(1-v_{\hat r_h}^m(w)\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw . \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: Express $\mathbb E g(\hat Y_h)$ through the three branches of the coupling.

nodes.name: Rewrite with the minimum of densities
nodes.statement: By the definitions of \(u_h(x)\) and \(v_{\hat r_h}^m\), \[v_{\hat r_h}^m(w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)= \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr] \wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr],\] we obtain \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E g(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z)) \\ =&\int_{(A_{\hat r_h}^m)^c} g(u_h(y)+w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw \\ &+\int_{\mathbb R^d} g\bigl(u_h(y)+\hat r_h+w\bigr) \Bigl(\bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr] \wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h(x,y)}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr)\,\mathrm dw \\ &+ \int_{\mathbb R^d} g\bigl(u_h(y)+\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma w\bigr) \Bigl(\mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w)-\Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr]\wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr) \Bigr)\,\mathrm dw . \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the weights as minima of the two shifted truncated densities.

nodes.name: Shift substitution
nodes.statement: In the second integral, use \(s=\hat r_h+w\), which gives \[\begin{aligned} &\int_{\mathbb R^d} g\bigl(u_h(y)+\hat r_h+w\bigr)\Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w) \bigr]\wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr)\,\mathrm dw \\ =& \int_{\mathbb R^d} g(u_h(y)+s)\Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(s-\hat r_h\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma\bigl(s-\hat r_h\bigr) \bigr]\wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(s) \varphi_\Gamma(s) \bigr] \Bigr)\,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned}\]
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $s=\hat r_h+w$ in the coalescing part.

nodes.name: Reflection substitution
nodes.statement: In the third integral, use \(v=\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma w\). By \eqref{R3}, the Jacobian is one. By \eqref{R4} and \eqref{R6}, \[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v\bigr) = \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(v)\varphi_\Gamma(v). \] Moreover, by \eqref{R7}, \eqref{R4}, and \eqref{R6}, \[\mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl( \hat r_h+ \mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v \bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl( \hat r_h+ \mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma v \bigr) = \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr).\] Therefore the third integral becomes \[\int_{\mathbb R^d} g(u_h(y)+v) \Bigl( \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(v)\varphi_\Gamma(v) - \Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(v) \varphi_\Gamma(v) \bigr] \wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(v-\hat r_h\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr) \Bigr) \,\mathrm dv.\]
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $v=\mathcal R w$ using the reflection properties (R3), (R4), (R6), (R7).

nodes.name: Recombine the integrals
nodes.statement: Hence we obtain \[\mathbb E g(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z))= \int_{(A_{\hat r_h}^m)^c} g(u_h(y)+w)\varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw + \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} g(u_h(y)+v)\varphi_\Gamma(v)\,\mathrm dv = \mathbb E g(u_h(y)+\Sigma Z).\] Since this holds for every bounded measurable \(g\), \[\mathcal L(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z))=\mathcal L(u_h(y)+\Sigma Z)=\mathcal L(\hat X_h(y,Z)).\] The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: The pieces recombine to $\mathbb E g(u_h(y)+\Sigma Z)$.

nodes.name: Reason the reflected noise keeps its law
nodes.statement: The proof of Lemma \ref{coup} relies on the orthogonality of the reflection operator and the invariance of the Gaussian law \(N(0, h\Gamma)\) under the \(\Gamma^{-1}\)-reflection. This is why the reflected noise \(R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma \Sigma Z\) has the same distribution as \(\Sigma Z\).

nodes.name: Comparison with the reflection coupling of Majka, Mijatovic and Szpruch
nodes.statement: The coupling constructed above is intrinsically discrete in time and is adapted to the one-step transition kernel of the TEM scheme. It is therefore not obtained by directly transferring a continuous-time reflection coupling to the numerical level. Instead, the coupling is applied after the nonlinear one-step map \(x\mapsto u_h(x)=\pi_h(x)+h b(\pi_h(x))\) has been performed. This point is important for the present analysis, because both the projection \(\pi_h\) and the nonlinear drift \(b\) enter the transition mechanism of the scheme. In this respect, the construction is specifically designed for discretizations of nonlinear SDEs, rather than for the standard Euler--Maruyama transition. The construction is also distinct from the reflection-type coupling developed in \cite{Majka}, which is formulated in a linear discrete-time setting with a scalar constant diffusion coefficient. That framework provides an important prototype for discrete reflection couplings with noise truncation. In contrast, the present coupling is adapted to the nonlinear one-step map of the TEM scheme and allows for a general non-degenerate constant diffusion matrix. In particular, the noise covariance is \(h\Gamma\), where \(\Gamma=\Sigma\Sigma^{\mathrm T}>0\), and the reflection is taken with respect to the \(\Gamma^{-1}\)-geometry. The relevant reflection direction and projection are therefore determined by the metric induced by \(\Gamma^{-1}\), rather than by the Euclidean geometry associated with a scalar or isotropic diffusion coefficient. This matrix-valued setting is essential for preserving the Gaussian marginal law under reflection. Moreover, while the truncation in \cite{Majka} is imposed on the magnitude of the full noise increment, here the truncation acts only on the component of \(\Sigma Z\) along the one-step separation direction, namely on \(|\lambda_{\hat r_h}(\Sigma Z)|\). The directional truncation has two advantages for the subsequent estimates. First, it is more local to the coupling mechanism, since the Euclidean distance between the two coupled components depends only on the noise projected along \(\hat r_h\). Secondly, it reduces the key estimates to one-dimensional Gaussian integrals along this coupling direction, while the full noise remains \(d\)-dimensional and has covariance \(h\Gamma\). This feature is particularly useful in high-dimensional settings and in the analysis of nonlinear projected numerical schemes.
nodes.statement_short: The coupling is built on the nonlinear TEM map, uses $\Gamma^{-1}$-geometry for matrix noise, and truncates noise only along the separation direction.

nodes.name: First-moment identity of the coupling
nodes.statement: For any $h, m>0$ and $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$, the coupling $(\hat{X}_h(x,Z), \hat{Y}_h(x, y,Z))$ defined by (\ref{hY}) satisfies $\mathbb{E}|\hat{X}_h(x,Z)-\hat{Y}_h(x, y,Z)| = |u_h(x)-u_h(y)|$.
nodes.statement_short: The coupling preserves the expected distance: $\mathbb E|\hat X_h-\hat Y_h|=|u_h(x)-u_h(y)|$.
nodes.label: 1mom

nodes.name: Proof of First-moment identity of the coupling
nodes.statement: For simplicity, we define \(\hat{R}_h(x, y):=\hat{X}_h(x, Z)-\hat{Y}_h(x, y,Z)\). For short, we write $\hat{R}_h = \hat{R}_h(x, y)$ and $|\hat{R}_h| = |\hat{R}_h(x, y)|$. If \(\hat r_h=\mathbf 0\) or \(|\hat r_h|>2R\), then the construction is synchronous. Hence \(\mathbb E|\hat{R}_h|=|\hat r_h|\). It remains to consider the case \(\hat r_h\neq\mathbf 0\) and \(|\hat r_h|\leqslant 2R\). On the event \[\left\{\zeta\leqslant v_{\hat r_h}^m(\Sigma Z), \ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h}^m\right\},\] the two components coincide, and hence \(|\hat{R}_h|=0\). On the event \[\left\{\zeta >v_{\hat r_h}^m(\Sigma Z),\ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h}^m \right\},\] we have \[\hat{R}_h =\hat r_h+\Sigma Z-\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma\Sigma Z= \left(1+2\frac{\langle \hat r_h,\Sigma Z\rangle_\Gamma}{ |\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}\right)\hat r_h.\] Therefore \begin{equation} |\hat{R}_h|=\left| |\hat r_h|+2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(\Sigma Z)\right|. \end{equation} On the event \(\{\Sigma Z\notin A_{\hat r_h}^m\}\), the coupling is synchronous and \(|\hat{R}_h| =|\hat r_h|\). Therefore, we get \[\mathbb E|\hat{R}_h|= \int_{(A_{\hat r_h}^m)^c} |\hat r_h|\varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw+ \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \left| |\hat r_h(x,y)| + 2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w) \right| \left( 1-v_{\hat r_h}^m(w) \right) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw .\] Subtracting \(|\hat r_h|\) from both sides gives \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb E|\hat{R}_h| -|\hat r_h|&= \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \left( \left| |\hat r_h| + 2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w) \right| - |\hat r_h| \right) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw- \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \left| |\hat r_h| + 2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w) \right| v_{\hat r_h}^m(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw . \end{aligned} \] Since \(\Sigma Z\sim N(\mathbf 0,h\Gamma)\), \(\lambda_{\hat r_h}(\Sigma Z) \sim N\left( 0, h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2 \right)\). Moreover, \(\lambda_{\hat r_h} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) = |\hat r_h| + \lambda_{\hat r_h}(w)\), and \[\frac{\varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr)}{\varphi_\Gamma(w)}= \frac{p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w) \bigr)}{p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w)\bigr)},\] where \(p_{0,\tau^2}\) denotes the density of \(N(0,\tau^2)\). Therefore the \(d\)-dimensional integral can be evaluated with respect to this one-dimensional Gaussian law, and we obtain \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E|\hat{R}_h| -|\hat r_h|\\ =& \int_{\mathbb{R}} \left( \left| |\hat r_h|+2s \right| - |\hat r_h| \right)1_{[-m,m]} p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds \\ &- \int_{\mathbb R} \left| |\hat r_h|+2s \right|\Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \bigr]\wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr) \,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned} \] The density \(p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}\) is even and decreasing on \([0,\infty)\). Hence \[p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) \leqslant p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s)\Longleftrightarrow s\geqslant -\frac{|\hat r_h|}{2}.\] It follows that the minimum in the last display equals \[ \begin{cases} \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s), & s<-\dfrac{|\hat r_h|}{2},\\[2mm] \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}\bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr), & s\geqslant -\dfrac{|\hat r_h|}{2}. \end{cases} \] Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E|\hat{R}_h| -|\hat r_h| \\ =& - |\hat r_h| \int_{-\infty}^{-|\hat r_h|/2} \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds+ 2 \int_{-|\hat r_h|/2}^{\infty} s\,\mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds\\ &- \int_{-|\hat r_h|/2}^{\infty} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+2s\bigr) \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) \,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned} \] In the last integral, set \(u=|\hat r_h|+s\). Then \[ \begin{aligned} &\int_{-|\hat r_h|/2}^{\infty} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+2s\bigr) \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) \,\mathrm ds \\ =& \int_{|\hat r_h|/2}^{\infty} \bigl(2u-|\hat r_h|\bigr) \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(u) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(u) \,\mathrm du . \end{aligned} \] Hence, we obtain \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb E|\hat{R}_h| -|\hat r_h| =& 2 \int_{-|\hat r_h|/2}^{|\hat r_h|/2} s\,\mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds+ |\hat r_h| \int_{|\hat r_h|/2}^{\infty} \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds \\ &- |\hat r_h| \int_{-\infty}^{-|\hat r_h|/2} \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned} \] The first integral vanishes because the integrand is odd. The last two integrals cancel because both \(\mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s)\) and \(p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s)\) are even functions. Hence \(\mathbb E|\hat{R}_h| -|\hat r_h| = 0\). The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to one-dimensional Gaussian integrals along the separation direction and cancel by symmetry.

nodes.name: Introduce the coupling difference
nodes.statement: For simplicity, we define \(\hat{R}_h(x, y):=\hat{X}_h(x, Z)-\hat{Y}_h(x, y,Z)\). For short, we write $\hat{R}_h = \hat{R}_h(x, y)$ and $|\hat{R}_h| = |\hat{R}_h(x, y)|$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $\hat R_h=\hat X_h-\hat Y_h$.

nodes.name: Synchronous case
nodes.statement: If \(\hat r_h=\mathbf 0\) or \(|\hat r_h|>2R\), then the construction is synchronous. Hence \(\mathbb E|\hat{R}_h|=|\hat r_h|\).
nodes.statement_short: In the synchronous case $\mathbb E|\hat R_h|=|\hat r_h|$.

nodes.name: Reflection case: distance on each event
nodes.statement: It remains to consider the case \(\hat r_h\neq\mathbf 0\) and \(|\hat r_h|\leqslant 2R\). On the event \[\left\{\zeta\leqslant v_{\hat r_h}^m(\Sigma Z), \ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h}^m\right\},\] the two components coincide, and hence \(|\hat{R}_h|=0\). On the event \[\left\{\zeta >v_{\hat r_h}^m(\Sigma Z),\ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h}^m \right\},\] we have \[\hat{R}_h =\hat r_h+\Sigma Z-\mathcal R_{\hat r_h}^\Gamma\Sigma Z= \left(1+2\frac{\langle \hat r_h,\Sigma Z\rangle_\Gamma}{ |\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}\right)\hat r_h.\] Therefore \begin{equation} |\hat{R}_h|=\left| |\hat r_h|+2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(\Sigma Z)\right|. \end{equation} On the event \(\{\Sigma Z\notin A_{\hat r_h}^m\}\), the coupling is synchronous and \(|\hat{R}_h| =|\hat r_h|\).
nodes.statement_short: On the coalescing event the distance is 0, on the reflection event $||\hat r_h|+2\lambda(\Sigma Z)|$, otherwise $|\hat r_h|$.

nodes.name: Equation (40)
nodes.statement: |\hat{R}_h|=\left| |\hat r_h|+2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(\Sigma Z)\right|.
nodes.label: refR

nodes.name: Integral formula for the mean distance
nodes.statement: Therefore, we get \[\mathbb E|\hat{R}_h|= \int_{(A_{\hat r_h}^m)^c} |\hat r_h|\varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw+ \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \left| |\hat r_h(x,y)| + 2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w) \right| \left( 1-v_{\hat r_h}^m(w) \right) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw .\] Subtracting \(|\hat r_h|\) from both sides gives \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb E|\hat{R}_h| -|\hat r_h|&= \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \left( \left| |\hat r_h| + 2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w) \right| - |\hat r_h| \right) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw- \int_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \left| |\hat r_h| + 2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w) \right| v_{\hat r_h}^m(w) \varphi_\Gamma(w)\,\mathrm dw . \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: Write $\mathbb E|\hat R_h|-|\hat r_h|$ as integrals over the truncation set.

nodes.name: Reduce to a one-dimensional Gaussian
nodes.statement: Since \(\Sigma Z\sim N(\mathbf 0,h\Gamma)\), \(\lambda_{\hat r_h}(\Sigma Z) \sim N\left( 0, h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2 \right)\). Moreover, \(\lambda_{\hat r_h} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) = |\hat r_h| + \lambda_{\hat r_h}(w)\), and \[\frac{\varphi_\Gamma\bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr)}{\varphi_\Gamma(w)}= \frac{p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w) \bigr)}{p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w)\bigr)},\] where \(p_{0,\tau^2}\) denotes the density of \(N(0,\tau^2)\). Therefore the \(d\)-dimensional integral can be evaluated with respect to this one-dimensional Gaussian law, and we obtain \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E|\hat{R}_h| -|\hat r_h|\\ =& \int_{\mathbb{R}} \left( \left| |\hat r_h|+2s \right| - |\hat r_h| \right)1_{[-m,m]} p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds \\ &- \int_{\mathbb R} \left| |\hat r_h|+2s \right|\Bigl( \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \bigr]\wedge \bigl[ \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) \bigr] \Bigr) \,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: Project onto the separation direction to reduce to one-dimensional Gaussian integrals.

nodes.name: Identify the minimum of densities
nodes.statement: The density \(p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}\) is even and decreasing on \([0,\infty)\). Hence \[p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) \leqslant p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s)\Longleftrightarrow s\geqslant -\frac{|\hat r_h|}{2}.\] It follows that the minimum in the last display equals \[ \begin{cases} \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s), & s<-\dfrac{|\hat r_h|}{2},\\[2mm] \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}\bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr), & s\geqslant -\dfrac{|\hat r_h|}{2}. \end{cases} \] Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E|\hat{R}_h| -|\hat r_h| \\ =& - |\hat r_h| \int_{-\infty}^{-|\hat r_h|/2} \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds+ 2 \int_{-|\hat r_h|/2}^{\infty} s\,\mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds\\ &- \int_{-|\hat r_h|/2}^{\infty} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+2s\bigr) \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) \,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of the centred density identifies the minimum in the coalescing weight.

nodes.name: Change variables
nodes.statement: In the last integral, set \(u=|\hat r_h|+s\). Then \[ \begin{aligned} &\int_{-|\hat r_h|/2}^{\infty} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+2s\bigr) \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2} \bigl(|\hat r_h|+s\bigr) \,\mathrm ds \\ =& \int_{|\hat r_h|/2}^{\infty} \bigl(2u-|\hat r_h|\bigr) \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(u) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(u) \,\mathrm du . \end{aligned} \] Hence, we obtain \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb E|\hat{R}_h| -|\hat r_h| =& 2 \int_{-|\hat r_h|/2}^{|\hat r_h|/2} s\,\mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds+ |\hat r_h| \int_{|\hat r_h|/2}^{\infty} \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds \\ &- |\hat r_h| \int_{-\infty}^{-|\hat r_h|/2} \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: Shift the variable in the last integral.

nodes.name: Symmetry cancellation
nodes.statement: The first integral vanishes because the integrand is odd. The last two integrals cancel because both \(\mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s)\) and \(p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s)\) are even functions. Hence \(\mathbb E|\hat{R}_h| -|\hat r_h| = 0\). The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Odd and even symmetry make all terms cancel.

nodes.name: Distances r_h, hat r_h, hat R_h
nodes.statement: For any $h>0$ and $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$, we recall $|\hat{r}_h|$, $|\hat{R}_h|$ and define $|r_h|$ by \begin{subequations} \begin{align} |r_h|: &= |r_h(x, y)| = |\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y)|, \\ |\hat{r}_h|: &= |\hat{r}_h(x, y)| = |u_h(x)-u_h(y)|, \\ |\hat{R}_h|: &= |\hat{R}_h(x, y)| = |\hat{X}_h(x,Z)-\hat{Y}_h(x, y,Z)|. \end{align} \end{subequations}

nodes.name: Distance |hat R_h|
nodes.statement: |\hat{R}_h|: &= |\hat{R}_h(x, y)| = |\hat{X}_h(x,Z)-\hat{Y}_h(x, y,Z)|.
nodes.label: Natc

nodes.name: First-moment identity of the coupling
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}(|\hat{R}_h| - |r_h|) = |\hat{r}_h| - |r_h|.
nodes.label: cc1

nodes.name: Ellipticity constants vartheta_pm
nodes.statement: Let \(\vartheta_-:=\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma)}\) and \(\vartheta_+:=\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(\Gamma)}\).

nodes.name: Constant alpha_{1,Gamma}
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation} \alpha_{1, \Gamma} := \frac1{16} \left(1-\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{8\vartheta_+^2}\right\}\right)\inf_{\vartheta\in[\vartheta_-,\vartheta_+]}\int_{1/4}^{3/8}p_{0,\vartheta^2}(u)\,\mathrm du . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Constant alpha_1
nodes.statement: \alpha_{1, \Gamma} := \frac1{16} \left(1-\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{8\vartheta_+^2}\right\}\right)\inf_{\vartheta\in[\vartheta_-,\vartheta_+]}\int_{1/4}^{3/8}p_{0,\vartheta^2}(u)\,\mathrm du .
nodes.label: c0

nodes.name: Functions varphi and Phi
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation} \varphi (u) = \mathrm{exp}\left(-\frac{2L+1}{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\left(u^2+2u\right)\right), \quad\quad\Phi(u)= \int_0^u \varphi(s) \mathrm{d} s, \quad u\geqslant 0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Functions varphi and Phi
nodes.statement: \varphi (u) = \mathrm{exp}\left(-\frac{2L+1}{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\left(u^2+2u\right)\right), \quad\quad\Phi(u)= \int_0^u \varphi(s) \mathrm{d} s, \quad u\geqslant 0.
nodes.label: varphi

nodes.name: Constants r_1 and alpha_{2,Gamma}
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation} r_1 = 2R+16 ,~~~~ \alpha_{2, \Gamma}= \frac{1}{2}\left(\int_0^{r_1}\frac{\Phi(s+1)}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}\varphi(s)}\mathrm{d} s\right)^{-1}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Constants r_1 and alpha_2
nodes.statement: r_1 = 2R+16 ,~~~~ \alpha_{2, \Gamma}= \frac{1}{2}\left(\int_0^{r_1}\frac{\Phi(s+1)}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}\varphi(s)}\mathrm{d} s\right)^{-1}.
nodes.label: Ac

nodes.name: Bounds on alpha_2
nodes.statement: \frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}\varphi(r_1)}{2r_1(r_1+1)}\leqslant \frac{1}{2}\left(\int_0^{r_1}\frac{r_1+1}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}\varphi(r_1)}\mathrm{d} s\right)^{-1}\leqslant \alpha_{2, \Gamma}\leqslant \frac{1}{2}\left(\int_0^{r_1}\frac{\Phi(1)}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\mathrm{d} s\right)^{-1} = \frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}{2r_1\Phi(1)}.
nodes.label: dd6

nodes.name: Concave distance function f
nodes.statement: For any $u\geqslant 0$, we define \begin{equation} \rho(u) = 1- \alpha_{2, \Gamma}\int_0^u \frac{\Phi(s+1)}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}\varphi(s)}\mathrm{d} s, \quad f(u) = \int_0^u \varphi (s\wedge r_1)\rho(s\wedge r_1) \mathrm{d} s. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $f$ is a concave increasing distance built from $\varphi$ and the weight $\rho$, frozen beyond $r_1$.

nodes.name: Concave distance function f
nodes.statement: \rho(u) = 1- \alpha_{2, \Gamma}\int_0^u \frac{\Phi(s+1)}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}\varphi(s)}\mathrm{d} s, \quad f(u) = \int_0^u \varphi (s\wedge r_1)\rho(s\wedge r_1) \mathrm{d} s.
nodes.label: f

nodes.name: Two-sided bounds on f
nodes.statement: \frac{1}{2}\varphi(r_1)u\leqslant \frac{1}{2}\int_0^u\varphi(s\wedge r_1) \mathrm{d} s \leqslant f(u)\leqslant \Phi(u)\leqslant u, ~~~~\forall~ u\geqslant 0.
nodes.label: f1

nodes.name: Choice of the truncation parameter M
nodes.statement: To preserve the ergodicity of our numerical scheme, we select the suitable parameter $M$ satisfying \begin{equation} M \geqslant \max\left\{|b(\mathbf{0})|, \frac{\sqrt{\varphi(r_1)RK}}{8\sqrt{r_1}}, \frac{\sqrt{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}}{4\sqrt{2r_1\Phi(1)}}, 1\right\} \end{equation} in the truncation mapping $\pi_h$ defined by \eqref{TF}.

nodes.name: Lower bound condition on M
nodes.statement: M \geqslant \max\left\{|b(\mathbf{0})|, \frac{\sqrt{\varphi(r_1)RK}}{8\sqrt{r_1}}, \frac{\sqrt{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}}{4\sqrt{2r_1\Phi(1)}}, 1\right\}
nodes.label: M1

nodes.name: Simple sufficient condition for the choice of M
nodes.statement: It is worth noting that \(M\geqslant \max\left\{|b(\mathbf{0})|, \sqrt{K}, \sqrt{L+1}, 1\right\}\) implies that \eqref{M1} holds. In fact, noting that $\varphi(u)\leqslant 1$ for all $u>0$ and \eqref{Ac}, we know that \(\sqrt{\varphi(r_1)RK}/(8\sqrt{r_1})<\sqrt{K}\). By using inequality \(\mathrm{e}^{-u}\leqslant 1/(1+u)\) for all $u>0$, we have \begin{align*} \Phi(1) &= \int_0^1 \mathrm{exp}\left(-\frac{2L+1}{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\left(u^2+2u\right)\right)\mathrm{d} u\geqslant \int_0^1 \mathrm{exp}\left(-\frac{6L+3}{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}u\right)\mathrm{d} u> \frac{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}+6L+3}, \end{align*} which together with \eqref{c0} and \eqref{Ac} implies that \(\sqrt{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}/(4\sqrt{2r_1\Phi(1)}) < \sqrt{L+1}\). Then the desired assertion follows.

nodes.name: Constants alpha_{3,Gamma} and alpha_{4,Gamma}
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation} \alpha_{3,\Gamma} := \inf_{\vartheta\in[\vartheta_-,\vartheta_+]} \frac{5}{\vartheta^3\sqrt{2\pi}} \min\left\{ \mathrm e^{-1/(2\vartheta^2)}, 8\mathrm e^{-32/\vartheta^2} \right\} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \alpha_{4,\Gamma} := \inf_{\vartheta\in[\vartheta_-,\vartheta_+]} 4\vartheta^3 \left(1-\mathrm e^{-1/\vartheta^2}\right) \int_0^{1/(2\vartheta)} u^3p_{0,1}(u)\,\mathrm du . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Constant alpha_3
nodes.statement: \alpha_{3,\Gamma} := \inf_{\vartheta\in[\vartheta_-,\vartheta_+]} \frac{5}{\vartheta^3\sqrt{2\pi}} \min\left\{ \mathrm e^{-1/(2\vartheta^2)}, 8\mathrm e^{-32/\vartheta^2} \right\}
nodes.label: c1

nodes.name: Constant alpha_4
nodes.statement: \alpha_{4,\Gamma} := \inf_{\vartheta\in[\vartheta_-,\vartheta_+]} 4\vartheta^3 \left(1-\mathrm e^{-1/\vartheta^2}\right) \int_0^{1/(2\vartheta)} u^3p_{0,1}(u)\,\mathrm du .
nodes.label: c2

nodes.name: Step-size threshold h_0
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation*} h_0 = \min\left\{\left(KM^{-2}\right)^{1/(1-2\bar{\theta})}, K^{-1}, L^{-1}\right\}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Deterministic estimate of the drift-updated distance
nodes.statement: Let Assumption \ref{A} hold. Then, for any \(h\in(0,h_0)\), if \(|r_h|>R\), then \begin{equation} |\hat r_h|\leqslant |r_h|\left(1-\frac{hK}{2}\right). \end{equation} If, in addition, Assumption \ref{A1} holds, then for any \(h\in(0,h_0)\), whenever \(|r_h|\leqslant R\), one has \begin{equation} |\hat r_h|\leqslant 2R. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: One drift step contracts distances larger than $R$ by $1-hK/2$ and keeps distances at most $R$ below $2R$.
nodes.label: Le4.8

nodes.name: Contraction of hat r_h beyond R
nodes.statement: |\hat r_h|\leqslant |r_h|\left(1-\frac{hK}{2}\right).
nodes.label: Sub4eq1

nodes.name: Bound of hat r_h within R
nodes.statement: |\hat r_h|\leqslant 2R.
nodes.label: Sub4eq2

nodes.name: Proof of Deterministic estimate of the drift-updated distance
nodes.statement: For any $h\in(0, h_0)$, we have \begin{equation} M^2h^{2-2\theta}\leqslant M^2h^{2-2\bar{\theta}}\leqslant hK\leqslant 1,\quad \forall \theta\in(0, \bar{\theta}]\quad \text{and} \quad 1+2hL+M^2h^{2-2\theta}\leqslant 4. \end{equation} Using (\ref{GL}) one notices from the definition of $|\hat{r}_h|$ that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} |\hat{r}_h| &=\sqrt{|r_h|^2+\!2h\left\langle\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y), b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y))\right\rangle+h^2|b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y))|^2}\\ &\leqslant \sqrt{(1+M^2h^{2-2\theta})|r_h|^2+\!2h\left\langle\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y), b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y))\right\rangle }. \end{aligned} \end{equation} If $|r_h|>R$, by virtue of \eqref{CaI} and \eqref{cc2}, it follows from \eqref{eq+6} that \begin{equation*} |\hat{r}_h| \leqslant |r_h|\sqrt{1+M^2h^{2-2\theta}-2hK}\leqslant |r_h|\sqrt{1-hK}. \end{equation*} Then, this together with the fact $\sqrt{1+x}\leqslant 1+x/2$ for all $x\geqslant-1$ implies that \eqref{Sub4eq1} holds. On the other hand, if $|r_h|\leqslant R$, by virtue of (\ref{CaI}) and \eqref{cc2}, it follows from \eqref{eq+6} that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} |\hat{r}_h| \leqslant |r_h|\sqrt{1+M^2h^{2-2\theta}+2hL}\leqslant 2R. \end{aligned} \end{equation} The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the squared updated distance and use the truncated Lipschitz bound with dissipativity at infinity, case by case.

nodes.name: Step-size consequences
nodes.statement: For any $h\in(0, h_0)$, we have \begin{equation} M^2h^{2-2\theta}\leqslant M^2h^{2-2\bar{\theta}}\leqslant hK\leqslant 1,\quad \forall \theta\in(0, \bar{\theta}]\quad \text{and} \quad 1+2hL+M^2h^{2-2\theta}\leqslant 4. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Record the bounds on $h$ implied by $h<h_0$.

nodes.name: Equation (54)
nodes.statement: M^2h^{2-2\theta}\leqslant M^2h^{2-2\bar{\theta}}\leqslant hK\leqslant 1,\quad \forall \theta\in(0, \bar{\theta}]\quad \text{and} \quad 1+2hL+M^2h^{2-2\theta}\leqslant 4.
nodes.label: cc2

nodes.name: Expand the updated distance
nodes.statement: Using (\ref{GL}) one notices from the definition of $|\hat{r}_h|$ that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} |\hat{r}_h| &=\sqrt{|r_h|^2+\!2h\left\langle\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y), b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y))\right\rangle+h^2|b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y))|^2}\\ &\leqslant \sqrt{(1+M^2h^{2-2\theta})|r_h|^2+\!2h\left\langle\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y), b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y))\right\rangle }. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Expand $|\hat r_h|^2$ and use the truncated Lipschitz bound.

nodes.name: Equation (55)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} |\hat{r}_h| &=\sqrt{|r_h|^2+\!2h\left\langle\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y), b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y))\right\rangle+h^2|b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y))|^2}\\ &\leqslant \sqrt{(1+M^2h^{2-2\theta})|r_h|^2+\!2h\left\langle\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y), b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y))\right\rangle }. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq+6

nodes.name: Case |r_h| > R
nodes.statement: If $|r_h|>R$, by virtue of \eqref{CaI} and \eqref{cc2}, it follows from \eqref{eq+6} that \begin{equation*} |\hat{r}_h| \leqslant |r_h|\sqrt{1+M^2h^{2-2\theta}-2hK}\leqslant |r_h|\sqrt{1-hK}. \end{equation*} Then, this together with the fact $\sqrt{1+x}\leqslant 1+x/2$ for all $x\geqslant-1$ implies that \eqref{Sub4eq1} holds.
nodes.statement_short: Dissipativity at infinity gives contraction by $1-hK/2$.

nodes.name: Case |r_h| <= R
nodes.statement: On the other hand, if $|r_h|\leqslant R$, by virtue of (\ref{CaI}) and \eqref{cc2}, it follows from \eqref{eq+6} that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} |\hat{r}_h| \leqslant |r_h|\sqrt{1+M^2h^{2-2\theta}+2hL}\leqslant 2R. \end{aligned} \end{equation} The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: The one-sided Lipschitz bound gives $|\hat r_h|\le 2R$.

nodes.name: Equation (56)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} |\hat{r}_h| \leqslant |r_h|\sqrt{1+M^2h^{2-2\theta}+2hL}\leqslant 2R. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: ss

nodes.name: Global one-step contractivity of the coupling
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{A} and \ref{A1} hold. For any $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and \(h \in (0, \bar{h}]\), consider the coupling $(\hat{X}_h(x,Z), \hat{Y}_h(x,y,Z))$ defined by \eqref{hY}, with the parameter $m=8$. Then, we have \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)\leqslant (1-ch)f(|r_h|), \end{equation*} where $|r_h|, |\hat{R}_h|$ are defined in (\ref{eq3}), function $f$ is defined by \eqref{f}, the constant $\bar{h}$ is defined by \begin{equation} \bar{h}=\min\left\{h_0, \left(\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\alpha_{3, \Gamma}\Phi(1)}{8M\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\right)^{2/(1-2\bar{\theta})}, \left(\frac{r_1}{18}\right)^2, R^2, (4M)^{-2}, (4Mr_1)^{2/(2\bar{\theta}-1)}, M^{1/(2\bar{\theta}-1)}\right\}, \end{equation} and the contractive rate $c$ is given by \begin{equation*} c = \min\left\{M, \frac{\varphi(r_1)KR }{4r_1}, \frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\alpha_{4, \Gamma}\Phi(1)}{4\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}, \alpha_{2, \Gamma}\right\}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Under the concave distance $f$, the one-step coupling contracts: $\mathbb E f(|\hat R_h|)\le(1-ch)f(|r_h|)$ for small $h$.
nodes.label: Th1

nodes.name: Step-size bound bar h
nodes.statement: \bar{h}=\min\left\{h_0, \left(\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\alpha_{3, \Gamma}\Phi(1)}{8M\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\right)^{2/(1-2\bar{\theta})}, \left(\frac{r_1}{18}\right)^2, R^2, (4M)^{-2}, (4Mr_1)^{2/(2\bar{\theta}-1)}, M^{1/(2\bar{\theta}-1)}\right\},
nodes.label: bar

nodes.name: Proof outline of Global one-step contractivity of the coupling
nodes.statement: Because the proof of Theorem \ref{Th1} is rather technical, we begin by outlining its structure; see Figure \ref{Figtu} for a roadmap. The proof is built on two main preparatory ingredients: the construction of a suitable concave distance function \(f\), and the one-step coupling estimate given in Lemma \ref{1mom}. With these tools in hand, we divide the argument according to the size of the current distance \(|r_h|\). More precisely, we consider three cases: \(0<|r_h|\leqslant \sqrt h\), \(\sqrt h<|r_h|\leqslant r_1\), and \(|r_h|>r_1\). The first and third cases are treated in Propositions \ref{PR1} and \ref{PR5}, respectively. The intermediate regime \(\sqrt h<|r_h|\leqslant r_1\) is the most delicate one, and it is further split according to the size of the one-step updated distance \(|\widehat r_h|\), which leads to three subcases handled separately in the proof of Proposition \ref{PR4}. More specifically, the subcases \(|\widehat r_h|\leqslant \sqrt h\) and \(\sqrt h<|\widehat r_h|\leqslant 2R\) are treated via Propositions \ref{PR2} and \ref{PR3}, while the case \(|\widehat r_h|>2R\) is controlled by synchronous coupling together with inequality \eqref{I-3}. Since these three propositions cover all possible values of \(|r_h|\), their combination yields the desired estimate in Theorem \ref{Th1}.
nodes.statement_short: Roadmap: split by the size of $|r_h|$ into three cases handled by Propositions 1, 2 and 5, with case 2 split further by $|\hat r_h|$.

nodes.name: Ingredients
nodes.statement: Because the proof of Theorem \ref{Th1} is rather technical, we begin by outlining its structure; see Figure \ref{Figtu} for a roadmap. The proof is built on two main preparatory ingredients: the construction of a suitable concave distance function \(f\), and the one-step coupling estimate given in Lemma \ref{1mom}.
nodes.statement_short: The proof rests on the concave distance $f$ and the first-moment identity.

nodes.name: Three distance regimes
nodes.statement: With these tools in hand, we divide the argument according to the size of the current distance \(|r_h|\). More precisely, we consider three cases: \(0<|r_h|\leqslant \sqrt h\), \(\sqrt h<|r_h|\leqslant r_1\), and \(|r_h|>r_1\). The first and third cases are treated in Propositions \ref{PR1} and \ref{PR5}, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Split according to the size of $|r_h|$.

nodes.name: Subcases of the intermediate regime
nodes.statement: The intermediate regime \(\sqrt h<|r_h|\leqslant r_1\) is the most delicate one, and it is further split according to the size of the one-step updated distance \(|\widehat r_h|\), which leads to three subcases handled separately in the proof of Proposition \ref{PR4}. More specifically, the subcases \(|\widehat r_h|\leqslant \sqrt h\) and \(\sqrt h<|\widehat r_h|\leqslant 2R\) are treated via Propositions \ref{PR2} and \ref{PR3}, while the case \(|\widehat r_h|>2R\) is controlled by synchronous coupling together with inequality \eqref{I-3}.
nodes.statement_short: Split Case 2 by the size of $|\hat r_h|$.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Since these three propositions cover all possible values of \(|r_h|\), their combination yields the desired estimate in Theorem \ref{Th1}.
nodes.statement_short: The cases cover all distances.

nodes.name: Second-moment lower bound for small distances
nodes.statement: Let Assumption \ref{A} hold. For any \(x,y\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(h\in(0,M^{-2}]\), the coupling \((\hat X_h(x,Z),\hat Y_h(x,y,Z))\) defined by \eqref{hY} has the property that \[\mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\geqslant \alpha_{3,\Gamma} |\hat r_h|\sqrt h\, \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|),\] where $|r_h|, |\hat{r}_h|, |\hat{R}_h|$ are defined in \eqref{eq3} and $\alpha_{3, \Gamma}$ is defined by \eqref{c1}.
nodes.statement_short: For $|r_h|\le\sqrt h$ the reflection part creates a second-moment spread of order $|\hat r_h|\sqrt h$.
conclusions: \[\mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\geqslant \alpha_{3,\Gamma} |\hat r_h|\sqrt h\, \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|),\]
nodes.label: Le9

nodes.name: Proof of Second-moment lower bound for small distances
nodes.statement: If \(\hat r_h=\mathbf 0\), then both sides are zero, and there is nothing to prove. We therefore assume that \(\hat r_h\neq \mathbf 0\). Since on the event \(|\hat R_h|\in(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)\), one has \((|\hat R_h|-|r_h|)^2\geqslant h\), we get \begin{equation} \mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\geqslant h\, \mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]. \end{equation} It is enough to estimate from below the probability on the right-hand side coming from the reflection part of the coupling. On the reflection event, by \eqref{refR}, \(|\hat R_h| = \left| |\hat r_h| + 2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(\Sigma Z) \right|\). By the definition of \(v_{\hat r_h}^m\), we obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right] \\ \geqslant& \int_{\mathbb R^d} \left( \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w)\varphi_\Gamma(w) - \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \right)^+ \\ &\qquad\qquad\times \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} \left( \left| |\hat r_h| + 2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w) \right| \right) \,\mathrm dw . \end{aligned} \end{equation} Since \(\lambda_{\hat r_h}(\Sigma Z) \sim N(0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2)\) and \(\lambda_{\hat r_h} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) = |\hat r_h|+\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w)\), the right-hand side of \eqref{matrix-J6} is bounded from below by \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\int_{\mathbb R} \Bigl( \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) - \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(|\hat r_h|+s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s) \Bigr)^+ \\ &\qquad\qquad\times \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} \bigl(|\,|\hat r_h|+2s\,|\bigr) \,\mathrm ds , \end{aligned} \end{equation} where \(p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}\) denotes the density of \(N(0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2)\). We now estimate a lower bound for the indicator function $\1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt{h}, |r_h|+17\sqrt{h})}\left(|\hat{r}_h|+2s\right)$ in \eqref{matrix-J6-one-dim}. Using (\ref{GL}), we have \begin{align*} |\hat{r}_h| = |\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y)+h(b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y)))|\leqslant (1+Mh^{1-\theta})|r_h|, \end{align*} and similarly \(|r_h|= |\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y)| \leqslant |\hat{r}_h|+Mh^{1-\theta}|r_h|\). Since \(h\in(0,M^{-2}]\) and \(M\geqslant 1\), this yields \begin{equation} \left||r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\right|\leqslant Mh^{1-\theta}|r_h|\leqslant M\sqrt{h}|r_h|\leqslant |r_h|. \end{equation} This implies that on the event \(\{|r_h|\in(0,\sqrt h]\}\), $$\frac{1}{2}\left(|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|+\sqrt{h}\right)\leqslant\sqrt{h}, \qquad \frac{1}{2}\left(|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|+17\sqrt{h}\right) \geqslant8\sqrt{h}.$$ Hence, on \(\{|r_h|\in(0,\sqrt h]\}\), \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} \bigl(|\,|\hat r_h|+2s\,|\bigr)\geqslant \mathbf 1_{(\sqrt h,\,8\sqrt h)}(s). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Using \eqref{matrix-indicator-lower} in \eqref{matrix-J6-one-dim}, and taking \(m=8\), we obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\geqslant& \int_{\sqrt h}^{8\sqrt h} \Bigl( p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) - p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s) \Bigr) \,\mathrm ds\\ &\qquad\qquad \times \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Here the positive part has been removed because, for \(s>0\), \(|\hat r_h|+s\geqslant s\), and the centered Gaussian density is decreasing on \([0,\infty)\). On \(\{|r_h|\in(0,\sqrt h]\}\), \eqref{rr} gives \(0\leqslant |\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}\leqslant2\). By the change of variables \(s=\sqrt h\,u\), \eqref{matrix-J6-lower1} yields \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right] \\ \geqslant& \frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma}{|\hat r_h|\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_1^8 \left[ \exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2u^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) - \exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2(u+|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h})^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) \right]\mathrm du \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{aligned} \end{equation*} Since \(0\leqslant |\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}\leqslant2\), the interval \((3-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h},8-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h})\) is contained in \((1,8)\). Therefore, \[ \begin{aligned} &\int_1^8 \left[ \exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2u^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) - \exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2(u+|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h})^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) \right]\mathrm du\\ \geqslant& \int_{3-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}}^{8-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}} \int_u^{u+|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}} \frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2v}{|\hat r_h|^2} \exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2v^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) \,\mathrm dv\,\mathrm du . \end{aligned} \] For \(u\in(3-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h},8-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h})\) and \(v\in[u,u+|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}]\), we have \(v\in[1,8]\). Hence \[ v\exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2v^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) \geqslant \min\left\{ \mathrm e^{-|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2/(2|\hat r_h|^2)}, 8\mathrm e^{-32|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2/|\hat r_h|^2} \right\}. \] It follows that \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\\ \geqslant& \frac{5|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^3} {|\hat r_h|^2\sqrt{2\pi h}} \min\left\{ \mathrm e^{-|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2/(2|\hat r_h|^2)}, 8\mathrm e^{-32|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2/|\hat r_h|^2} \right\}\mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{aligned} \] By the definition of \(\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\), and since \(|\hat r_h|/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma\in[\vartheta_-,\vartheta_+]\), we obtain \begin{equation} \mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\geqslant \frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}|\hat r_h|}{\sqrt h} \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{equation} Combining \eqref{matrix-J6-start} and \eqref{matrix-J6-final}, we obtain the desired result. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound the event probability by the reflection branch, reduce to a one-dimensional Gaussian integral and bound the density difference uniformly.

nodes.name: Trivial case
nodes.statement: If \(\hat r_h=\mathbf 0\), then both sides are zero, and there is nothing to prove. We therefore assume that \(\hat r_h\neq \mathbf 0\).
nodes.statement_short: Dispose of $\hat r_h=0$.

nodes.name: Reduce to a probability bound
nodes.statement: Since on the event \(|\hat R_h|\in(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)\), one has \((|\hat R_h|-|r_h|)^2\geqslant h\), we get \begin{equation} \mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\geqslant h\, \mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: On the event the squared jump is at least $h$, so it suffices to bound its probability.

nodes.name: Equation (58)
nodes.statement: \mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\geqslant h\, \mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right].
nodes.label: matrix-J6-start

nodes.name: Restrict to the reflection part
nodes.statement: It is enough to estimate from below the probability on the right-hand side coming from the reflection part of the coupling. On the reflection event, by \eqref{refR}, \(|\hat R_h| = \left| |\hat r_h| + 2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(\Sigma Z) \right|\). By the definition of \(v_{\hat r_h}^m\), we obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right] \\ \geqslant& \int_{\mathbb R^d} \left( \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w)\varphi_\Gamma(w) - \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \right)^+ \\ &\qquad\qquad\times \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} \left( \left| |\hat r_h| + 2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w) \right| \right) \,\mathrm dw . \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound the probability by the reflection branch of the coupling.

nodes.name: Equation (59)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right] \\ \geqslant& \int_{\mathbb R^d} \left( \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m}(w)\varphi_\Gamma(w) - \mathbf 1_{A_{\hat r_h}^m} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \varphi_\Gamma \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) \right)^+ \\ &\qquad\qquad\times \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} \left( \left| |\hat r_h| + 2\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w) \right| \right) \,\mathrm dw . \end{aligned}
nodes.label: matrix-J6

nodes.name: One-dimensional reduction
nodes.statement: Since \(\lambda_{\hat r_h}(\Sigma Z) \sim N(0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2)\) and \(\lambda_{\hat r_h} \bigl(\hat r_h+w\bigr) = |\hat r_h|+\lambda_{\hat r_h}(w)\), the right-hand side of \eqref{matrix-J6} is bounded from below by \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\int_{\mathbb R} \Bigl( \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) - \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(|\hat r_h|+s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s) \Bigr)^+ \\ &\qquad\qquad\times \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} \bigl(|\,|\hat r_h|+2s\,|\bigr) \,\mathrm ds , \end{aligned} \end{equation} where \(p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}\) denotes the density of \(N(0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2)\).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a one-dimensional Gaussian integral along the separation direction.

nodes.name: Equation (60)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\int_{\mathbb R} \Bigl( \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) - \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(|\hat r_h|+s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s) \Bigr)^+ \\ &\qquad\qquad\times \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} \bigl(|\,|\hat r_h|+2s\,|\bigr) \,\mathrm ds , \end{aligned}
nodes.label: matrix-J6-one-dim

nodes.name: Lower bound for the indicator
nodes.statement: We now estimate a lower bound for the indicator function $\1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt{h}, |r_h|+17\sqrt{h})}\left(|\hat{r}_h|+2s\right)$ in \eqref{matrix-J6-one-dim}. Using (\ref{GL}), we have \begin{align*} |\hat{r}_h| = |\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y)+h(b(\pi_h(x))-b(\pi_h(y)))|\leqslant (1+Mh^{1-\theta})|r_h|, \end{align*} and similarly \(|r_h|= |\pi_h(x)-\pi_h(y)| \leqslant |\hat{r}_h|+Mh^{1-\theta}|r_h|\). Since \(h\in(0,M^{-2}]\) and \(M\geqslant 1\), this yields \begin{equation} \left||r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\right|\leqslant Mh^{1-\theta}|r_h|\leqslant M\sqrt{h}|r_h|\leqslant |r_h|. \end{equation} This implies that on the event \(\{|r_h|\in(0,\sqrt h]\}\), $$\frac{1}{2}\left(|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|+\sqrt{h}\right)\leqslant\sqrt{h}, \qquad \frac{1}{2}\left(|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|+17\sqrt{h}\right) \geqslant8\sqrt{h}.$$ Hence, on \(\{|r_h|\in(0,\sqrt h]\}\), \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} \bigl(|\,|\hat r_h|+2s\,|\bigr)\geqslant \mathbf 1_{(\sqrt h,\,8\sqrt h)}(s). \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Compare $|r_h|$ and $|\hat r_h|$ and bound the indicator below by $\mathbf 1_{(\sqrt h,8\sqrt h)}(s)$.

nodes.name: Equation (61)
nodes.statement: \left||r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\right|\leqslant Mh^{1-\theta}|r_h|\leqslant M\sqrt{h}|r_h|\leqslant |r_h|.
nodes.label: rr

nodes.name: Equation (62)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} \bigl(|\,|\hat r_h|+2s\,|\bigr)\geqslant \mathbf 1_{(\sqrt h,\,8\sqrt h)}(s). \end{aligned}
nodes.label: matrix-indicator-lower

nodes.name: Insert the indicator bound
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{matrix-indicator-lower} in \eqref{matrix-J6-one-dim}, and taking \(m=8\), we obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\geqslant& \int_{\sqrt h}^{8\sqrt h} \Bigl( p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) - p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s) \Bigr) \,\mathrm ds\\ &\qquad\qquad \times \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Here the positive part has been removed because, for \(s>0\), \(|\hat r_h|+s\geqslant s\), and the centered Gaussian density is decreasing on \([0,\infty)\).
nodes.statement_short: Insert the indicator bound with $m=8$ and drop the positive part.

nodes.name: Equation (63)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\geqslant& \int_{\sqrt h}^{8\sqrt h} \Bigl( p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) - p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s) \Bigr) \,\mathrm ds\\ &\qquad\qquad \times \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{aligned}
nodes.label: matrix-J6-lower1

nodes.name: Rescale
nodes.statement: On \(\{|r_h|\in(0,\sqrt h]\}\), \eqref{rr} gives \(0\leqslant |\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}\leqslant2\). By the change of variables \(s=\sqrt h\,u\), \eqref{matrix-J6-lower1} yields \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right] \\ \geqslant& \frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma}{|\hat r_h|\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_1^8 \left[ \exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2u^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) - \exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2(u+|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h})^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) \right]\mathrm du \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{aligned} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Change variables $s=\sqrt h u$.

nodes.name: Bound the density difference
nodes.statement: Since \(0\leqslant |\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}\leqslant2\), the interval \((3-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h},8-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h})\) is contained in \((1,8)\). Therefore, \[ \begin{aligned} &\int_1^8 \left[ \exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2u^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) - \exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2(u+|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h})^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) \right]\mathrm du\\ \geqslant& \int_{3-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}}^{8-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}} \int_u^{u+|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}} \frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2v}{|\hat r_h|^2} \exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2v^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) \,\mathrm dv\,\mathrm du . \end{aligned} \] For \(u\in(3-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h},8-|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h})\) and \(v\in[u,u+|\hat r_h|/\sqrt{h}]\), we have \(v\in[1,8]\). Hence \[ v\exp\left(-\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2v^2}{2|\hat r_h|^2}\right) \geqslant \min\left\{ \mathrm e^{-|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2/(2|\hat r_h|^2)}, 8\mathrm e^{-32|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2/|\hat r_h|^2} \right\}. \] It follows that \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\\ \geqslant& \frac{5|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^3} {|\hat r_h|^2\sqrt{2\pi h}} \min\left\{ \mathrm e^{-|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2/(2|\hat r_h|^2)}, 8\mathrm e^{-32|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2/|\hat r_h|^2} \right\}\mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: Write the density difference as an integral of the derivative and bound it below on $[1,8]$.

nodes.name: Uniform constant alpha_3
nodes.statement: By the definition of \(\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\), and since \(|\hat r_h|/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma\in[\vartheta_-,\vartheta_+]\), we obtain \begin{equation} \mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\geqslant \frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}|\hat r_h|}{\sqrt h} \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Use ellipticity to replace the direction-dependent constant by $\alpha_{3,\Gamma}$.

nodes.name: Equation (64)
nodes.statement: \mathbb E\left[ \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\geqslant \frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}|\hat r_h|}{\sqrt h} \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|).
nodes.label: matrix-J6-final

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{matrix-J6-start} and \eqref{matrix-J6-final}, we obtain the desired result. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the two bounds.

nodes.name: Contractivity for small distances (Case 1)
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{A} and \ref{A1} hold. For any $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and \(h \in (0, \bar{h}]\), where $\bar{h}$ is defined by \eqref{bar}, consider the coupling $(\hat{X}_h(x,Z), \hat{Y}_h(x,y,Z))$ defined by (\ref{hY}), with $m=8$. Then, if $|r_h|\in(0, \sqrt{h}]$, we have \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)\leqslant (1-Mh)f(|r_h|), \end{equation*} where $|r_h|$ and $|\hat{R}_h|$ are defined by \eqref{Nata} and \eqref{Natc} respectively, function $f$ is given by \eqref{f}.
nodes.statement_short: For $|r_h|\le\sqrt h$ the coupling contracts $f$ at rate $M$.
nodes.label: PR1

nodes.name: Proof of Contractivity for small distances (Case 1)
nodes.statement: We use Taylor's formula with integral remainder: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\left[f(|\hat R_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]=& f'(|r_h|) \mathbb E\bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr) \\ &+ \mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \int_0^1 (1-\tau) f''\bigl(|r_h|+\tau(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|)) \,\mathrm d\tau \right]. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Here \(f''\) is understood in the a.e. sense, which is sufficient since \(f'\) is absolutely continuous. By Lemma \ref{1mom} and $0<f'\leqslant 1$, we get \begin{equation} f'(|r_h|)\mathbb{E}(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|) = f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|)\leqslant ||\hat{r}_h|-|r_h||. \end{equation} We next estimate the second-order term of \eqref{cc4}. Since $h\leqslant R^2$ and $|r_h|\in(0, \sqrt{h}]$, we have $|r_h|\leqslant R$. Then, by (\ref{Sub4eq2}), we get $|\hat{r}_h|\leqslant 2R$. Moreover, since \(h\leqslant (r_1/18)^2\), \(|r_h|+17\sqrt h \leqslant 18\sqrt h \leqslant r_1\). On the event \(|\hat R_h|\in(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)\), all points between \(|r_h|\) and \(|\hat R_h|\) lie in \((0,18\sqrt h)\subset(0,r_1)\). Hence, using \(f''<0\) and Lemma \ref{Le9}, we may discard the complement of this event and obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \int_0^1 (1-\tau) f''\bigl(|r_h|+\tau(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|)\bigr) \,\mathrm d\tau \right] \\ \leqslant& \frac12 \sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)} f''(u)\, \mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\\ \leqslant& \frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}}{2}\sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)} f''(u)\, |\hat r_h|\sqrt h\, \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Since we are working under \(|r_h|\in(0,\sqrt h]\) and have already shown \(|\hat r_h|\leqslant 2R\), it remains to estimate \(f''\). Since \(18\sqrt h\leqslant r_1\), the definitions of \(\varphi,\rho\), and \(f\) give, for \(u\in(0,18\sqrt h)\), \[f''(u)=\varphi'(u)\rho(u)+\varphi(u)\rho'(u).\] Since \(\varphi'(u)\rho(u)\leqslant 0\), we have \begin{equation} \sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)}f''(u)\leqslant \sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)} \varphi(u)\rho'(u)= -\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} \inf_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)}\Phi(u+1)= -\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\Phi(1), \end{equation} because \(\Phi\) is increasing. Substituting (\ref{Theq12}) into \eqref{Tqq1} and combining with \eqref{cc4}, (\ref{cc5}) gives \begin{equation} \mathbb E\left[f(|\hat R_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]\leqslant \bigl||\hat r_h|-|r_h|\bigr| -\frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}}{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} |\hat r_h|\sqrt h\,\Phi(1). \end{equation} We now compare \(|r_h|\) and \(|\hat r_h|\). For any $0<h\leqslant (2M)^{-2}$, we see that $M\sqrt{h}\leqslant 1/2$. Then, by \eqref{rr}, we find that \(\left||r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\right|\leqslant M\sqrt{h}|r_h|\leqslant |r_h|/2\). Therefore, \begin{equation} |r_h|\leqslant 2|\hat{r}_h|\quad \text{and then,} \quad \left||r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\right|\leqslant 2Mh^{1-\bar{\theta}}|\hat{r}_h|. \end{equation} This, together with (\ref{cc6}), yields \begin{equation} \mathbb{E} \left[f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]\leqslant |\hat r_h|\sqrt h \left(2Mh^{1/2-\bar\theta} -\frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(1)} {2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} \right). \end{equation} By the definition of \(\bar h\), \(2Mh^{1/2-\bar\theta} \leqslant \alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(1)/(4\alpha_{1, \Gamma})\). This implies that \begin{equation*} 2Mh^{1/2-\bar\theta} -\frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(1)} {2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} \leqslant-\frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(1)} {4\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\leqslant -2Mh^{1/2-\bar{\theta}}\leqslant -2M\sqrt{h}. \end{equation*} Inserting this into \eqref{tqq3} gives \begin{equation} \mathbb{E} \left[f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]\leqslant -2Mh|\hat{r}_h|. \end{equation} Moreover, as shown in (\ref{f1}), we have $f(u)\leqslant u$ for all $u\geqslant 0$. Then, using (\ref{tqq2}), we get $f(|r_h|)\leqslant |r_h|\leqslant 2|\hat{r}_h|$. Therefore, combining this with \eqref{P4.9}, we arrive at the desired conclusion. Note that $1-Mh\in(0, 1)$ for any $h\in(0, h_1]$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Second-order Taylor expansion of $f$: the first-moment identity controls the linear term and Lemma 4.9 gives a negative curvature gain. The step-size restriction makes the gain dominate.

nodes.name: Taylor expansion of f
nodes.statement: We use Taylor's formula with integral remainder: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\left[f(|\hat R_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]=& f'(|r_h|) \mathbb E\bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr) \\ &+ \mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \int_0^1 (1-\tau) f''\bigl(|r_h|+\tau(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|)) \,\mathrm d\tau \right]. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Here \(f''\) is understood in the a.e. sense, which is sufficient since \(f'\) is absolutely continuous.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $f(|\hat R_h|)-f(|r_h|)$ to second order with integral remainder.

nodes.name: Equation (65)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\left[f(|\hat R_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]=& f'(|r_h|) \mathbb E\bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr) \\ &+ \mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \int_0^1 (1-\tau) f''\bigl(|r_h|+\tau(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|)) \,\mathrm d\tau \right]. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: cc4

nodes.name: First-order term
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{1mom} and $0<f'\leqslant 1$, we get \begin{equation} f'(|r_h|)\mathbb{E}(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|) = f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|)\leqslant ||\hat{r}_h|-|r_h||. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The first-moment identity bounds the first-order term.

nodes.name: Equation (66)
nodes.statement: f'(|r_h|)\mathbb{E}(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|) = f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|)\leqslant ||\hat{r}_h|-|r_h||.
nodes.label: cc5

nodes.name: Second-order term via Lemma 4.9
nodes.statement: We next estimate the second-order term of \eqref{cc4}. Since $h\leqslant R^2$ and $|r_h|\in(0, \sqrt{h}]$, we have $|r_h|\leqslant R$. Then, by (\ref{Sub4eq2}), we get $|\hat{r}_h|\leqslant 2R$. Moreover, since \(h\leqslant (r_1/18)^2\), \(|r_h|+17\sqrt h \leqslant 18\sqrt h \leqslant r_1\). On the event \(|\hat R_h|\in(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)\), all points between \(|r_h|\) and \(|\hat R_h|\) lie in \((0,18\sqrt h)\subset(0,r_1)\). Hence, using \(f''<0\) and Lemma \ref{Le9}, we may discard the complement of this event and obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \int_0^1 (1-\tau) f''\bigl(|r_h|+\tau(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|)\bigr) \,\mathrm d\tau \right] \\ \leqslant& \frac12 \sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)} f''(u)\, \mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\\ \leqslant& \frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}}{2}\sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)} f''(u)\, |\hat r_h|\sqrt h\, \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to the event of Lemma 4.9 and use concavity of $f$.

nodes.name: Equation (67)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \int_0^1 (1-\tau) f''\bigl(|r_h|+\tau(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|)\bigr) \,\mathrm d\tau \right] \\ \leqslant& \frac12 \sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)} f''(u)\, \mathbb E\left[ \bigl(|\hat R_h|-|r_h|\bigr)^2 \mathbf 1_{(|r_h|+\sqrt h,\,|r_h|+17\sqrt h)} (|\hat R_h|) \right]\\ \leqslant& \frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}}{2}\sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)} f''(u)\, |\hat r_h|\sqrt h\, \mathbf 1_{(0,\sqrt h]}(|r_h|) \mathbf 1_{[0,2R]}(|\hat r_h|). \end{aligned}
nodes.label: Tqq1

nodes.name: Bound f''
nodes.statement: Since we are working under \(|r_h|\in(0,\sqrt h]\) and have already shown \(|\hat r_h|\leqslant 2R\), it remains to estimate \(f''\). Since \(18\sqrt h\leqslant r_1\), the definitions of \(\varphi,\rho\), and \(f\) give, for \(u\in(0,18\sqrt h)\), \[f''(u)=\varphi'(u)\rho(u)+\varphi(u)\rho'(u).\] Since \(\varphi'(u)\rho(u)\leqslant 0\), we have \begin{equation} \sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)}f''(u)\leqslant \sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)} \varphi(u)\rho'(u)= -\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} \inf_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)}\Phi(u+1)= -\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\Phi(1), \end{equation} because \(\Phi\) is increasing.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\sup f''$ by $-\alpha_{2,\Gamma}\Phi(1)/\alpha_{1,\Gamma}$.

nodes.name: Equation (68)
nodes.statement: \sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)}f''(u)\leqslant \sup_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)} \varphi(u)\rho'(u)= -\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} \inf_{u\in(0,18\sqrt h)}\Phi(u+1)= -\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\Phi(1),
nodes.label: Theq12

nodes.name: Combine first- and second-order terms
nodes.statement: Substituting (\ref{Theq12}) into \eqref{Tqq1} and combining with \eqref{cc4}, (\ref{cc5}) gives \begin{equation} \mathbb E\left[f(|\hat R_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]\leqslant \bigl||\hat r_h|-|r_h|\bigr| -\frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}}{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} |\hat r_h|\sqrt h\,\Phi(1). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Obtain $\mathbb E[f(|\hat R_h|)-f(|r_h|)]\le ||\hat r_h|-|r_h||-c|\hat r_h|\sqrt h$.

nodes.name: Equation (69)
nodes.statement: \mathbb E\left[f(|\hat R_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]\leqslant \bigl||\hat r_h|-|r_h|\bigr| -\frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}}{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} |\hat r_h|\sqrt h\,\Phi(1).
nodes.label: cc6

nodes.name: Compare r_h and hat r_h
nodes.statement: We now compare \(|r_h|\) and \(|\hat r_h|\). For any $0<h\leqslant (2M)^{-2}$, we see that $M\sqrt{h}\leqslant 1/2$. Then, by \eqref{rr}, we find that \(\left||r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\right|\leqslant M\sqrt{h}|r_h|\leqslant |r_h|/2\). Therefore, \begin{equation} |r_h|\leqslant 2|\hat{r}_h|\quad \text{and then,} \quad \left||r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\right|\leqslant 2Mh^{1-\bar{\theta}}|\hat{r}_h|. \end{equation} This, together with (\ref{cc6}), yields \begin{equation} \mathbb{E} \left[f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]\leqslant |\hat r_h|\sqrt h \left(2Mh^{1/2-\bar\theta} -\frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(1)} {2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} \right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Show $|r_h|\le2|\hat r_h|$ and bound their difference.

nodes.name: Equation (70)
nodes.statement: |r_h|\leqslant 2|\hat{r}_h|\quad \text{and then,} \quad \left||r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\right|\leqslant 2Mh^{1-\bar{\theta}}|\hat{r}_h|.
nodes.label: tqq2

nodes.name: Equation (71)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E} \left[f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]\leqslant |\hat r_h|\sqrt h \left(2Mh^{1/2-\bar\theta} -\frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(1)} {2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} \right).
nodes.label: tqq3

nodes.name: Use the step-size restriction
nodes.statement: By the definition of \(\bar h\), \(2Mh^{1/2-\bar\theta} \leqslant \alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(1)/(4\alpha_{1, \Gamma})\). This implies that \begin{equation*} 2Mh^{1/2-\bar\theta} -\frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(1)} {2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} \leqslant-\frac{\alpha_{3,\Gamma}\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(1)} {4\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\leqslant -2Mh^{1/2-\bar{\theta}}\leqslant -2M\sqrt{h}. \end{equation*} Inserting this into \eqref{tqq3} gives \begin{equation} \mathbb{E} \left[f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]\leqslant -2Mh|\hat{r}_h|. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The choice of $\bar h$ makes the second-order gain dominate.

nodes.name: Equation (72)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E} \left[f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\right]\leqslant -2Mh|\hat{r}_h|.
nodes.label: P4.9

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Moreover, as shown in (\ref{f1}), we have $f(u)\leqslant u$ for all $u\geqslant 0$. Then, using (\ref{tqq2}), we get $f(|r_h|)\leqslant |r_h|\leqslant 2|\hat{r}_h|$. Therefore, combining this with \eqref{P4.9}, we arrive at the desired conclusion. Note that $1-Mh\in(0, 1)$ for any $h\in(0, h_1]$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Use $f(u)\le u$ to get contraction at rate $M$.

nodes.name: Constant alpha_{5,Gamma}
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation} \alpha_{5, \Gamma}=\mathrm{min}\left\{\frac{\varphi(r_1)R K}{4r_1},\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\alpha_{4, \Gamma}\Phi(1)}{4\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\right\}, \end{equation} where \(R, K\) are given in Assumption \ref{A1}, and constants $\alpha_{1, \Gamma}, \alpha_{2, \Gamma}, \alpha_{4, \Gamma}$ are defined in (\ref{c0}), (\ref{Ac}), and (\ref{c2}), respectively.

nodes.name: Constant alpha_5
nodes.statement: \alpha_{5, \Gamma}=\mathrm{min}\left\{\frac{\varphi(r_1)R K}{4r_1},\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\alpha_{4, \Gamma}\Phi(1)}{4\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\right\},
nodes.label: hatc

nodes.name: Contractivity for intermediate distances (Case 2)
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{A} and \ref{A1} hold. For any $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and \(h \in (0, \bar{h}]\), where $\bar{h}$ is defined by \eqref{bar}, consider the coupling $(\hat{X}_h(x,Z), \hat{Y}_h(x,y,Z))$ defined by (\ref{hY}), with $m=8$. Then, if $|r_h|\in(\sqrt{h}, r_1]$, we have \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)\leqslant (1-\left(\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\wedge\alpha_{5, \Gamma}\right)h)f(|r_h|), \end{equation*} where $|r_h|, |\hat{r}_h|, |\hat{R}_h|$ are defined in (\ref{eq3}), function $f$, constants $\alpha_{2, \Gamma}$ and $\alpha_{5, \Gamma}$ are given by (\ref{f}), (\ref{Ac}) and (\ref{hatc}) respectively.
nodes.statement_short: For $\sqrt h<|r_h|\le r_1$ the coupling contracts $f$ at rate $\alpha_{2,\Gamma}\wedge\alpha_{5,\Gamma}$.
nodes.label: PR4

nodes.name: Proof of Contractivity for intermediate distances (Case 2)
