nodes.name: Noise term via Jensen
nodes.statement: {\bf Step I. The case $|r_h|\in(R,r_1]$.} We first show that \(\mathbb E\bigl[f(|\hat R_h|)-f(|\hat r_h|)\bigr]\leqslant 0\). According to \eqref{hY} and \eqref{Ac}, we have \[0\leqslant |\hat{R}_h|\leqslant |\hat{r}_h|+2|\lambda_{\hat r_h}(\Sigma Z)|\leqslant 2R+2m=r_1.\] By Lemma \ref{1mom}, \(\mathbb E|\hat R_h|=|\hat r_h|\). Since $f$ is concave on $(0,r_1)$, Jensen's inequality yields \[\mathbb E f(|\hat R_h|) \leqslant f(\mathbb E|\hat R_h|)=f(|\hat r_h|).\] Consequently, \(\mathbb E\bigl[f(|\hat R_h|)-f(|\hat r_h|)\bigr]\leqslant 0\).
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.6 and concavity give $\mathbb E f(|\hat R_h|)\le f(|\hat r_h|)$.

nodes.name: Drift term contraction
nodes.statement: On the other hand, together with the fact that $f''(u)< 0$ on $u\in(0, r_1)$ and \eqref{Sub4eq1}, we have \begin{align*} f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|)\leqslant -\frac{hK}{2}f'(|r_h|)|r_h|. \end{align*} Since $f'(u)= \varphi(u)\rho(u)\geqslant \varphi(u)/2$ for all $u\in(0, r_1)$, $\varphi$ is decreasing on $[0, +\infty)$ and $f(u)\leqslant u$ for all $u\geqslant 0$, we obtain $$\frac{hK}{2}f'(|r_h|)|r_h|\geqslant \frac{hK}{4}\varphi(|r_h|)|r_h|\geqslant \frac{hK}{4}\varphi(r_1)R\geqslant \frac{\varphi(r_1)R K}{4r_1}hf(r_1)\geqslant \frac{\varphi(r_1)R K}{4r_1}hf(|r_h|).$$ This, together with the definition of $\alpha_{5, \Gamma}$ in \eqref{hatc}, yields \begin{equation*} f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|) \leqslant -\frac{\varphi(r_1)R K}{4r_1}hf(|r_h|)\leqslant -\alpha_{5, \Gamma}hf(|r_h|). \end{equation*} Hence \eqref{Sc1} holds for $|r_h|\in(R,r_1]$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.7 gives $f(|\hat r_h|)-f(|r_h|)\le-\alpha_{5,\Gamma}hf(|r_h|)$.

nodes.name: Step II: |r_h| in (sqrt h, R]
nodes.statement: {\bf Step II. The case $|r_h|\in(\sqrt h,R]$.} Since $|\hat r_h|\leqslant \sqrt h<|r_h|$ and $f$ is increasing, we have \(f(|\hat r_h|)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant 0\). For $|\hat{r}_h|\in [0, \sqrt{h}]$, by using Lemmas \ref{1mom} and \ref{Le10}, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|\hat{r}_h|) &\leqslant \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|\hat{r}_h|)^2\1_{(0, |\hat{r}_h|+\sqrt{h})}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\sup_{u\in(0, |\hat{r}_h|+\sqrt{h})}f''(u)\\ &\leqslant \frac{\alpha_{4, \Gamma}}{2}|\hat{r}_h|\sqrt{h}\sup_{u\in(0,2\sqrt{h})}f''(u). \end{align*} Similarly to (\ref{Theq12}), we get \(\sup_{u\in(0, 2\sqrt{h})}f''(u)\leqslant -\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\Phi(1)\), which yields \begin{equation} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|\hat{r}_h|)\leqslant -\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\alpha_{4, \Gamma}}{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\Phi(1)|\hat{r}_h|\sqrt{h}. \end{equation} This, together with $f(|r_h|)\leqslant |r_h|$ and \eqref{tqq2} implies $-|\hat{r}_h|\sqrt{h}\leqslant -|r_h| h/2\leqslant -h f(|r_h|)/2$. Substituting this into \eqref{ccc} and using \eqref{hatc} gives \(\mathbb{E}[f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|\hat{r}_h|)]\leqslant-\alpha_{5, \Gamma}hf(|r_h|)\). Hence \eqref{Sc2} holds for $|r_h|\in(\sqrt{h}, R]$.
nodes.statement_short: The drift term is non-positive and Lemma 4.10 makes the noise term contractive.

nodes.name: Drift term non-positive
nodes.statement: {\bf Step II. The case $|r_h|\in(\sqrt h,R]$.} Since $|\hat r_h|\leqslant \sqrt h<|r_h|$ and $f$ is increasing, we have \(f(|\hat r_h|)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant 0\).
nodes.statement_short: Since $|\hat r_h|<|r_h|$, $f(|\hat r_h|)\le f(|r_h|)$.

nodes.name: Noise term via Lemma 4.10
nodes.statement: For $|\hat{r}_h|\in [0, \sqrt{h}]$, by using Lemmas \ref{1mom} and \ref{Le10}, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|\hat{r}_h|) &\leqslant \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|\hat{r}_h|)^2\1_{(0, |\hat{r}_h|+\sqrt{h})}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\sup_{u\in(0, |\hat{r}_h|+\sqrt{h})}f''(u)\\ &\leqslant \frac{\alpha_{4, \Gamma}}{2}|\hat{r}_h|\sqrt{h}\sup_{u\in(0,2\sqrt{h})}f''(u). \end{align*} Similarly to (\ref{Theq12}), we get \(\sup_{u\in(0, 2\sqrt{h})}f''(u)\leqslant -\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\Phi(1)\), which yields \begin{equation} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|\hat{r}_h|)\leqslant -\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\alpha_{4, \Gamma}}{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\Phi(1)|\hat{r}_h|\sqrt{h}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Second-order Taylor bound with Lemma 4.10 gives a gain of order $|\hat r_h|\sqrt h$.

nodes.name: Equation (77)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|\hat{r}_h|)\leqslant -\frac{\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\alpha_{4, \Gamma}}{2\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\Phi(1)|\hat{r}_h|\sqrt{h}.
nodes.label: ccc

nodes.name: Convert to a contraction rate
nodes.statement: This, together with $f(|r_h|)\leqslant |r_h|$ and \eqref{tqq2} implies $-|\hat{r}_h|\sqrt{h}\leqslant -|r_h| h/2\leqslant -h f(|r_h|)/2$. Substituting this into \eqref{ccc} and using \eqref{hatc} gives \(\mathbb{E}[f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|\hat{r}_h|)]\leqslant-\alpha_{5, \Gamma}hf(|r_h|)\). Hence \eqref{Sc2} holds for $|r_h|\in(\sqrt{h}, R]$.
nodes.statement_short: Convert the gain into $-\alpha_{5,\Gamma}hf(|r_h|)$.

nodes.name: Combine and check positivity
nodes.statement: Therefore, combining the above results leads to the desired conclusion. Note that $\bar{\theta}\in(0, 1/2)$ and $M\geqslant 1\vee [\sqrt{\varphi(r_1)RK}/(8\sqrt{r_1})]$. Thus, by \eqref{hatc}, \[(4M)^{-2}\leqslant \frac{4r_1}{\varphi(r_1)RK}\leqslant \alpha_{5, \Gamma}^{-1}.\] Therefore, we have $1-\alpha_{5, \Gamma}h>0$ for any $h\in(0, (4M)^{-2}]$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Combine both steps and check $1-\alpha_{5,\Gamma}h>0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Contractivity for intermediate distances (Case 2), subcase (III)
nodes.statement: For \underline{\bf{Case 2. \textit{$|r_h|\in(\sqrt{h}, r_1]$}}} and \underline{$(\mathrm{III})~|\hat{r}_h|>2R$}, the synchronous coupling occurs. Hence, $|\hat{R}_h| = |\hat{r}_h|$. This implies $\mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|\hat{r}_h|) = 0$. Hence, similarly to {\bf Step I} in Proposition \ref{PR2}, using \eqref{Sub4eq1} and \eqref{f1}, we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|) =f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|) \leqslant -\frac{\varphi(r_1)R K}{4r_1}hf(|r_h|). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: When $|\hat r_h|>2R$ the coupling is synchronous, so the contraction comes from the drift step as in Step I of Proposition 3.

nodes.name: Synchronous coupling removes the noise term
nodes.statement: For \underline{\bf{Case 2. \textit{$|r_h|\in(\sqrt{h}, r_1]$}}} and \underline{$(\mathrm{III})~|\hat{r}_h|>2R$}, the synchronous coupling occurs. Hence, $|\hat{R}_h| = |\hat{r}_h|$. This implies $\mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|\hat{r}_h|) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: When $|\hat r_h|>2R$ the coupling is synchronous so $|\hat R_h|=|\hat r_h|$.

nodes.name: Drift contraction
nodes.statement: Hence, similarly to {\bf Step I} in Proposition \ref{PR2}, using \eqref{Sub4eq1} and \eqref{f1}, we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|) =f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|) \leqslant -\frac{\varphi(r_1)R K}{4r_1}hf(|r_h|). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.7 and (f1) give the contraction (I-3).

nodes.name: Contraction estimate in case (III)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|) =f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|) \leqslant -\frac{\varphi(r_1)R K}{4r_1}hf(|r_h|).
nodes.label: I-3

nodes.name: Second-moment lower bound for moderate distances
nodes.statement: Let Assumption \ref{A} hold. For any $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $h\in (0, (4M)^{-2}\wedge (4R^2)]$, consider the coupling $(\hat{X}_h(x,Z), \hat{Y}_h(x, y,Z))$ defined by (\ref{hY}), with \(m=8\). Then, we have $$\mathbb{E}\left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h},|r_h|\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\geqslant \alpha_{1, \Gamma}h\1_{\left[\sqrt{h}, 2R\right]}(|\hat{r}_h|)\1_{\left[\sqrt{h}, h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)\right]}(|r_h|),$$ where $|r_h|, |\hat{r}_h|, |\hat{R}_h|$ are given by (\ref{eq3}), constant \(\alpha_{1,\Gamma}\) is defined by \eqref{c0}.
nodes.statement_short: For moderate $|r_h|$ and $|\hat r_h|\in[\sqrt h,2R]$ the coupling moves inwards by order $\sqrt h$ with probability bounded below.
nodes.label: 2mom

nodes.name: Proof of Second-moment lower bound for moderate distances
nodes.statement: If either \(|\hat r_h|\notin[\sqrt h,2R]\) or \(|r_h|\notin[\sqrt h,h^{\bar\theta-1/2}/(4M)]\), then the right-hand side is zero and the assertion is immediate. Hence it remains to consider the case \(|\hat r_h|\in[\sqrt h,2R]\) and \(|r_h|\in[\sqrt h,h^{\bar\theta-1/2}/(4M)]\). By \(\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\geqslant \1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\), we observe that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb{E} \left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\geqslant& \mathbb{E} \left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant &\frac{h}{16}\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]. \end{aligned} \end{equation} We next establish a lower bound for \(\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\). Since $h\in(0, (4M)^{-2}]$, we have $\sqrt{h}\leqslant h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)$. Therefore, under the condition $|r_h|\in[\sqrt{h}, h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)]$, we obtain $Mh^{1-\bar{\theta}}|r_h|\leqslant \sqrt{h}/4$. This, together with \eqref{rr}, yields \(\left||r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\right|\leqslant Mh^{1-\bar{\theta}}|r_h|\leqslant \sqrt{h}/4\), which implies \(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}\leqslant|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4\) and \(|\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\leqslant |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\). Hence, \begin{equation} \1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\geqslant \1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\1_{\left[\sqrt{h}, h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)\right]}(|r_h|). \end{equation} Then, inserting \eqref{ST2} into \eqref{ST1} gives \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E}\left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant&\frac{h}{16}\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\1_{\left[\sqrt{h}, h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)\right]}(|r_h|). \end{aligned} \end{equation*} It remains to derive a uniform lower bound for \(\mathbb{E}[\1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)]\). As in the proof of Lemma \ref{Le10}, by \eqref{refR}, the reflection contribution gives \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant& \int_{\mathbb R} \mathbf 1_{\left(|\hat r_h|-3\sqrt h/4,\,|\hat r_h|-\sqrt h/2\right)} \left(\left||\hat r_h|+2s\right|\right) \\ &\qquad\times \left( \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) - \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(|\hat r_h|+s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s) \right)^+ \,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned} \] We now restrict the integral to \(s\in(-3\sqrt h/8,-\sqrt h/4)\). Since \(M\geqslant 1\) and \(h\leqslant (4M)^{-2}\), we have \(|s|<3\sqrt h/8<m\). Moreover, for \(|\hat r_h|\in[\sqrt h,2R]\), we have \(\left||\hat r_h|+2s\right|<m\) and \[ \left||\hat r_h|+2s\right| = |\hat r_h|+2s \in \left(|\hat r_h|-\frac{3\sqrt h}{4}, |\hat r_h|-\frac{\sqrt h}{2}\right). \] Furthermore, \(|\hat r_h|+2s>0\) implies \(|s|<|\hat r_h|+s\). By monotonicity of the centred Gaussian density on \([0,\infty)\), \(p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \geq p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s)\). Consequently, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant& \mathbf 1_{[\sqrt h,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \int_{-3\sqrt h/8}^{-\sqrt h/4} \left[ p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) - p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s) \right] \,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned} \end{equation} Making the change of variables \(s=\sqrt h\,u\), the right-hand side of \eqref{J8-lower1} becomes \begin{equation} \mathbf 1_{[\sqrt h,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \int_{-3/8}^{-1/4} p_{0,|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(u) \left[ 1- \exp\left\{ -\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}{|\hat r_h|^2} \frac{|\hat r_h|}{\sqrt h} \left( \frac{|\hat r_h|}{2\sqrt h}+u \right) \right\} \right] \,\mathrm du . \end{equation} On the present event, \(|\hat r_h|\geqslant \sqrt h\). For fixed \(u\in (-3/8,-1/4)\) define \[ H_u(t) := 1- \exp\left\{ -\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}{|\hat r_h|^2} t\left(\frac{t}{2}+u\right) \right\}. \] Observe that \(H_u(t)\geqslant H_u(1)\) for all \(t\geqslant 1\). Moreover, for \(u\in(-3/8,-1/4)\), \(1/2+u\in (1/8, 1/4)\). Thus \[ H_u(1) = 1- \exp\left\{ -\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}{|\hat r_h|^2} \left(\frac12+u\right) \right\} \geqslant 1- \exp\left\{ -\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}{8|\hat r_h|^2} \right\}. \] Consequently, since \(p_{0,a}(\cdot)\) is even, \eqref{J8-lower2} implies \[\begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant& \mathbf 1_{[\sqrt h,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \left( 1- \exp\left\{ -\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}{8|\hat r_h|^2} \right\} \right) \int^{3/8}_{1/4} p_{0,|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(u) \,\mathrm du . \end{aligned}\] By the uniform ellipticity bounds, \(|\hat r_h|/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma\in[\vartheta_-,\vartheta_+]\), and by the definition of \(\alpha_{1,\Gamma}\) in \eqref{c0}, we obtain the desired conclusion. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Shift the target event to one centred at $|\hat r_h|$ and lower-bound the reflection probability by a one-dimensional Gaussian integral.

nodes.name: Trivial cases
nodes.statement: If either \(|\hat r_h|\notin[\sqrt h,2R]\) or \(|r_h|\notin[\sqrt h,h^{\bar\theta-1/2}/(4M)]\), then the right-hand side is zero and the assertion is immediate. Hence it remains to consider the case \(|\hat r_h|\in[\sqrt h,2R]\) and \(|r_h|\in[\sqrt h,h^{\bar\theta-1/2}/(4M)]\).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the case where both indicators equal one.

nodes.name: Reduce to a probability
nodes.statement: By \(\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\geqslant \1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\), we observe that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbb{E} \left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\geqslant& \mathbb{E} \left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant &\frac{h}{16}\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Shrink the event so the squared jump is at least $h/16$.

nodes.name: Equation (79)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathbb{E} \left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\geqslant& \mathbb{E} \left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant &\frac{h}{16}\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: ST1

nodes.name: Compare the events
nodes.statement: We next establish a lower bound for \(\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\). Since $h\in(0, (4M)^{-2}]$, we have $\sqrt{h}\leqslant h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)$. Therefore, under the condition $|r_h|\in[\sqrt{h}, h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)]$, we obtain $Mh^{1-\bar{\theta}}|r_h|\leqslant \sqrt{h}/4$. This, together with \eqref{rr}, yields \(\left||r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\right|\leqslant Mh^{1-\bar{\theta}}|r_h|\leqslant \sqrt{h}/4\), which implies \(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}\leqslant|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4\) and \(|\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\leqslant |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\). Hence, \begin{equation} \1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\geqslant \1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\1_{\left[\sqrt{h}, h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)\right]}(|r_h|). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Use (rr) to shift the event to one centred at $|\hat r_h|$.

nodes.name: Equation (80)
nodes.statement: \1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|-\sqrt{h}/4\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\geqslant \1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\1_{\left[\sqrt{h}, h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)\right]}(|r_h|).
nodes.label: ST2

nodes.name: Insert the event comparison
nodes.statement: Then, inserting \eqref{ST2} into \eqref{ST1} gives \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E}\left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{\left(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant&\frac{h}{16}\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\1_{\left[\sqrt{h}, h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)\right]}(|r_h|). \end{aligned} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Combine (ST1) and (ST2).

nodes.name: Reflection contribution
nodes.statement: It remains to derive a uniform lower bound for \(\mathbb{E}[\1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)]\). As in the proof of Lemma \ref{Le10}, by \eqref{refR}, the reflection contribution gives \[ \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant& \int_{\mathbb R} \mathbf 1_{\left(|\hat r_h|-3\sqrt h/4,\,|\hat r_h|-\sqrt h/2\right)} \left(\left||\hat r_h|+2s\right|\right) \\ &\qquad\times \left( \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) - \mathbf 1_{[-m,m]}(|\hat r_h|+s) p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s) \right)^+ \,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: As in Lemma 4.10, bound the probability below by the reflection branch.

nodes.name: Restrict the integral
nodes.statement: We now restrict the integral to \(s\in(-3\sqrt h/8,-\sqrt h/4)\). Since \(M\geqslant 1\) and \(h\leqslant (4M)^{-2}\), we have \(|s|<3\sqrt h/8<m\). Moreover, for \(|\hat r_h|\in[\sqrt h,2R]\), we have \(\left||\hat r_h|+2s\right|<m\) and \[ \left||\hat r_h|+2s\right| = |\hat r_h|+2s \in \left(|\hat r_h|-\frac{3\sqrt h}{4}, |\hat r_h|-\frac{\sqrt h}{2}\right). \] Furthermore, \(|\hat r_h|+2s>0\) implies \(|s|<|\hat r_h|+s\). By monotonicity of the centred Gaussian density on \([0,\infty)\), \(p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) \geq p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s)\). Consequently, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant& \mathbf 1_{[\sqrt h,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \int_{-3\sqrt h/8}^{-\sqrt h/4} \left[ p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) - p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s) \right] \,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to $s\in(-3\sqrt h/8,-\sqrt h/4)$.

nodes.name: Equation (81)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant& \mathbf 1_{[\sqrt h,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \int_{-3\sqrt h/8}^{-\sqrt h/4} \left[ p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(s) - p_{0,h|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(|\hat r_h|+s) \right] \,\mathrm ds . \end{aligned}
nodes.label: J8-lower1

nodes.name: Rescale
nodes.statement: Making the change of variables \(s=\sqrt h\,u\), the right-hand side of \eqref{J8-lower1} becomes \begin{equation} \mathbf 1_{[\sqrt h,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \int_{-3/8}^{-1/4} p_{0,|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(u) \left[ 1- \exp\left\{ -\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}{|\hat r_h|^2} \frac{|\hat r_h|}{\sqrt h} \left( \frac{|\hat r_h|}{2\sqrt h}+u \right) \right\} \right] \,\mathrm du . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Change variables $s=\sqrt h u$.

nodes.name: Equation (82)
nodes.statement: \mathbf 1_{[\sqrt h,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \int_{-3/8}^{-1/4} p_{0,|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(u) \left[ 1- \exp\left\{ -\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}{|\hat r_h|^2} \frac{|\hat r_h|}{\sqrt h} \left( \frac{|\hat r_h|}{2\sqrt h}+u \right) \right\} \right] \,\mathrm du .
nodes.label: J8-lower2

nodes.name: Monotonicity in t
nodes.statement: On the present event, \(|\hat r_h|\geqslant \sqrt h\). For fixed \(u\in (-3/8,-1/4)\) define \[ H_u(t) := 1- \exp\left\{ -\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}{|\hat r_h|^2} t\left(\frac{t}{2}+u\right) \right\}. \] Observe that \(H_u(t)\geqslant H_u(1)\) for all \(t\geqslant 1\). Moreover, for \(u\in(-3/8,-1/4)\), \(1/2+u\in (1/8, 1/4)\). Thus \[ H_u(1) = 1- \exp\left\{ -\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}{|\hat r_h|^2} \left(\frac12+u\right) \right\} \geqslant 1- \exp\left\{ -\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}{8|\hat r_h|^2} \right\}. \] Consequently, since \(p_{0,a}(\cdot)\) is even, \eqref{J8-lower2} implies \[\begin{aligned} &\mathbb{E} \left[\1_{\left(|\hat{r}_h|-3\sqrt{h}/4, |\hat{r}_h|-\sqrt{h}/2\right)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\\ \geqslant& \mathbf 1_{[\sqrt h,2R]}(|\hat r_h|) \left( 1- \exp\left\{ -\frac{|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}{8|\hat r_h|^2} \right\} \right) \int^{3/8}_{1/4} p_{0,|\hat r_h|^2/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma^2}(u) \,\mathrm du . \end{aligned}\]
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of $H_u$ bounds the bracket below uniformly.

nodes.name: Uniform constant alpha_1
nodes.statement: By the uniform ellipticity bounds, \(|\hat r_h|/|\hat r_h|_\Gamma\in[\vartheta_-,\vartheta_+]\), and by the definition of \(\alpha_{1,\Gamma}\) in \eqref{c0}, we obtain the desired conclusion. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Ellipticity gives the constant $\alpha_{1,\Gamma}$.

nodes.name: Contractivity in case 2(II)
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{A} and \ref{A1} hold. For any $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $h \in (0, \bar{h}]$, where $\bar{h}$ is defined by \eqref{bar}, consider the coupling $(\hat{X}_h(x,Z), \hat{Y}_h(x,y,Z))$ defined by (\ref{hY}), with $m=8$. Then, if $|r_h|\in(\sqrt{h}, r_1]$ and $|\hat{r}_h|\in (\sqrt{h}, 2R]$, we have \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)\leqslant (1-\alpha_{2, \Gamma}h)f(|r_h|), \end{equation*} where $|r_h|, |\hat{r}_h|, |\hat{R}_h|$ are defined in (\ref{eq3}), the function $f$ is defined in \eqref{f}, and the constant $\alpha_{2,\Gamma}$ is defined in \eqref{Ac}.
nodes.statement_short: For $\sqrt h<|r_h|\le r_1$ and $\sqrt h<|\hat r_h|\le 2R$ the coupling contracts $f$ at rate $\alpha_{2,\Gamma}$.
nodes.label: PR3

nodes.name: Proof of Contractivity in case 2(II)
nodes.statement: By the definition of $\bar h$, we have $h \in (0, (4Mr_1)^{2/(2\bar{\theta}-1)}]$. Since $\bar\theta\in(0,1/2)$, this implies $r_1\leqslant h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)$. Hence, for every $|r_h|\in(\sqrt h,r_1]$, \(|r_h|\in[\sqrt h,h^{\bar\theta-1/2}/(4M)]\). Together with $|\hat{r}_h|\in(\sqrt h,2R]$, Lemma \ref{2mom} gives \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}\left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\geqslant \alpha_{1, \Gamma}h. \end{equation} Since $f''< 0$ on $(0, r_1)$, by \eqref{cc4} and Lemma \ref{1mom}, we have \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\\ \leqslant &f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|)+\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}f''(u). \end{align*} We therefore obtain from (\ref{Theq1}) that \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|) + \frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}{2}\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}f''(u). \end{equation*} Since $f'(u) = \varphi(u)\rho(u)$ on $u\in (0, r_1]$, we have $$\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}f''(u)\leqslant \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi'(u)\rho(u))+\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi(u)\rho'(u)).$$ Therefore, \begin{align*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant& f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|) + \frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}{2} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi'(u)\rho(u))\\ &+\frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}{2}\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi(u)\rho'(u)). \end{align*} It remains to prove \begin{equation} f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|)+\frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}{2} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi'(u)\rho(u))\leqslant 0 \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}h}{2}\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi(u)\rho'(u))\leqslant -\alpha_{2, \Gamma}h f(|r_h|). \end{equation} {\bf Step I. Proof of \eqref{Ca1}.} Since $\rho$ is decreasing and positive, while $\varphi'<0$, we have \begin{align*} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi'(u)\rho(u)) \leqslant \rho(|r_h|)\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u), \end{align*} Since $f'=\varphi\rho$, it is enough to show that \begin{equation} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u)\leqslant \frac{2(|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|)}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}\varphi(|r_h|). \end{equation} If $|r_h|\in(R, r_1]$, then by \eqref{Sub4eq1}, $|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\geqslant (hK/2)|r_h|>0$. Since $\varphi'\leqslant 0$, \eqref{Theq7} follows immediately. It remains to consider the case $|r_h|\in(\sqrt h,R]$. By \eqref{varphi}, \(\varphi'(u) = -(2L+1)(u+1)\varphi(u)/\alpha_{1,\Gamma}\). Hence \begin{equation} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u) =-\frac{2L+1}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\inf_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\left((u+1) \varphi(u)\right). \end{equation} Since $\varphi$ is decreasing and $h\leqslant 1$, we have \begin{equation} \inf_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\left((u+1) \varphi(u)\right)\geqslant(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}+1)\varphi(|r_h|)\geqslant |r_h|\varphi(|r_h|). \end{equation} Substituting (\ref{Tq2}) into (\ref{Theq3}) yields \begin{equation} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u)\leqslant -\frac{(2L+1)|r_h|}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\varphi(|r_h|). \end{equation} We now estimate $|r_h|-|\hat r_h|$. By (\ref{ss}), and using the fact that \(h\leqslant M^{1/(2\bar\theta-1)}\) so that \(Mh^{1-2\bar{\theta}}\leqslant 1\), we get \begin{equation*} \frac{|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|}{h}\geqslant \frac{|r_h|}{h}\left(1-\sqrt{1+2hL+Mh^{2-2\bar{\theta}}}\right)\geqslant \frac{1-\sqrt{1+(2L+1)h}}{h}|r_h|. \end{equation*} One observes that function $x\mapsto (\sqrt{1+(2L+1) x}-1)/x$ is decreasing on $(0, +\infty)$. This implies that for any $x>0$, \begin{align*} 0\leqslant \frac{\sqrt{1+(2L+1)x}-1}{x}\leqslant \frac{2L+1}{2}. \end{align*} Consequently, \((1-\sqrt{1+(2L+1)h})/h \geqslant -(2L+1)/2\). Thus, \(-(2L+1)|r_h|\leqslant 2(|r_h|-|\hat r_h|)/h\). Combining this with \eqref{Tq3} proves \eqref{Theq7}. Hence \eqref{Ca1} follows. {\bf Step II. Proof of \eqref{Ca2}.} By the definition of \(f\) given in \eqref{f}, we have $\rho'(u) = -2\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(u+1)/(\alpha_{1, \Gamma}\varphi(u))$. Therefore, \(\varphi(u)\rho'(u)=-2\alpha_{2,\Gamma} \Phi(u+1)/\alpha_{1,\Gamma}\). Since \(\Phi\) is increasing, \begin{align*} \frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}{2}\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h},|r_h|)}(\varphi(u)\rho'(u)) = -\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(|r_h|+1-\sqrt{h})\leqslant-\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(|r_h|), \end{align*} where we use the fact that $\Phi(\cdot)$ is increasing. Using $f(|r_h|)\leqslant \Phi(|r_h|)$ as shown in (\ref{f1}), we obtain $$\frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}{2}\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi(u)\rho'(u))\leqslant -\alpha_{2, \Gamma}f(|r_h|).$$ Multiplying by \(h\) gives \eqref{Ca2}. Combining \eqref{Ca1} and \eqref{Ca2}, we conclude that \(\mathbb E f(|\hat R_h|) \leqslant (1-\alpha_{2,\Gamma}h)f(|r_h|)\). Finally, by \eqref{dd6}, $\alpha_{2, \Gamma}^{-1}\geqslant 2r_1\Phi(1)/\alpha_{1, \Gamma}$. Moreover, since $M\geqslant \sqrt{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}/\sqrt{32r_1\Phi(1)}$, we have \[(4M)^{-2}\leqslant \frac{2r_1\Phi(1)}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} \leqslant \alpha_{2, \Gamma}^{-1}.\] Thus, for \(h\leqslant (4M)^{-2}\), $1-\alpha_{2, \Gamma}h>0$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Taylor expansion with Lemma 4.11; the curvature of $\varphi$ compensates the drift loss (Ca1) and the weight $\rho$ gives the contraction (Ca2).

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 4.11
nodes.statement: By the definition of $\bar h$, we have $h \in (0, (4Mr_1)^{2/(2\bar{\theta}-1)}]$. Since $\bar\theta\in(0,1/2)$, this implies $r_1\leqslant h^{\bar{\theta}-1/2}/(4M)$. Hence, for every $|r_h|\in(\sqrt h,r_1]$, \(|r_h|\in[\sqrt h,h^{\bar\theta-1/2}/(4M)]\). Together with $|\hat{r}_h|\in(\sqrt h,2R]$, Lemma \ref{2mom} gives \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}\left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\geqslant \alpha_{1, \Gamma}h. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The step-size restriction puts $|r_h|$ in the range of Lemma 4.11.

nodes.name: Equation (83)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\geqslant \alpha_{1, \Gamma}h.
nodes.label: Theq1

nodes.name: Taylor bound
nodes.statement: Since $f''< 0$ on $(0, r_1)$, by \eqref{cc4} and Lemma \ref{1mom}, we have \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\\ \leqslant &f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|)+\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[(|\hat{R}_h|-|r_h|)^2\1_{(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(|\hat{R}_h|)\right]\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}f''(u). \end{align*} We therefore obtain from (\ref{Theq1}) that \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|) + \frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}{2}\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}f''(u). \end{equation*} Since $f'(u) = \varphi(u)\rho(u)$ on $u\in (0, r_1]$, we have $$\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}f''(u)\leqslant \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi'(u)\rho(u))+\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi(u)\rho'(u)).$$ Therefore, \begin{align*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant& f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|) + \frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}{2} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi'(u)\rho(u))\\ &+\frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}{2}\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi(u)\rho'(u)). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Taylor expansion with the first-moment identity and Lemma 4.11.

nodes.name: Reduce to two inequalities
nodes.statement: It remains to prove \begin{equation} f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|)+\frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}{2} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi'(u)\rho(u))\leqslant 0 \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}h}{2}\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi(u)\rho'(u))\leqslant -\alpha_{2, \Gamma}h f(|r_h|). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to (Ca1) and (Ca2).

nodes.name: Equation (84)
nodes.statement: f'(|r_h|)(|\hat{r}_h|-|r_h|)+\frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}{2} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi'(u)\rho(u))\leqslant 0
nodes.label: Ca1

nodes.name: Equation (85)
nodes.statement: \frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}h}{2}\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi(u)\rho'(u))\leqslant -\alpha_{2, \Gamma}h f(|r_h|).
nodes.label: Ca2

nodes.name: Step I: proof of (Ca1)
nodes.statement: {\bf Step I. Proof of \eqref{Ca1}.} Since $\rho$ is decreasing and positive, while $\varphi'<0$, we have \begin{align*} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi'(u)\rho(u)) \leqslant \rho(|r_h|)\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u), \end{align*} Since $f'=\varphi\rho$, it is enough to show that \begin{equation} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u)\leqslant \frac{2(|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|)}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}\varphi(|r_h|). \end{equation} If $|r_h|\in(R, r_1]$, then by \eqref{Sub4eq1}, $|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\geqslant (hK/2)|r_h|>0$. Since $\varphi'\leqslant 0$, \eqref{Theq7} follows immediately. It remains to consider the case $|r_h|\in(\sqrt h,R]$. By \eqref{varphi}, \(\varphi'(u) = -(2L+1)(u+1)\varphi(u)/\alpha_{1,\Gamma}\). Hence \begin{equation} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u) =-\frac{2L+1}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\inf_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\left((u+1) \varphi(u)\right). \end{equation} Since $\varphi$ is decreasing and $h\leqslant 1$, we have \begin{equation} \inf_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\left((u+1) \varphi(u)\right)\geqslant(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}+1)\varphi(|r_h|)\geqslant |r_h|\varphi(|r_h|). \end{equation} Substituting (\ref{Tq2}) into (\ref{Theq3}) yields \begin{equation} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u)\leqslant -\frac{(2L+1)|r_h|}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\varphi(|r_h|). \end{equation} We now estimate $|r_h|-|\hat r_h|$. By (\ref{ss}), and using the fact that \(h\leqslant M^{1/(2\bar\theta-1)}\) so that \(Mh^{1-2\bar{\theta}}\leqslant 1\), we get \begin{equation*} \frac{|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|}{h}\geqslant \frac{|r_h|}{h}\left(1-\sqrt{1+2hL+Mh^{2-2\bar{\theta}}}\right)\geqslant \frac{1-\sqrt{1+(2L+1)h}}{h}|r_h|. \end{equation*} One observes that function $x\mapsto (\sqrt{1+(2L+1) x}-1)/x$ is decreasing on $(0, +\infty)$. This implies that for any $x>0$, \begin{align*} 0\leqslant \frac{\sqrt{1+(2L+1)x}-1}{x}\leqslant \frac{2L+1}{2}. \end{align*} Consequently, \((1-\sqrt{1+(2L+1)h})/h \geqslant -(2L+1)/2\). Thus, \(-(2L+1)|r_h|\leqslant 2(|r_h|-|\hat r_h|)/h\). Combining this with \eqref{Tq3} proves \eqref{Theq7}. Hence \eqref{Ca1} follows.
nodes.statement_short: The drift loss is compensated by the curvature of $\varphi$.

nodes.name: Reduce (Ca1) to (Theq7)
nodes.statement: {\bf Step I. Proof of \eqref{Ca1}.} Since $\rho$ is decreasing and positive, while $\varphi'<0$, we have \begin{align*} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi'(u)\rho(u)) \leqslant \rho(|r_h|)\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u), \end{align*} Since $f'=\varphi\rho$, it is enough to show that \begin{equation} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u)\leqslant \frac{2(|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|)}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}\varphi(|r_h|). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of $\rho$ reduces (Ca1) to (Theq7).

nodes.name: Equation (86)
nodes.statement: \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u)\leqslant \frac{2(|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|)}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma} h}\varphi(|r_h|).
nodes.label: Theq7

nodes.name: Case |r_h| > R
nodes.statement: If $|r_h|\in(R, r_1]$, then by \eqref{Sub4eq1}, $|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|\geqslant (hK/2)|r_h|>0$. Since $\varphi'\leqslant 0$, \eqref{Theq7} follows immediately. It remains to consider the case $|r_h|\in(\sqrt h,R]$.
nodes.statement_short: Here $|r_h|-|\hat r_h|>0$ and (Theq7) is immediate.

nodes.name: Bound varphi'
nodes.statement: By \eqref{varphi}, \(\varphi'(u) = -(2L+1)(u+1)\varphi(u)/\alpha_{1,\Gamma}\). Hence \begin{equation} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u) =-\frac{2L+1}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\inf_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\left((u+1) \varphi(u)\right). \end{equation} Since $\varphi$ is decreasing and $h\leqslant 1$, we have \begin{equation} \inf_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\left((u+1) \varphi(u)\right)\geqslant(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}+1)\varphi(|r_h|)\geqslant |r_h|\varphi(|r_h|). \end{equation} Substituting (\ref{Tq2}) into (\ref{Theq3}) yields \begin{equation} \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u)\leqslant -\frac{(2L+1)|r_h|}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\varphi(|r_h|). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\varphi'$ and bound its supremum.

nodes.name: Equation (87)
nodes.statement: \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u) =-\frac{2L+1}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\inf_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\left((u+1) \varphi(u)\right).
nodes.label: Theq3

nodes.name: Equation (88)
nodes.statement: \inf_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\left((u+1) \varphi(u)\right)\geqslant(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}+1)\varphi(|r_h|)\geqslant |r_h|\varphi(|r_h|).
nodes.label: Tq2

nodes.name: Equation (89)
nodes.statement: \sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}\varphi'(u)\leqslant -\frac{(2L+1)|r_h|}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}\varphi(|r_h|).
nodes.label: Tq3

nodes.name: Bound the drift loss
nodes.statement: We now estimate $|r_h|-|\hat r_h|$. By (\ref{ss}), and using the fact that \(h\leqslant M^{1/(2\bar\theta-1)}\) so that \(Mh^{1-2\bar{\theta}}\leqslant 1\), we get \begin{equation*} \frac{|r_h|-|\hat{r}_h|}{h}\geqslant \frac{|r_h|}{h}\left(1-\sqrt{1+2hL+Mh^{2-2\bar{\theta}}}\right)\geqslant \frac{1-\sqrt{1+(2L+1)h}}{h}|r_h|. \end{equation*} One observes that function $x\mapsto (\sqrt{1+(2L+1) x}-1)/x$ is decreasing on $(0, +\infty)$. This implies that for any $x>0$, \begin{align*} 0\leqslant \frac{\sqrt{1+(2L+1)x}-1}{x}\leqslant \frac{2L+1}{2}. \end{align*} Consequently, \((1-\sqrt{1+(2L+1)h})/h \geqslant -(2L+1)/2\). Thus, \(-(2L+1)|r_h|\leqslant 2(|r_h|-|\hat r_h|)/h\). Combining this with \eqref{Tq3} proves \eqref{Theq7}. Hence \eqref{Ca1} follows.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $|r_h|-|\hat r_h|$ from below and conclude (Ca1).

nodes.name: Step II: proof of (Ca2)
nodes.statement: {\bf Step II. Proof of \eqref{Ca2}.} By the definition of \(f\) given in \eqref{f}, we have $\rho'(u) = -2\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(u+1)/(\alpha_{1, \Gamma}\varphi(u))$. Therefore, \(\varphi(u)\rho'(u)=-2\alpha_{2,\Gamma} \Phi(u+1)/\alpha_{1,\Gamma}\). Since \(\Phi\) is increasing, \begin{align*} \frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}{2}\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h},|r_h|)}(\varphi(u)\rho'(u)) = -\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(|r_h|+1-\sqrt{h})\leqslant-\alpha_{2, \Gamma}\Phi(|r_h|), \end{align*} where we use the fact that $\Phi(\cdot)$ is increasing. Using $f(|r_h|)\leqslant \Phi(|r_h|)$ as shown in (\ref{f1}), we obtain $$\frac{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}{2}\sup_{u\in(|r_h|-\sqrt{h}, |r_h|)}(\varphi(u)\rho'(u))\leqslant -\alpha_{2, \Gamma}f(|r_h|).$$ Multiplying by \(h\) gives \eqref{Ca2}.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\varphi\rho'=-2\alpha_{2,\Gamma}\Phi(u+1)/\alpha_{1,\Gamma}$ and use $f\le\Phi$.

nodes.name: Combine and check positivity
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{Ca1} and \eqref{Ca2}, we conclude that \(\mathbb E f(|\hat R_h|) \leqslant (1-\alpha_{2,\Gamma}h)f(|r_h|)\). Finally, by \eqref{dd6}, $\alpha_{2, \Gamma}^{-1}\geqslant 2r_1\Phi(1)/\alpha_{1, \Gamma}$. Moreover, since $M\geqslant \sqrt{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}}/\sqrt{32r_1\Phi(1)}$, we have \[(4M)^{-2}\leqslant \frac{2r_1\Phi(1)}{\alpha_{1, \Gamma}} \leqslant \alpha_{2, \Gamma}^{-1}.\] Thus, for \(h\leqslant (4M)^{-2}\), $1-\alpha_{2, \Gamma}h>0$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Combine both inequalities and check $1-\alpha_{2,\Gamma}h>0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Contractivity for large distances (Case 3), reduction
nodes.statement: For \underline{\bf{Case 3. \textit{$|r_h|\in(r_1, +\infty)$}}}, we note that $|\hat{r}_h|\leqslant (1-hK/2)|r_h|<|r_h|$. Thus, by \eqref{cc4} and Lemma \ref{1mom}, we have $\mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|\hat{r}_h|)\leqslant 0$. Hence we only consider $f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)$. Since we do not know whether $|r_h|(1-hK/2)$ is larger or smaller than $r_1$, we use a case-by-case discussion for establishing Theorem \ref{Th1}.
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality removes the noise contribution, reducing Case 3 to the deterministic drift contraction $f(|\hat r_h|)-f(|r_h|)$.

nodes.name: Noise term non-positive
nodes.statement: For \underline{\bf{Case 3. \textit{$|r_h|\in(r_1, +\infty)$}}}, we note that $|\hat{r}_h|\leqslant (1-hK/2)|r_h|<|r_h|$. Thus, by \eqref{cc4} and Lemma \ref{1mom}, we have $\mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|\hat{r}_h|)\leqslant 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.6 and concavity give $\mathbb E f(|\hat R_h|)\le f(|\hat r_h|)$.

nodes.name: Reduce to the drift term
nodes.statement: Hence we only consider $f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)$. Since we do not know whether $|r_h|(1-hK/2)$ is larger or smaller than $r_1$, we use a case-by-case discussion for establishing Theorem \ref{Th1}.
nodes.statement_short: Only the drift term remains, treated case by case.

nodes.name: Contractivity for large distances (Case 3)
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{A} and \ref{A2} hold. For any $x, y\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $h\in(0, 2/K]$, consider the coupling $(\hat{X}_h(x,Z), \hat{Y}_h(x,y,Z))$ defined by (\ref{hY}). If $|r_h|\in(r_1, +\infty)$, then \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)\leqslant (1-K\varphi(r_1)h/8)f(|r_h|), \end{equation*} where $|r_h|, |\hat{r}_h|, |\hat{R}_h|$ are defined in (\ref{eq3}), functions $f$ and $\varphi$ are defined by (\ref{f}) and (\ref{varphi}) respectively.
nodes.statement_short: For $|r_h|>r_1$ the coupling contracts $f$ at rate $K\varphi(r_1)/8$.
nodes.label: PR5

nodes.name: Proof of Contractivity for large distances (Case 3)
nodes.statement: If $|r_h|(1-hK/2)>r_1$, since $f$ is increasing, using the fact $\rho(u)\geqslant 1/2$ for $u\in(0,r_1)$, we have \begin{align*} f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)&\leqslant f\left(|r_h|\left(1-hK/2\right)\right)-f(|r_h|)\\ &\leqslant -\frac{1}{2}\int_{|r_h|(1-hK/2)}^{|r_h|}\varphi(s\wedge r_1)\mathrm{d} s= -\frac{hK}{4}\varphi(r_1)|r_h|. \end{align*} Therefore, by the fact $f(|r_h|)\leqslant |r_h|$ given in (\ref{f1}), we obtain the desired result. It remains to consider the case \(|r_h|(1-hK/2)\leqslant r_1\). Set the intermediate point \(|r_h|(1-hK/4)\). We distinguish two subcases. If $|r_h|(1-hK/4)< r_1$, then using the fact that $\varphi$ is decreasing and $\rho(r)\geqslant 1/2$ for $r\in(0,r_1)$, we have \begin{align*} f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)&\leqslant f\left(|r_h|\left(1-\frac{hK}{2}\right)\right)-f\left(|r_h|\left(1-\frac{hK}{4}\right)\right)\\ &\leqslant -\frac{1}{2}\int_{|r_h|(1-\frac{hK}{2})}^{|r_h|(1-hK/4)}\varphi(s\wedge r_1)\mathrm{d} s\leqslant -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}h|r_h|\leqslant -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}hf(|r_h|). \end{align*} If $|r_h|(1-hk/4)\geqslant r_1$, then \begin{align*} f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)&\leqslant f\left(|r_h|\left(1-\frac{hK}{4}\right)\right)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant -\frac{1}{2}\int_{|r_h|(1-hK/4)}^{|r_h|}\varphi(s\wedge r_1)\mathrm{d} s\\ &= -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}h|r_h|\leqslant -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}hf(|r_h|). \end{align*} Hence, combining all estimates, we obtain \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}hf(|r_h|) \end{equation*} for $|r_h|\in(r_1, +\infty)$. Finally, since $0<\varphi(r_1)<1$ and $h\leqslant 2/K$, we have $K\varphi(r_1)h/ 8 \leqslant\varphi(r_1)/4<1$. Then, $1-K\varphi(r_1)h/8>0$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Drift contraction alone suffices; integrate $f'$ over the removed interval, case by case relative to $r_1$.

nodes.name: Case: contracted distance beyond r_1
nodes.statement: If $|r_h|(1-hK/2)>r_1$, since $f$ is increasing, using the fact $\rho(u)\geqslant 1/2$ for $u\in(0,r_1)$, we have \begin{align*} f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)&\leqslant f\left(|r_h|\left(1-hK/2\right)\right)-f(|r_h|)\\ &\leqslant -\frac{1}{2}\int_{|r_h|(1-hK/2)}^{|r_h|}\varphi(s\wedge r_1)\mathrm{d} s= -\frac{hK}{4}\varphi(r_1)|r_h|. \end{align*} Therefore, by the fact $f(|r_h|)\leqslant |r_h|$ given in (\ref{f1}), we obtain the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate $f'$ over the interval removed by the drift contraction.

nodes.name: Case: contracted distance within r_1
nodes.statement: It remains to consider the case \(|r_h|(1-hK/2)\leqslant r_1\). Set the intermediate point \(|r_h|(1-hK/4)\). We distinguish two subcases. If $|r_h|(1-hK/4)< r_1$, then using the fact that $\varphi$ is decreasing and $\rho(r)\geqslant 1/2$ for $r\in(0,r_1)$, we have \begin{align*} f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)&\leqslant f\left(|r_h|\left(1-\frac{hK}{2}\right)\right)-f\left(|r_h|\left(1-\frac{hK}{4}\right)\right)\\ &\leqslant -\frac{1}{2}\int_{|r_h|(1-\frac{hK}{2})}^{|r_h|(1-hK/4)}\varphi(s\wedge r_1)\mathrm{d} s\leqslant -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}h|r_h|\leqslant -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}hf(|r_h|). \end{align*} If $|r_h|(1-hk/4)\geqslant r_1$, then \begin{align*} f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)&\leqslant f\left(|r_h|\left(1-\frac{hK}{4}\right)\right)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant -\frac{1}{2}\int_{|r_h|(1-hK/4)}^{|r_h|}\varphi(s\wedge r_1)\mathrm{d} s\\ &= -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}h|r_h|\leqslant -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}hf(|r_h|). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use the intermediate point $|r_h|(1-hK/4)$ and split into two subcases.

nodes.name: Intermediate point
nodes.statement: It remains to consider the case \(|r_h|(1-hK/2)\leqslant r_1\). Set the intermediate point \(|r_h|(1-hK/4)\). We distinguish two subcases.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the intermediate point $|r_h|(1-hK/4)$.

nodes.name: Subcase below r_1
nodes.statement: If $|r_h|(1-hK/4)< r_1$, then using the fact that $\varphi$ is decreasing and $\rho(r)\geqslant 1/2$ for $r\in(0,r_1)$, we have \begin{align*} f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)&\leqslant f\left(|r_h|\left(1-\frac{hK}{2}\right)\right)-f\left(|r_h|\left(1-\frac{hK}{4}\right)\right)\\ &\leqslant -\frac{1}{2}\int_{|r_h|(1-\frac{hK}{2})}^{|r_h|(1-hK/4)}\varphi(s\wedge r_1)\mathrm{d} s\leqslant -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}h|r_h|\leqslant -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}hf(|r_h|). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate over $[|r_h|(1-hK/2),|r_h|(1-hK/4)]$.

nodes.name: Subcase above r_1
nodes.statement: If $|r_h|(1-hk/4)\geqslant r_1$, then \begin{align*} f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)&\leqslant f\left(|r_h|\left(1-\frac{hK}{4}\right)\right)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant -\frac{1}{2}\int_{|r_h|(1-hK/4)}^{|r_h|}\varphi(s\wedge r_1)\mathrm{d} s\\ &= -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}h|r_h|\leqslant -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}hf(|r_h|). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate over $[|r_h|(1-hK/4),|r_h|]$.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Hence, combining all estimates, we obtain \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E} f(|\hat{R}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant f(|\hat{r}_h|)-f(|r_h|)\leqslant -\frac{K\varphi(r_1)}{8}hf(|r_h|) \end{equation*} for $|r_h|\in(r_1, +\infty)$. Finally, since $0<\varphi(r_1)<1$ and $h\leqslant 2/K$, we have $K\varphi(r_1)h/ 8 \leqslant\varphi(r_1)/4<1$. Then, $1-K\varphi(r_1)h/8>0$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the cases and check positivity of the rate factor.

nodes.name: Proof of Global one-step contractivity of the coupling
nodes.statement: Combining Propositions \ref{PR1}, \ref{PR4} and \ref{PR5}, we establish the contractivity of coupling $(\hat{X}_h(x,Z),$ $ \hat{Y}_h(x, y,Z))$, as formalized in Theorem \ref{Th1}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the three distance regimes (Propositions 1, 2 and 5) to obtain the global contraction.

nodes.name: Random initial values xi_1, xi_2
nodes.statement: More precisely, let \(\xi_1\) and \(\xi_2\) be \(\mathbb R^d\)-valued random variables which are independent of \((Z,\zeta)\), where \(Z\sim N(\mathbf 0,h\mathbf I_q)\) and \(\zeta\sim {\rm Unif}[0,1]\). The random variables \(\xi_1\) and \(\xi_2\) need not be independent of each other.

nodes.name: Drift-updated random points
nodes.statement: Define \[ u_h(\xi_i):=\pi_h(\xi_i)+h b(\pi_h(\xi_i)), \qquad i=1,2, \] and \(\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2):=u_h(\xi_1)-u_h(\xi_2)\).

nodes.name: One-step TEM map from a random point
nodes.statement: Define \(\hat X_h(\xi_1,Z):=u_h(\xi_1)+\Sigma Z\).

nodes.name: Coupling with random initial values
nodes.statement: If \(\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)=\mathbf 0\), set \(\hat Y_h(\xi_1,\xi_2,Z):=u_h(\xi_2)+\Sigma Z\). If \(\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)\neq\mathbf 0\), define \begin{equation} \hat Y_h(\xi_1,\xi_2,Z) := \begin{cases} u_h(\xi_1)+\Sigma Z, & \zeta\leqslant v_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m(\Sigma Z),\ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m,\\ &~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\text{and}~|\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)|\leqslant 2R,\\[1mm] u_h(\xi_2)+\mathcal R_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^\Gamma \Sigma Z, & \zeta> v_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m(\Sigma Z),\ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m,\\ &~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\text{and}~|\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)|\leqslant 2R,\\[1mm] u_h(\xi_2)+\Sigma Z, & \Sigma Z\notin A_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m ~\text{or}~ |\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)|>2R . \end{cases} \end{equation} Here \(v_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m\) and \(A_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m\) are defined exactly as in the deterministic case, with \(x\) and \(y\) replaced by \(\xi_1\) and \(\xi_2\), respectively.
nodes.statement_short: The one-step reflection-synchronous coupling applied to random starting points independent of the noise.

nodes.name: Coupling with random initial values
nodes.statement: \hat Y_h(\xi_1,\xi_2,Z) := \begin{cases} u_h(\xi_1)+\Sigma Z, & \zeta\leqslant v_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m(\Sigma Z),\ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m,\\ &~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\text{and}~|\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)|\leqslant 2R,\\[1mm] u_h(\xi_2)+\mathcal R_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^\Gamma \Sigma Z, & \zeta> v_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m(\Sigma Z),\ \Sigma Z\in A_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m,\\ &~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\text{and}~|\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)|\leqslant 2R,\\[1mm] u_h(\xi_2)+\Sigma Z, & \Sigma Z\notin A_{\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)}^m ~\text{or}~ |\hat r_h(\xi_1,\xi_2)|>2R . \end{cases}
nodes.label: XY0

nodes.name: Coupling property with random initial values
nodes.statement: For fixed \(h>0\), let \(\xi_1\) and \(\xi_2\) be \(\mathbb R^d\)-valued random variables independent of \((Z,\zeta)\). Then the $2d$-dimensional random vector $(\hat{X}_h(\xi_1,Z), \hat{Y}_h(\xi_1, \xi_2,Z))$ defined by (\ref{XY0}) is a coupling of the laws of \(\hat X_h(\xi_1,Z)\) and \(\hat X_h(\xi_2,Z)\).
assumptions: let \(\xi_1\) and \(\xi_2\) be \(\mathbb R^d\)-valued random variables independent of \((Z,\zeta)\).
conclusions: the $2d$-dimensional random vector $(\hat{X}_h(\xi_1,Z), \hat{Y}_h(\xi_1, \xi_2,Z))$ defined by (\ref{XY0}) is a coupling of the laws of \(\hat X_h(\xi_1,Z)\) and \(\hat X_h(\xi_2,Z)\).
nodes.label: rvcoup

nodes.name: Proof of Coupling property with random initial values
nodes.statement: The first marginal is clear from the definition of \(\hat X_h(\xi_1,Z)\). It remains to identify the second marginal. Let \(g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be bounded and continuous, and denote \(\mathcal G:=\Sigma(\xi_1,\xi_2)\). Since \((\xi_1,\xi_2)\) is independent of \((Z,\zeta)\), conditioning on \(\mathcal G\) freezes the values of \(\xi_1\) and \(\xi_2\). Hence, by \cite[Theorem 2.24]{FC} and Lemma \ref{coup}, \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\left[ g\bigl(\hat Y_h(\xi_1,\xi_2,Z)\bigr) \right] &= \mathbb E\left[ \mathbb E\left[ g\bigl(\hat Y_h(\xi_1,\xi_2,Z)\bigr) \mid \mathcal G \right] \right]= \mathbb E\left[ \left. \mathbb E\left[ g\bigl(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z)\bigr) \right] \right|_{x=\xi_1,\ y=\xi_2} \right] \\ &= \mathbb E\left[ \left. \mathbb E\left[ g\bigl(u_h(y)+\Sigma Z\bigr) \right] \right|_{y=\xi_2} \right]= \mathbb E\left[ g\bigl(\hat X_h(\xi_2,Z)\bigr) \right]. \end{aligned} \] Therefore, \(\mathcal L\bigl(\hat Y_h(\xi_1,\xi_2,Z)\bigr) =\mathcal L\bigl(\hat X_h(\xi_2,Z)\bigr)\). Thus \(\bigl(\hat X_h(\xi_1,Z),\hat Y_h(\xi_1,\xi_2,Z)\bigr)\) is indeed a coupling of the laws of \(\hat X_h(\xi_1,Z)\) and \(\hat X_h(\xi_2,Z)\). The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Condition on the initial values and apply the deterministic coupling lemma.

nodes.name: Reduce to the second marginal
nodes.statement: The first marginal is clear from the definition of \(\hat X_h(\xi_1,Z)\). It remains to identify the second marginal. Let \(g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be bounded and continuous, and denote \(\mathcal G:=\Sigma(\xi_1,\xi_2)\).
nodes.statement_short: Only the second marginal needs identification.

nodes.name: Condition on the initial values
nodes.statement: Since \((\xi_1,\xi_2)\) is independent of \((Z,\zeta)\), conditioning on \(\mathcal G\) freezes the values of \(\xi_1\) and \(\xi_2\). Hence, by \cite[Theorem 2.24]{FC} and Lemma \ref{coup}, \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbb E\left[ g\bigl(\hat Y_h(\xi_1,\xi_2,Z)\bigr) \right] &= \mathbb E\left[ \mathbb E\left[ g\bigl(\hat Y_h(\xi_1,\xi_2,Z)\bigr) \mid \mathcal G \right] \right]= \mathbb E\left[ \left. \mathbb E\left[ g\bigl(\hat Y_h(x,y,Z)\bigr) \right] \right|_{x=\xi_1,\ y=\xi_2} \right] \\ &= \mathbb E\left[ \left. \mathbb E\left[ g\bigl(u_h(y)+\Sigma Z\bigr) \right] \right|_{y=\xi_2} \right]= \mathbb E\left[ g\bigl(\hat X_h(\xi_2,Z)\bigr) \right]. \end{aligned} \]
nodes.statement_short: Conditioning on $(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ reduces to the deterministic coupling lemma.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Therefore, \(\mathcal L\bigl(\hat Y_h(\xi_1,\xi_2,Z)\bigr) =\mathcal L\bigl(\hat X_h(\xi_2,Z)\bigr)\). Thus \(\bigl(\hat X_h(\xi_1,Z),\hat Y_h(\xi_1,\xi_2,Z)\bigr)\) is indeed a coupling of the laws of \(\hat X_h(\xi_1,Z)\) and \(\hat X_h(\xi_2,Z)\). The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: The laws coincide.

nodes.name: Contractivity for the coupling with random initial values
nodes.statement: Similarly, the conclusion of Theorem \ref{Th1} remains valid for the coupling defined by \eqref{XY0}.
conclusions: the conclusion of Theorem \ref{Th1} remains valid for the coupling defined by \eqref{XY0}

nodes.name: Uniform-in-time strong convergence of the TEM scheme
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{A1} and \ref{A2} hold. For any \(h\in(0,\bar h]\), we have \[\sup_{k\geqslant 0} \mathbb E\left|X_k-x_{t_k}\right| \leqslant C h^{1/2},\] where \(\bar h\) is defined in \eqref{bar}, and \(C\) is a positive constant independent of \(h\) and \(k\).
nodes.statement_short: The TEM scheme has strong error $O(h^{1/2})$ uniformly over all times.
nodes.label: Th2

nodes.name: Proof of Uniform-in-time strong convergence of the TEM scheme
nodes.statement: We construct a process \((\hat G_k)_{k\geqslant 0}\) coupled with \((\hat S_k)_{k\geqslant 1}\) according to the coupling mechanism \eqref{XY0}. By Corollary \ref{rvcoup}, if \(\hat G_0=\hat X_0\), then \(\mathcal L(\hat G_k)=\mathcal L(\hat X_k)\) for all \(k\geqslant 0\). Moreover, the processes \((\hat G_k)_{k\geq 0}\) and \((\hat S_k)_{k\geq 1}\) inherit the moment estimates stated in Lemma \ref{Le2}. By \eqref{f1}, Corollary \ref{co2} with \(s\geqslant 1\vee(3\ell/(2\theta))\), and Lemma \ref{Le5}, we obtain, for any \(k\geqslant 0\), \begin{equation} \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_{k+1})-x_{t_{k+1}}\right| \right) \leqslant C h^{3/2} + \mathbb E f\left( \left|\hat G_{k+1}-\hat S_{k+1}\right| \right). \end{equation} Using Theorem \ref{Th1}, Corollary \ref{rvcoup}, and Corollary \ref{co2}, we have, for any \(k\geqslant 0\), \[\begin{aligned} \mathbb E f\left( \left|\hat G_{k+1}-\hat S_{k+1}\right| \right) &\leqslant (1-ch) \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_k)-\pi_h(x_{t_k})\right| \right) \\ &\leqslant (1-ch) \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_k)-x_{t_k}\right| \right)+(1-ch) \mathbb E f\left( \left|x_{t_k}-\pi_h(x_{t_k})\right| \right) \\ &\leqslant(1-ch) \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_k)-x_{t_k}\right| \right) +C h^{3/2}. \end{aligned}\] Here we used the subadditivity of \(f\), which follows from the fact that \(f\) is increasing, concave, and \(f(0)=0\). Substituting the above estimate into \eqref{35} gives \[\mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_{k+1})-x_{t_{k+1}}\right| \right)\leqslant (1-ch) \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_k)-x_{t_k}\right| \right) +C h^{3/2}.\] Iterating this inequality yields \[\mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_{k+1})-x_{t_{k+1}}\right| \right) \leqslant (1-ch)^{k+1} f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_0)-\pi_h(x_0)\right| \right)+ C h^{3/2} \sum_{j=0}^{k}(1-ch)^j .\] Since the two processes start from the same initial value, the first term vanishes. Therefore, \[\sup_{k\geqslant 0} \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_k)-x_{t_k}\right| \right) \leqslant C h^{1/2}.\] Finally, by \eqref{f1}, using \(X_k=\pi_h(\hat X_k)\) and \(\mathcal L(\hat X_k)=\mathcal L(\hat G_k)\), we obtain $$\mathbb{E}\left|X_{k}-x_{t_{k}}\right|\leqslant \frac{2}{\varphi(r_1)}\mathbb{E} f\left(\left|X_{k}-x_{t_{k}}\right|\right)= \frac{2}{\varphi(r_1)}\mathbb{E} f(|\pi_h(\hat{G}_{k})-x_{t_{k}}|)\leqslant Ch^{1/2}.$$ Taking the supremum over \(k\geqslant 0\) gives the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Couple the scheme step by step with the one-step process, use the contraction of Theorem 4.8 and the $O(h^{3/2})$ local error, and iterate. The key step is the contractive recursion with geometric summation.

nodes.name: Coupled copy of the scheme
nodes.statement: We construct a process \((\hat G_k)_{k\geqslant 0}\) coupled with \((\hat S_k)_{k\geqslant 1}\) according to the coupling mechanism \eqref{XY0}. By Corollary \ref{rvcoup}, if \(\hat G_0=\hat X_0\), then \(\mathcal L(\hat G_k)=\mathcal L(\hat X_k)\) for all \(k\geqslant 0\). Moreover, the processes \((\hat G_k)_{k\geq 0}\) and \((\hat S_k)_{k\geq 1}\) inherit the moment estimates stated in Lemma \ref{Le2}.
nodes.statement_short: Build $\hat G_k$ coupled step by step with $\hat S_k$ and having the law of $\hat X_k$.

nodes.name: Error split via truncation and consistency
nodes.statement: By \eqref{f1}, Corollary \ref{co2} with \(s\geqslant 1\vee(3\ell/(2\theta))\), and Lemma \ref{Le5}, we obtain, for any \(k\geqslant 0\), \begin{equation} \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_{k+1})-x_{t_{k+1}}\right| \right) \leqslant C h^{3/2} + \mathbb E f\left( \left|\hat G_{k+1}-\hat S_{k+1}\right| \right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the $f$-error by local consistency plus the coupled distance.

nodes.name: Equation (91)
nodes.statement: \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_{k+1})-x_{t_{k+1}}\right| \right) \leqslant C h^{3/2} + \mathbb E f\left( \left|\hat G_{k+1}-\hat S_{k+1}\right| \right).

nodes.name: One-step contraction
nodes.statement: Using Theorem \ref{Th1}, Corollary \ref{rvcoup}, and Corollary \ref{co2}, we have, for any \(k\geqslant 0\), \[\begin{aligned} \mathbb E f\left( \left|\hat G_{k+1}-\hat S_{k+1}\right| \right) &\leqslant (1-ch) \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_k)-\pi_h(x_{t_k})\right| \right) \\ &\leqslant (1-ch) \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_k)-x_{t_k}\right| \right)+(1-ch) \mathbb E f\left( \left|x_{t_k}-\pi_h(x_{t_k})\right| \right) \\ &\leqslant(1-ch) \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_k)-x_{t_k}\right| \right) +C h^{3/2}. \end{aligned}\] Here we used the subadditivity of \(f\), which follows from the fact that \(f\) is increasing, concave, and \(f(0)=0\).
nodes.statement_short: Apply the coupling contraction and subadditivity of $f$.

nodes.name: Recursive inequality
nodes.statement: Substituting the above estimate into \eqref{35} gives \[\mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_{k+1})-x_{t_{k+1}}\right| \right)\leqslant (1-ch) \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_k)-x_{t_k}\right| \right) +C h^{3/2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Obtain a contractive recursion with $O(h^{3/2})$ forcing.

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement: Iterating this inequality yields \[\mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_{k+1})-x_{t_{k+1}}\right| \right) \leqslant (1-ch)^{k+1} f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_0)-\pi_h(x_0)\right| \right)+ C h^{3/2} \sum_{j=0}^{k}(1-ch)^j .\] Since the two processes start from the same initial value, the first term vanishes. Therefore, \[\sup_{k\geqslant 0} \mathbb E f\left( \left|\pi_h(\hat G_k)-x_{t_k}\right| \right) \leqslant C h^{1/2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Sum the geometric series to get $O(h^{1/2})$ uniformly in $k$.

nodes.name: Return to the Euclidean error
nodes.statement: Finally, by \eqref{f1}, using \(X_k=\pi_h(\hat X_k)\) and \(\mathcal L(\hat X_k)=\mathcal L(\hat G_k)\), we obtain $$\mathbb{E}\left|X_{k}-x_{t_{k}}\right|\leqslant \frac{2}{\varphi(r_1)}\mathbb{E} f\left(\left|X_{k}-x_{t_{k}}\right|\right)= \frac{2}{\varphi(r_1)}\mathbb{E} f(|\pi_h(\hat{G}_{k})-x_{t_{k}}|)\leqslant Ch^{1/2}.$$ Taking the supremum over \(k\geqslant 0\) gives the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Use $f(u)\ge\varphi(r_1)u/2$ to bound $\mathbb E|X_k-x_{t_k}|$.

nodes.name: Convergence of the numerical invariant measure
nodes.statement: Let Assumptions \ref{A1} and \ref{A2} hold. Then, for any initial value \(x_0\in\mathbb R^d\) and any \(h\in(0,\bar h]\), we have \[ \mathcal W_1(\mu_h,\mu) \leqslant C h^{1/2}, \] where \(\bar h\) is defined in \eqref{bar}, and \(C\) is a positive constant independent of \(h\).
nodes.statement_short: The TEM invariant measure $\mu_h$ is within $O(h^{1/2})$ of the true invariant measure in $\mathcal W_1$.
assumptions: for any initial value \(x_0\in\mathbb R^d\) and any \(h\in(0,\bar h]\)
nodes.label: Th3

nodes.name: Proof of Convergence of the numerical invariant measure
nodes.statement: By the triangle inequality, for every \(k\geqslant 0\), \[\mathcal W_1(\mu_h,\mu) \leqslant \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mu_h,\mathcal L(X_k)\bigr) + \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mathcal L(X_k),\mathcal L(x_{t_k})\bigr)+ \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mathcal L(x_{t_k}),\mu\bigr).\] By Lemma \ref{LeX} and Theorem \ref{Co}, \[\lim_{k\to\infty} \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mu_h,\mathcal L(X_k)\bigr) =0,\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty} \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mathcal L(x_{t_k}),\mu\bigr) =0.\] Therefore, taking \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\) in the preceding inequality gives \[\mathcal W_1(\mu_h,\mu) \leqslant \limsup_{k\to\infty} \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mathcal L(X_k),\mathcal L(x_{t_k})\bigr).\] Using Theorem \ref{Th2}, we obtain \(\mathcal W_1\bigl(\mathcal L(X_k),\mathcal L(x_{t_k})\bigr) \leqslant\mathbb E\left|X_k-x_{t_k}\right| \leqslant C h^{1/2}\). Consequently, the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality plus exponential ergodicity of both dynamics and the uniform strong error bound.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement: By the triangle inequality, for every \(k\geqslant 0\), \[\mathcal W_1(\mu_h,\mu) \leqslant \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mu_h,\mathcal L(X_k)\bigr) + \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mathcal L(X_k),\mathcal L(x_{t_k})\bigr)+ \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mathcal L(x_{t_k}),\mu\bigr).\]
nodes.statement_short: Split $\mathcal W_1(\mu_h,\mu)$ through the laws of $X_k$ and $x_{t_k}$.

nodes.name: Ergodicity of both dynamics
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{LeX} and Theorem \ref{Co}, \[\lim_{k\to\infty} \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mu_h,\mathcal L(X_k)\bigr) =0,\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty} \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mathcal L(x_{t_k}),\mu\bigr) =0.\] Therefore, taking \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\) in the preceding inequality gives \[\mathcal W_1(\mu_h,\mu) \leqslant \limsup_{k\to\infty} \mathcal W_1\bigl(\mathcal L(X_k),\mathcal L(x_{t_k})\bigr).\]
nodes.statement_short: Exponential ergodicity of exact and numerical solutions kills the outer terms as $k\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Apply the strong error bound
nodes.statement: Using Theorem \ref{Th2}, we obtain \(\mathcal W_1\bigl(\mathcal L(X_k),\mathcal L(x_{t_k})\bigr) \leqslant\mathbb E\left|X_k-x_{t_k}\right| \leqslant C h^{1/2}\). Consequently, the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the middle term by the strong error.

nodes.name: Planar SDE with rough radial drift
nodes.statement: Consider the planar SDE \begin{equation} \mathrm{d} X_t = b(X_t)\mathrm{d} t+\Sigma\mathrm{d} B_t,\qquad X_0=(1,0.5)^{\mathrm T}, \end{equation} where $X_t=(x_t,y_t)^{\mathrm T}$, $B_t=(B_t^1,B_t^2)^{\mathrm T}$ is a standard two-dimensional Brownian motion, and \[b(z)=-z|z|+6z-2z\cos(|z|),\qquad z=(x,y)^{\mathrm T}\in\mathbb{R}^2.\] In the numerical experiment, we choose a correlated non-degenerate diffusion matrix \[ \Sigma= \begin{pmatrix} 1&0\\ 0.6&0.8 \end{pmatrix}. \] The eigenvalues of \(\Sigma\Sigma^{\mathrm T}\) are $1.6$ and $0.4$. Hence $\Sigma\Sigma^{\mathrm T}>0$.
nodes.statement_short: A 2D SDE with drift $-z|z|+6z-2z\cos|z|$ and correlated non-degenerate noise.
nodes.label: EX

nodes.name: Planar SDE of Example 1
nodes.statement: \mathrm{d} X_t = b(X_t)\mathrm{d} t+\Sigma\mathrm{d} B_t,\qquad X_0=(1,0.5)^{\mathrm T},
nodes.label: Ex

nodes.name: Verification of dissipativity at infinity for Example 1
nodes.statement: We first verify that the drift coefficient in Example \ref{EX} satisfies Assumption \ref{A1}. A direct computation shows that \[ \left\langle z_1-z_2,b(z_1)-b(z_2)\right\rangle \leqslant 8|z_1-z_2|^2,\qquad z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{R}^2. \] Moreover, the dominant term \(-z|z|\) yields dissipation at large distances. More precisely, for all \(z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{R}^2\) satisfying \(|z_1-z_2|>20\), one has \[ \left\langle z_1-z_2,b(z_1)-b(z_2)\right\rangle \leqslant -|z_1-z_2|^2 . \]
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation: one-sided Lipschitz bound 8 everywhere and dissipativity with constant 1 for separations above 20.

nodes.name: One-sided Lipschitz bound
nodes.statement: We first verify that the drift coefficient in Example \ref{EX} satisfies Assumption \ref{A1}. A direct computation shows that \[ \left\langle z_1-z_2,b(z_1)-b(z_2)\right\rangle \leqslant 8|z_1-z_2|^2,\qquad z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{R}^2. \]
nodes.statement_short: Compute the one-sided Lipschitz constant 8.

nodes.name: Dissipativity at large distances
nodes.statement: Moreover, the dominant term \(-z|z|\) yields dissipation at large distances. More precisely, for all \(z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{R}^2\) satisfying \(|z_1-z_2|>20\), one has \[ \left\langle z_1-z_2,b(z_1)-b(z_2)\right\rangle \leqslant -|z_1-z_2|^2 . \]
nodes.statement_short: The term $-z|z|$ gives dissipativity for separations above 20.

nodes.name: Example 1 satisfies Assumption 2
nodes.statement: Consequently, condition \eqref{CaI} holds with \(L=8\), \(K=1\) and \(R=20\). Thus Assumption \ref{A1} is satisfied.

nodes.name: Well-posedness and ergodicity of Example 1
nodes.statement: By Lemmas \ref{Ju} and \ref{LeX}, system \eqref{Ex} admits a unique global solution and a unique invariant probability measure.
conclusions: system \eqref{Ex} admits a unique global solution and a unique invariant probability measure

nodes.name: Numerical solution and its radius for Example 1
nodes.statement: Let \(X_k^h=(x_k^h,y_k^h)^{\mathrm T}\) denote the numerical solution at time $t_k=kh$, and set \[ r_k^h=|X_k^h| = \sqrt{(x_k^h)^2+(y_k^h)^2}. \]

nodes.name: TEM scheme for the planar rough-potential SDE
nodes.statement: For the truncation function, we choose \(\phi(u)=4u+8, u\geqslant 0\), so that \(\phi^{-1}(v)=(v-8)/4\). Taking \(M=16\) and \(\theta=1/4\), the truncation radius becomes \(4h^{-1/4}-2\). The TEM scheme for \eqref{Ex} is then written explicitly as \[\left\{\begin{aligned} \widehat x_{k+1}^h &= x_k^h+h(-r_k^h+6-2\cos r_k^h)x_k^h +\Delta B_{k+1}^{1},\\ \widehat y_{k+1}^h &= y_k^h+h(-r_k^h+6-2\cos r_k^h)y_k^h +0.6\Delta B_{k+1}^{1} +0.8\Delta B_{k+1}^{2},\\ x_{k+1}^h &= \left(1\wedge \frac{4h^{-1/4}-2}{\sqrt{(\widehat x_{k+1}^h)^2+(\widehat y_{k+1}^h)^2}}\right) \widehat x_{k+1}^h,\\ y_{k+1}^h &= \left(1\wedge \frac{4h^{-1/4}-2}{\sqrt{(\widehat x_{k+1}^h)^2+(\widehat y_{k+1}^h)^2}}\right) \widehat y_{k+1}^h. \end{aligned}\right.\] Here \(\Delta B_{k+1}^{i} = B_{t_{k+1}}^i-B_{t_k}^i\), \(i=1,2\), and $\Delta B_{k+1}^{1}$, $\Delta B_{k+1}^{2}$ are independent normal random variables distributed as $N(0,h)$. The multiplicative truncation factor is understood to be equal to one when \((\widehat x_{k+1}^h)^2+(\widehat y_{k+1}^h)^2=0\).
nodes.statement_short: Explicit TEM recursion for Example 1 with $\phi(u)=4u+8$, $M=16$, $\theta=1/4$.

nodes.name: Numerical evidence of ergodicity
nodes.statement: The curves approach a common limiting level as time increases, independently of the initial condition. This behaviour is consistent with the convergence-to-equilibrium statement in Theorem \ref{Pro1}.

nodes.name: Numerical strong convergence rate
nodes.statement: The error decreases as the step size becomes smaller. The observed slope is close to the first-order reference line; in particular, it is consistent with, and in this example appears sharper than, the rate guaranteed by Theorem \ref{Th2}.
nodes.statement_short: Observed terminal-time strong error decays at roughly first order, sharper than the guaranteed order 1/2.

nodes.name: Numerical stability of invariant-measure approximations
nodes.statement: The marginal densities corresponding to different step sizes almost overlap, while the joint density surfaces are also visually close to each other and become increasingly stable as \(h\) decreases. These observations indicate that the long-time distribution of the numerical solution is stable with respect to time discretisation, and provide numerical support for the convergence of numerical invariant measures asserted in Theorem \ref{Th3}.
nodes.statement_short: Empirical long-time densities for several step sizes nearly coincide, supporting convergence of numerical invariant measures.
